498a-misuse-claim-police-data.en:
"498A is the most misused law in India." The line turns up in comment sections, WhatsApp forwards and family arguments, often as soon as a woman complains of cruelty by her husband or in-laws. It is repeated so often that many people treat it as a statistic. It is not one. The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) does publish what happened to these cases in 2024, and its numbers point the other way [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The myth and why it spreads

Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, now Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty: wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause her grave injury, or harassment to force her or her family to meet unlawful demands for property. The maximum sentence is three years and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In 2024 police registered 1,20,227 such cases, more than any other crime against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The myth spreads because the fear behind it is real. A cruelty complaint can name a husband's parents and sisters, and a family that believes it has been wrongly accused feels every police visit and court date. Some complaints are false, and a false case does real harm to the people named in it. But "some" is not "most", and a forward is not data. The same "she is lying" reflex meets women who report rape, a myth we have checked separately against the record.

## Police files: 4,593 closed as false, 1,08,574 charge-sheeted

When police finish investigating, they either file a charge-sheet, which sends the accused for trial, or close the case with a final report. In 2024 police disposed of 1,20,390 cruelty cases. They closed 4,593 as "false", about 3.8%, and charge-sheeted 1,08,574, a charge-sheeting rate of 90.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Another 3,459 were closed as a "mistake of fact or law or civil dispute". Even adding those, fewer than 7 in 100 cases ended in either kind of closure.

Across all crimes against women, police charge-sheeted 77.2% of the cases they disposed of [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cruelty complaints did better than average: after investigating, police found enough to send nine in ten to court.

## What a 'false' closure actually means

"Final report false" is a police classification after investigation, not a court finding, and NCRB does not report why a case was classified that way.

How much depends on the police force? Across all crimes against women, Rajasthan alone produced 12,217 of India's 36,895 "false" closures in 2024, a third of the national total, and had the lowest charge-sheeting rate of any state or union territory, 54.1% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It is hard to believe that complainants in one state invent cases far more often than complainants everywhere else. More likely, "false" partly measures how a state's police close cases.

So 3.8% is not a count of proven lies. It is not proof that every other case is true, either. It is the police's own verdict after investigation, the closest thing there is to a national measure, and it does not support "most".

## Acquittal and compromise are not proof of a false case

The other numbers people quote come from the courts. In 2024, 9,27,199 cruelty cases were before the courts. Trials were completed in only 53,137 of them, and 10,689 ended in conviction, a conviction rate of 20.1% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most of the other completed trials ended in acquittal. Another 16,396 cases ended in compromise or compounding, more than the number that ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

An acquittal means the prosecution did not prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. In a marriage case that can happen for reasons that have nothing to do with lying: years pass before trial, witnesses are relatives who change their minds, there is little evidence of what happened behind a closed door, or the woman has gone back to the marriage or moved on. A compromise can be genuine reconciliation, mediation, or pressure on a woman who may depend on the family she accused. The data do not say which.

If a low conviction rate proved that complaints were fake, the same logic would call most rape complaints fake: courts convicted in 24.4% of rape trials completed in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That logic would be wrong for rape. It is wrong for cruelty too.

## Truth: the bigger failure is delay

The number that should worry everyone is not 3.8% or 20.1%. It is 8,54,798: the cruelty cases still pending trial at the end of 2024, 92.2% of all those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At the pace courts disposed of cruelty cases in 2024, by every route, it would take more than a decade just to clear the ones already waiting.

Delay hurts everyone the myth claims to care about. A woman can wait years for a verdict, sometimes while still depending on the family she accused. A man who says he was falsely accused also waits years to be cleared. Long waits can push both sides towards compromises, which are later quoted as proof of misuse.

The other half of the truth is silence. Only 14.1% of women who faced physical or sexual violence ever sought help, and only 6.3% of those went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For every cruelty complaint that reaches a police station, many more never do. The fix is faster investigations and trials, so that the guilty are punished and the wrongly accused are cleared, not disbelief of the women who do complain.

This is general information, not legal advice. If you are facing cruelty now, call 112 in an emergency or the Women Helpline for advice. If you are struggling to cope or having thoughts of suicide, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and open round the clock.
498a-misuse-claim-police-data.hg:
"498A India ka sabse zyada misuse hone wala law hai." Koi aurat pati ya sasural walon ki cruelty ki complaint kare, toh aksar turant yeh line comment sections, WhatsApp forwards aur family arguments mein aa jaati hai. Ise itni baar dohraaya jaata hai ki log ise statistic samajh lete hain. Yeh statistic nahi hai. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) batata hai ki 2024 mein in cases ka kya hua, aur uske numbers ulti kahani kehte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Myth kya hai aur kyun phailta hai

Indian Penal Code ka Section 498A ab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 85 hai. Yeh us pati ya uske relative ko saza deta hai jo kisi aurat ke saath cruelty kare: jaan-boojhkar aisa behaviour jo use suicide ki taraf dhakel sake ya gambhir nuksaan pahunchaye, ya use ya uske parivaar ko property ki gair-kaanooni maang ke liye harass karna. Maximum saza teen saal ki jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2024 mein police ne aise 1,20,227 cases register kiye, jo women ke khilaaf kisi bhi doosre crime se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh myth isliye phailta hai kyunki iske peeche ka darr asli hai. Cruelty complaint mein pati ke maa-baap aur behnon ka naam bhi aa sakta hai, aur jo family maanti hai ki us par jhootha aarop laga hai, use har police visit aur har court date bhaari padti hai. Kuch complaints false hoti hain, aur false case un logon ko sach mein nuksaan pahunchata hai jinke naam usmein hain. Lekin "kuch" ka matlab "zyada tar" nahi hota, aur forward data nahi hota. Rape report karne wali women ko bhi "yeh jhooth bol rahi hai" wali soch jhelni padti hai; us myth ko humne alag se record ke saamne check kiya hai.

## Police files: 4,593 false bata kar band, 1,08,574 mein charge-sheet

Investigation poori hone par police ya toh charge-sheet file karti hai, jisse accused par trial chalta hai, ya final report laga kar case band kar deti hai. 2024 mein police ne cruelty ke 1,20,390 cases ki jaanch poori ki. Inmein se 4,593 "false" bata kar band hue, yaani lagbhag 3.8%, aur 1,08,574 mein charge-sheet file hui, yaani charge-sheeting rate 90.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 3,459 aur cases "mistake of fact or law or civil dispute" bata kar band hue. Inhe jod bhi dein, toh 100 mein se 7 se kam cases kisi bhi tarah ke closure mein gaye.

Women ke khilaaf saare crimes ko milaakar dekhein toh police ne 77.2% cases mein charge-sheet file ki [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cruelty complaints is average se aage rahin: jaanch ke baad police ko das mein se nau cases mein itna saboot mila ki unhe court bheja ja sake.

## 'False' closure ka asli matlab

"Final report false" police ki apni classification hai jo jaanch ke baad hoti hai. Yeh court ka faisla nahi hai, aur NCRB yeh bhi nahi batata ki kisi case ko is category mein kyun daala gaya.

Yeh kitna police par depend karta hai? Women ke khilaaf saare crimes mein 2024 mein India bhar mein 36,895 cases "false" bata kar band hue, aur inmein se 12,217 akele Rajasthan ke the, yaani ek-tihaai. Rajasthan ka charge-sheeting rate 54.1% tha, jo kisi bhi state ya union territory mein sabse kam hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh maanna mushkil hai ki ek state ke complainants baaki desh ke mukaable kahin zyada jhoothe cases banate hain. Zyada chance yeh hai ki "false" wala figure kuch had tak yeh dikhata hai ki kisi state ki police cases kaise band karti hai.

Toh 3.8% saabit hue jhooth ki ginti nahi hai. Yeh is baat ka saboot bhi nahi ki baaki har case sachcha hai. Yeh jaanch ke baad police ka apna verdict hai, national level par false complaints ko naapne ka sabse qareebi number, aur yeh "zyada tar" wali baat ka saath nahi deta.

## Acquittal aur compromise false case ka saboot nahi

Log jo doosre numbers ginate hain, woh courts se aate hain. 2024 mein cruelty ke 9,27,199 cases courts ke saamne the. Inmein se sirf 53,137 mein trial poora hua, aur 10,689 mein conviction hua, yaani conviction rate 20.1% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Baaki poore hue trials mein se zyada tar mein accused bari ho gaye. Iske alawa 16,396 cases compromise ya compounding se khatam hue, jo conviction wale cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Acquittal ka matlab hai ki prosecution case ko har shak se pare saabit nahi kar paaya. Shaadi ke case mein aisa kai wajahon se ho sakta hai jinka jhooth se koi lena-dena nahi: trial shuru hone mein saal lag jaate hain, gawah relatives hote hain jo baad mein palat sakte hain, band darwaze ke peeche kya hua iske saboot kam hote hain, ya aurat shaadi mein wapas ja chuki hoti hai ya zindagi mein aage badh chuki hoti hai. Compromise sachcha mel-milaap bhi ho sakta hai, mediation bhi, aur us aurat par pressure bhi jo shayad usi family par depend karti hai jis par usne aarop lagaya. Data yeh nahi batata ki kaun sa case kis tarah ka tha.

Agar kam conviction rate se saabit hota ki complaints fake hain, toh isi logic se zyada tar rape complaints bhi fake kehlaatin: 2024 mein rape ke jin cases mein trial poora hua, unmein se sirf 24.4% mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape ke liye yeh logic galat hoga. Cruelty ke liye bhi yeh galat hai.

## Sach: sabse badi failure deri hai

Jis number se sabko chinta honi chahiye, woh 3.8% ya 20.1% nahi hai. Woh hai 8,54,798: cruelty ke itne cases 2024 ke end mein trial ke intezaar mein the, courts ke saamne aise saare cases ka 92.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 mein courts ne jis speed se, har tarike se, cruelty cases nipataaye, us speed se sirf pehle se atke cases nipataane mein hi das saal se zyada lagenge.

Deri un sabko chot pahunchati hai jinki fikar ka daawa yeh myth karta hai. Aurat ko saalon tak faisle ka intezaar karna pad sakta hai, kabhi-kabhi usi family par depend rehte hue jis par usne aarop lagaya. Jo aadmi kehta hai ki us par jhootha aarop hai, use bhi bari hone ke liye saalon intezaar karna padta hai. Lamba intezaar dono ko compromise ki taraf dhakel sakta hai, aur phir yahi compromise misuse ke saboot ke taur par ginaaye jaate hain.

Sach ka doosra hissa hai chuppi. Physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali sirf 14.1% women ne kabhi help maangi, aur unmein se bhi sirf 6.3% police ke paas gayin [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Police station tak pahunchne wali har cruelty complaint ke peeche aisi bahut si kahaniyan hain jo kabhi wahan tak nahi pahunchin. Ilaaj hai fast investigation aur fast trial, taaki guilty ko saza mile aur begunaah jaldi bari ho, na ki complaint karne wali women par shak karna.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar aap abhi cruelty jhel rahi hain, toh emergency mein 112 par aur advice ke liye Women Helpline par call kijiye. Agar sab sambhaalna mushkil lag raha hai ya suicide ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye. Yeh free hai aur din-raat khula hai.

acid-attack-trials-by-the-numbers.en:
In 2024, Indian courts finished 24 trials in acid-attack cases involving women. Of those, 13 ended in conviction. That same year 804 such cases were before the courts, and 778 of them, 96.8%, were still pending when the year closed [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The law promises at least 10 years in prison for an acid attack [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Here is what each number in that gap says.

## 118 attacks, 32 attempts, and West Bengal's 30

Police registered 118 acid attacks on women in 2024, with 126 victims, and 32 attempted acid attacks on women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Counting victims of every sex, the totals were 207 attacks and 68 attempts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]: acid attacks are not only crimes against women. The year was split between two codes. Of the 118 attacks on women, 69 were registered under Section 326A of the Indian Penal Code, for offences before 1 July 2024, and 49 under Section 124(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) after that date [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

West Bengal registered 30 of the 118, more than any other state [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A high count can mean more attacks, or more attacks reported and registered for what they are. The table cannot tell those apart. It can only say where police recorded the most.

All of these are FIRs registered under the acid-attack sections, so attacks never reported to police, or booked under other sections, are missing from every line [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 804 in court, 24 finished, 13 convicted

| Acid-attack cases on women in court, 2024 | Cases |
|---|---|
| Before the courts during the year | 804 |
| Trials completed | 24 |
| Ended in conviction | 13 |
| Ended in acquittal | 8 |
| Ended in discharge | 3 |
| Still pending at year end | 778 (96.8%) |

All figures are NCRB's [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Only 115 of the 804 were new cases sent for trial in 2024; the rest had been waiting since earlier years [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Thirteen convictions from 24 finished trials gives a conviction rate of just over half, which sounds respectable. It is a rate built on almost nothing: it describes the few cases that ended, and says nothing about the 778 that did not.

Compare rape, where the courts' backlog is widely called a crisis. At the end of 2024, 89.8% of rape cases before the courts were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For acid attacks on women, the share was higher still.

Now imagine a 20-year-old in a district town whose attacker is charged in 2022. By the end of 2024 her case may be one of the 778. She has gone to hearing after hearing, and the sentence the law promises has not yet been tested in her courtroom. Each year of waiting gives witnesses time to move away, memories time to fade and pressure to give up time to build.

## 10 years to life, on paper

Under Section 124(1) of the BNS, an acid attack that causes permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns or disability is punishable with at least 10 years and up to life imprisonment, plus a fine that must be paid to the victim. Throwing or attempting to throw acid carries 5 to 7 years under Section 124(2) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. These are the same terms that Sections 326A and 326B brought into the Indian Penal Code in 2013 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

A minimum sentence applies only when a trial ends in conviction. In 2024 that happened in 13 acid-attack cases on women, while 778 stayed pending.

The fine meant for the survivor waits on a conviction too. That is why the state's compensation scheme matters: under Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), a survivor can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the attacker is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## 'No deterrent effect': the Supreme Court in 2026

On 4 May 2026, hearing Shaheen Malik v. Union of India, Chief Justice Surya Kant spoke about the acid-attack provisions added to the IPC in 2013, including the 5-to-7-year term for attempts. "Unfortunately, there has been no deterrent effect of the provision," he said. "The cases have increased, victims have multiplied." He asked whether punishment should be harsher, and said those who sell acid illegally should be made liable [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]]. These were oral remarks during a hearing, not a judgment.

The registered numbers have indeed not fallen: across all victims, 202 acid attacks in 2022, 207 in 2023 and 207 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But the court data point to a problem that a longer sentence cannot reach. A harsher penalty changes the outcome for the few cases that finish. It does nothing for the 778 that have not.

The numbers show where to push: courts that finish acid-attack trials, compensation that reaches survivors while they wait, and yearly public data on how long these cases take in each state. Until then, "10 years to life" is a promise that, in 2024, reached a conviction in 13 cases.

This is general information, not legal advice.
acid-attack-trials-by-the-numbers.hg:
2024 mein Indian courts ne auraton par acid attack ke cases mein 24 trials poore kiye. Inmein se 13 mein conviction hua. Usi saal aise 804 cases courts ke saamne the, aur saal khatam hote-hote unmein se 778, yaani 96.8%, abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kanoon acid attack ke liye kam se kam 10 saal jail ka waada karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Is waade aur asliyat ke beech ke gap ka har number kya kehta hai, yeh rahi poori tasveer.

## 118 attacks, 32 koshishein, aur West Bengal ke 30

2024 mein police ne auraton par 118 acid attacks register kiye, jinmein 126 victims the, aur auraton par acid attack ki 32 koshishein bhi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har sex ke victims ko ginein toh total 207 attacks aur 68 koshishein thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]: acid attack sirf auraton ke khilaaf crime nahi hai. Yeh saal do codes mein bata hua tha. Auraton par hue 118 attacks mein se 69 Indian Penal Code ki Section 326A mein register hue, jo 1 July 2024 se pehle ke offences the, aur 49 us tareekh ke baad Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 124(1) mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

West Bengal ne 118 mein se 30 cases register kiye, kisi bhi aur state se zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Zyada count ka matlab zyada attacks bhi ho sakta hai, ya yeh bhi ki zyada attacks report hue aur sahi section mein register hue. Table in dono mein fark nahi kar sakti. Woh sirf yeh batati hai ki police ne sabse zyada cases kahan darj kiye.

Yeh sab acid-attack sections mein register FIRs hain, isliye jo attacks police tak kabhi pahunche hi nahi, ya doosri sections mein book hue, woh kisi bhi line mein nahi hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Court mein 804, poore hue 24, conviction 13

| Auraton par acid attack ke cases, court mein, 2024 | Cases |
|---|---|
| Saal bhar courts ke saamne | 804 |
| Trial poore hue | 24 |
| Conviction hua | 13 |
| Acquittal hua | 8 |
| Discharge hua | 3 |
| Saal ke end mein pending | 778 (96.8%) |

Saare figures NCRB ke hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 804 mein se sirf 115 naye cases the jo 2024 mein trial ke liye bheje gaye; baaki pichhle saalon se intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

24 poore hue trials mein 13 convictions ka matlab hai aadhe se thoda zyada conviction rate, jo sunne mein theek-thaak lagta hai. Par yeh rate lagbhag kuch nahi par tika hai: yeh un gine-chune cases ki baat karta hai jo khatam hue, aur un 778 ke baare mein kuch nahi kehta jo khatam nahi hue.

Rape se compare kijiye, jahan courts ke backlog ko aksar crisis kaha jaata hai. 2024 ke end mein courts ke saamne ke 89.8% rape cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Auraton par acid attack ke cases mein yeh hissa usse bhi zyada tha.

Ab ek hypothetical sochiye: ek district town ki 20 saal ki ladki, jiske attacker par 2022 mein charge lagta hai. 2024 ke end tak uska case un 778 mein se ek ho sakta hai. Woh ek ke baad ek hearing mein jaati hai, aur jo saza kanoon wada karta hai, woh uske courtroom mein abhi tak test hi nahi hui. Intezaar ka har saal gawahon ko idhar-udhar jaane ka, yaadon ko dhundhla padne ka, aur case chhod dene ke pressure ko badhne ka waqt deta hai.

## Kaagaz par 10 saal se umr qaid

BNS ki Section 124(1) ke under, aisa acid attack jo permanent ya partial damage, deformity, burns ya disability kare, uski saza kam se kam 10 saal aur zyada se zyada umr qaid hai, saath mein fine jo victim ko dena hoga. Acid phenkne ya phenkne ki koshish par Section 124(2) ke under 5 se 7 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh wahi sazaein hain jo 2013 mein Sections 326A aur 326B ke zariye Indian Penal Code mein aayi thi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Minimum saza tabhi lagti hai jab trial conviction par khatam ho. 2024 mein auraton par acid attack ke 13 cases mein aisa hua, jabki 778 pending rahe.

Survivor ke liye tay fine bhi conviction ka intezaar karta hai. Isliye state ki compensation scheme maayne rakhti hai: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ki Section 396 ke under survivor State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, tab bhi jab attacker ka kabhi pata na chale aur koi trial na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## 'No deterrent effect': 2026 mein Supreme Court

4 May 2026 ko, Shaheen Malik v. Union of India ki sunwai mein, Chief Justice Surya Kant ne 2013 mein IPC mein jode gaye acid-attack provisions par baat ki, jinmein koshish ke liye 5 se 7 saal wali saza bhi shaamil hai. Unhone kaha, "Unfortunately, there has been no deterrent effect of the provision. The cases have increased, victims have multiplied." Yaani is provision se koi darr nahi bana: cases badhe hain, victims badhe hain. Unhone poochha ki kya saza aur sakht honi chahiye, aur kaha ki gair-kanooni tareeke se acid bechne walon ko bhi zimmedar thehraya jaana chahiye [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]]. Yeh sunwai ke dauraan kahi gayi baatein thi, judgment nahi.

Registered numbers sach mein kam nahi hue: sabhi victims ko milakar 2022 mein 202 acid attacks, 2023 mein 207 aur 2024 mein 207 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Par court ka data ek aisi problem ki taraf ishara karta hai jahan tak lambi saza pahunch hi nahi sakti. Sakht saza un gine-chune cases ka nateeja badlegi jo khatam hote hain. Jo 778 cases khatam hi nahi hue, unke liye woh kuch nahi karti.

Numbers batate hain ki zor kahan lagana hai: aise courts jo acid-attack trials poore karein, compensation jo intezaar ke dauraan hi survivors tak pahunche, aur har saal public data ki har state mein yeh cases kitna time le rahe hain. Tab tak "10 saal se umr qaid" ek aisa waada hai jo 2024 mein sirf 13 cases mein conviction tak pahuncha.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

after-a-daughters-death-family-rights.en:
In 2024, police in India registered 5,737 dowry-death cases, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Behind each is a family that lost a daughter within seven years of her wedding. If that is your family, this guide sets out what the law gives you, from the first report to compensation. It is general information, not legal advice, and free legal aid is available through your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) [[nalsa]].

## The first days: the FIR and what to tell police

Report the death as soon as you can. Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), information about a cognizable offence can be given at any police station, whatever the area where it happened, or electronically, as long as you sign it within three days. The person who reports it must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A family in another town can go to its own local station.

Tell the police, in writing if you can:

- when she married;
- every dowry demand you know of: what was asked for, by whom, when, and what was given;
- what she told you about how she was treated, especially in her last weeks, and who else she told;
- any earlier complaint she made, to the police, a helpline, a counsellor or elders in the family.

If you doubt the account of how she died, say so in writing at the start, before the last rites if you can. Ask which sections the FIR applies, and check that the dowry demands are written into it. If police refuse, our guide to escalating a refused FIR sets out what to do.

## Section 80: what the family will need to show

Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) calls a woman's death a "dowry death" when it was caused by burns or bodily injury, or happened "otherwise than under normal circumstances", within seven years of her marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death her husband or his relative subjected her to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, a demand for dowry. Once that is proved, the law deems the husband or relative to have caused her death, and the punishment is seven years to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For a death before 1 July 2024, the same offence is Section 304B of the old Indian Penal Code [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Because the section covers any death that occurs "otherwise than under normal circumstances", a death the in-laws call an accident or a suicide can still come under it if the dowry-linked cruelty is shown [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The pattern is old: the UN Office on Drugs and Crime, analysing NCRB data, found that dowry deaths made up 40% to 50% of all female homicides recorded each year in India between 1999 and 2016 [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]].

Much of the proof sits with her own family. Start gathering it now:

| What must be shown | What can help prove it |
|---|---|
| Death within seven years of marriage | Wedding card, marriage certificate, photos |
| A demand for dowry | Messages, lists, receipts, bank transfers, names of those present |
| Cruelty or harassment soon before her death | Call logs, voice notes, chats, letters, people she confided in |
| Death not under normal circumstances | Post-mortem report, hospital records |

Section 80 does not define "soon before" in days, which is why her last calls and messages matter. Keep the originals safe, make copies, and note who holds what.

## Your rights as her family under the BNSS

The procedure code that replaced the CrPC on 1 July 2024 gives the informant and the victim's side specific rights [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]:

- **A free copy of the FIR**, as soon as it is recorded.
- **An update within 90 days.** Police must tell the informant or the victim how the investigation is going within 90 days, by any means, including electronically.
- **Free copies of the case papers.** Within 14 days of the accused first appearing in court, the victim, if represented by a lawyer, must get free copies of the police report, the FIR and the recorded statements.
- **A say before any withdrawal.** No court may allow the prosecution to be withdrawn without first hearing the victim.

The third right depends on having a lawyer, one more reason to find one early. If you cannot afford one, ask the DLSA for free legal aid [[nalsa]].

## Compensation: Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh, and how to apply

Under Section 396 of the BNSS, formerly Section 357A of the CrPC, every state must run a victim compensation scheme [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. NALSA's 2018 scheme for women victims of crime sets Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for the family of a woman killed [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

Compensation is not tied only to a conviction. Under Section 396, where the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, the victim's dependants can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority, which must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

To begin, go to the DLSA, usually at the district court, with copies of the FIR, the post-mortem report and the death certificate. Ask how your state's scheme works, who in the family can claim, and what support exists for any children she left behind.

## Staying with a case that may take years

Expect a long road. In 2024, courts had 63,516 dowry-death cases before them and finished trials in only 4,043. Of those, 1,869 ended in conviction, a rate of 46.2%, well above the 25.7% for all crimes against women. At the end of the year, 59,446 cases, or 93.6%, were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A case with good evidence can succeed, but slowly. To stay with it:

- keep one file with the FIR, every notice, every order and every hearing date;
- meet the public prosecutor before important hearings, and tell the court if anyone pressures a witness;
- write to the investigating officer if 90 days pass without an update.

Grief does not follow the court calendar. If it becomes too heavy, or if anyone in the family has thoughts of suicide, Tele-MANAS offers free counselling round the clock on 14416 [[tele-manas]].
after-a-daughters-death-family-rights.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne dowry death ke 5,737 cases register kiye, yaani roz qareeb 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har case ke peeche ek family hai jisne apni beti ko uski shaadi ke saat saal ke andar kho diya. Agar yeh aapki family ke saath hua hai, toh yeh guide batati hai ki pehli report se lekar compensation tak kanoon aapko kya deta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi, aur aapki District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) ke zariye free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]].

## Pehle kuch din: FIR aur police ko kya batayein

Maut ki report jitni jaldi ho sake kijiye. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173 ke mutabik, kisi cognizable offence ki jaankari kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, chahe offence kisi bhi area mein hua ho, ya electronically bhi, bas teen din ke andar us par sign karna hoga. Report karne wale ko FIR ki copy free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Doosre shehar mein rehne wali family apne local police station ja sakti hai.

Police ko, ho sake toh likhkar, yeh batayiye:

- uski shaadi kab hui thi;
- dowry ki har woh demand jo aapko pata hai: kya maanga gaya, kisne maanga, kab, aur kya diya gaya;
- usne aapko apne saath hone wale bartaav ke baare mein kya bataya, khaaskar aakhri hafton mein, aur kis-kis ko bataya;
- usne pehle koi complaint ki ho toh woh bhi, chahe police mein, kisi helpline par, kisi counsellor se ya family ke bado se.

Agar aapko uski maut ki batayi gayi kahani par shak hai, toh shuru mein hi likhkar kahiye, ho sake toh antim sanskar se pehle. Poochiye ki FIR mein kaunse sections lagaye gaye hain, aur check kijiye ki dowry ki demands usme likhi hain. Agar police FIR likhne se mana kare, toh refused FIR ko escalate karne par hamari guide batati hai ki kya karna hai.

## Section 80: family ko kya dikhana hoga

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 80 kisi aurat ki maut ko "dowry death" tab kehta hai jab maut jalne ya shareer par chot se hui ho, ya "normal circumstances se hatkar" hui ho, shaadi ke saat saal ke andar, aur yeh dikhaya jaye ki maut se kuch hi pehle uske pati ya pati ke kisi rishtedar ne dowry ki kisi demand ke liye, ya usse jude maamle mein, uske saath cruelty ki ya use harass kiya. Yeh prove ho jaye, toh kanoon maan leta hai ki uski maut pati ya us rishtedar ne hi ki, aur saza saat saal se lekar umrqaid tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 1 July 2024 se pehle hui maut ke liye yahi offence purane Indian Penal Code ka Section 304B hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Kyunki yeh section "normal circumstances se hatkar" hui kisi bhi maut ko cover karta hai, isliye jis maut ko sasural wale accident ya suicide batayein, woh bhi iske daayre mein aa sakti hai, agar dowry se judi cruelty dikhayi jaye [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh pattern purana hai: UN Office on Drugs and Crime ne NCRB data ka analysis karke paaya ki 1999 se 2016 ke beech India mein har saal record hue auraton ke saare homicides mein 40% se 50% dowry deaths thi [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]].

Zyada tar saboot uski apni family ke paas hote hain. Inhe abhi se ikattha karna shuru kijiye:

| Kya dikhana hoga | Kya prove karne mein madad karega |
|---|---|
| Shaadi ke saat saal ke andar maut | Shaadi ka card, marriage certificate, photos |
| Dowry ki demand | Messages, lists, receipts, bank transfers, wahan maujood logon ke naam |
| Maut se kuch hi pehle cruelty ya harassment | Call logs, voice notes, chats, chitthiyan, woh log jinse usne apni baat kahi |
| Normal circumstances se hatkar maut | Post-mortem report, hospital records |

Section 80 "kuch hi pehle" ko dinon mein define nahi karta, isliye uske aakhri calls aur messages bahut maayne rakhte hain. Originals sambhaal kar rakhiye, copies banaiye, aur likh lijiye ki kaunsi cheez kiske paas hai.

## BNSS ke under uski family ke haq

1 July 2024 ko CrPC ki jagah lene wala procedure code informant aur victim ki side ko kuch saaf haq deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]:

- **FIR ki free copy**, jaise hi woh darj ho.
- **90 din ke andar update.** Police ko 90 din ke andar informant ya victim ko batana hota hai ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi, kisi bhi tareeke se, electronically bhi.
- **Case ke papers ki free copies.** Accused ke court mein pehli baar pesh hone ke 14 din ke andar, victim ko, agar uska lawyer hai, police report, FIR aur record kiye gaye statements ki free copies milni chahiye.
- **Case wapas lene se pehle sunwai.** Koi bhi court victim ki baat sune bina prosecution ko case wapas lene ki ijaazat nahi de sakti.

Teesra haq lawyer hone par tika hai, isliye jaldi lawyer dhoondhne ki yeh ek aur wajah hai. Agar aap lawyer afford nahi kar sakte, toh DLSA se free legal aid maangiye [[nalsa]].

## Compensation: Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh, aur apply kaise karein

BNSS ke Section 396 (pehle CrPC ka Section 357A) ke mutabik har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Crime ki shikaar auraton ke liye NALSA ki 2018 ki scheme maari gayi aurat ki family ke liye Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh tay karti hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

Compensation sirf conviction par tika nahi hai. Section 396 ke under, jahan offender ka kabhi pata na chale aur trial hi na ho, wahan victim ke dependants seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority ko apply kar sakte hain, aur authority ko do mahine ke andar apni inquiry poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Shuruaat ke liye DLSA jaiye, jo aksar district court mein hoti hai, aur saath mein FIR, post-mortem report aur death certificate ki copies le jaiye. Poochiye ki aapke state ki scheme kaise kaam karti hai, family mein kaun claim kar sakta hai, aur agar uske bachche hain toh unke liye kya madad hai.

## Saalon chal sakne wale case ke saath kaise tike rahein

Lamba raasta maankar chaliye. 2024 mein courts ke saamne dowry death ke 63,516 cases the, aur sirf 4,043 ke trials poore hue. Unme se 1,869 mein conviction hua, yaani 46.2% rate, jo auraton ke khilaf saare crimes ke 25.7% se kaafi zyada hai. Saal ke end mein 59,446 cases, yaani 93.6%, abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Achhe saboot wala case jeet sakta hai, par dheere-dheere. Tike rehne ke liye:

- ek file banaiye jisme FIR, har notice, har order aur har hearing ki date ho;
- zaroori hearings se pehle public prosecutor se miliye, aur agar koi kisi gawah par dabaav daale toh court ko bataiye;
- agar 90 din tak koi update na mile, toh investigating officer ko likhiye.

Dukh court ke calendar ke hisaab se nahi chalta. Agar yeh bahut bhaari ho jaye, ya family mein kisi ke man mein suicide ke khayal aayein, toh Tele-MANAS din-raat free counselling deta hai, 14416 par [[tele-manas]].

bns-renumbered-home-crimes-498a-section-.en:
Consider a hypothetical: a woman who reported a violent husband for cruelty in 2023 would have got an FIR that said "498A". Had the cruelty happened after 1 July 2024, it would say "Section 85". The crime did not change; the number did, and that still confuses complainants, families and anyone reading India's crime data. Here is a cheat sheet to the home crimes the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) renumbered, and the one rule Parliament chose to keep. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why the numbers changed on 1 July 2024

The BNS, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam came into force across India on 1 July 2024, replacing the Indian Penal Code (IPC), the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Evidence Act [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]].

The date of the offence, not the date of the complaint, decides which code applies. Offences committed before 1 July 2024 are still registered under the IPC [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is why the National Crime Records Bureau's 2024 tables have an IPC column and a BNS column, and why 2024's 1,20,227 cruelty cases are counted under 498A IPC and Section 85 BNS together [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| The crime | IPC section | BNS section | Punishment or effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cruelty by husband or his relatives | 498A | 85, with "cruelty" defined in 86 | Up to 3 years and a fine |
| Dowry death | 304B | 80 | 7 years to life |
| Acid attack | 326A | 124(1) | 10 years to life, plus a fine paid to the victim |
| Throwing or attempting to throw acid | 326B | 124(2) | 5 to 7 years |
| Marital rape exception | 375, Exception 2 | 63, Exception 2 | A husband's sex with his wife, if she is 18 or over, is not rape |

Two other home-crime laws kept their numbers, because they were never part of the IPC: the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, under which giving or taking dowry carries at least five years [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]], and the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## 498A to 85-86: cruelty

Section 85 punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty with up to three years in prison and a fine. Section 86 defines cruelty in two parts: wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or to cause her grave injury; or harassment to force her or her family to meet an unlawful demand for property [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide is enough under the first part, so a complaint does not need a bruise.

It remains India's largest single category of crime against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A related change matters to the same families. Abetment of suicide moved from IPC Sections 305 and 306 to BNS Sections 107 and 108, and police registered 4,220 cases of abetment of suicide of women in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Anyone having thoughts of suicide can call Tele-MANAS on 14416, free and round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

## 304B to 80: dowry death

Section 80 calls a woman's death a "dowry death" when she dies of burns, bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of marriage, after her husband or his relatives subjected her to cruelty or harassment over dowry soon before her death. The husband or relative is then deemed to have caused the death, and the punishment is seven years to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

India recorded 5,737 dowry-death cases with 5,811 victims in 2024, about 16 a day, counted under 304B IPC and Section 80 BNS together [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 326A to 124: acid attack

The acid-attack offences date from 2013: the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 created them as Sections 326A and 326B of the IPC [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. The BNS folded both into Section 124: at least 10 years and up to life for an attack, with a fine paid to the victim for treatment, and five to seven years for throwing or attempting to throw acid [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

India registered 207 acid attacks in 2024, the same as in 2023, plus 68 attempts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In May 2026 Chief Justice Surya Kant remarked in court that the 2013 provisions had had "no deterrent effect" [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]]. The duties around it moved too. Every hospital must treat a survivor immediately and free under Section 397 of the BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; a hospital in-charge who refuses can be punished under Section 200 BNS, and a police officer who fails to record an acid-attack complaint commits a crime under Section 199 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## The exception that survived: Section 63

When Parliament rewrote rape law in 2013, it kept Exception 2 to Section 375: sex by a man with his own wife, if she was not under 15, was not rape [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. In *Independent Thought v. Union of India* (2017), the Supreme Court read the exception down to cover only wives aged 18 or over, and left the question of adult wives open [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

The BNS renumbered these offences and could have ended the exception. It kept it. Exception 2 to Section 63 says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Forced sex with a wife who lives separately is a crime under Section 67, but it carries two to seven years, well below the 10-year minimum for rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

In December 2024 the government told the Rajya Sabha it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape, pointing instead to the 2005 Domestic Violence Act and to BNS sections including Section 85 [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. On 9 September 2026 a three-judge Supreme Court bench posted the marital rape cases for final hearing, to decide whether the exception is valid [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

Until it rules, a wife aged 18 or over who is forced by her husband is left with routes like the ones the government named: a cruelty complaint under Section 85, or the 2005 Act, which counts sexual abuse as domestic violence [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. The numbers are new. The gap is the old one.
bns-renumbered-home-crimes-498a-section-.hg:
Ek hypothetical sochiye: agar kisi aurat ne 2023 mein apne violent pati ki cruelty ki police mein report ki hoti, toh uski FIR par likha hota "498A". Agar yahi cruelty 1 July 2024 ke baad hui hoti, toh FIR par likha hota "Section 85". Crime nahi badla; number badal gaya, aur yeh chhota sa badlaav aaj bhi complainants, families aur India ka crime data padhne wale har insaan ko confuse karta hai. Yeh ghar ke un crimes ki cheat sheet hai jinka number Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne badla, aur us ek rule ki bhi jo Parliament ne rehne diya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1 July 2024 ko number kyun badle

BNS, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) aur Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 1 July 2024 se poore India mein laagu hue, aur inhone Indian Penal Code (IPC), Code of Criminal Procedure aur Evidence Act ki jagah le li [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]].

Kaunsa code lagega, yeh complaint ki date se nahi, offence ki date se tay hota hai. 1 July 2024 se pehle hue offences aaj bhi IPC ke under register hote hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isiliye National Crime Records Bureau ki 2024 tables mein ek IPC column hai aur ek BNS column, aur isiliye 2024 ke 1,20,227 cruelty cases 498A IPC aur Section 85 BNS dono ko mila kar gine gaye hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| Crime | IPC section | BNS section | Saza ya asar |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty | 498A | 85, "cruelty" ki definition 86 mein | 3 saal tak jail aur fine |
| Dowry death | 304B | 80 | 7 saal se umrkaid tak |
| Acid attack | 326A | 124(1) | 10 saal se umrkaid tak, aur victim ko diya jaane wala fine |
| Acid phenkna ya phenkne ki koshish | 326B | 124(2) | 5 se 7 saal |
| Marital rape exception | 375, Exception 2 | 63, Exception 2 | 18 ya usse zyada umar ki wife ke saath pati ka sex rape nahi maana jaata |

Ghar se jude do aur laws ke number nahi badle, kyunki woh kabhi IPC ka hissa the hi nahi: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, jisme dowry dene ya lene par kam se kam paanch saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]], aur Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## 498A se 85-86: cruelty

Section 85 us pati ya uske relative ko teen saal tak jail aur fine ki saza deta hai jo kisi aurat ke saath cruelty karta hai. Section 86 cruelty ko do hisson mein define karta hai: jaan-boojh kar kiya gaya aisa bartaav jo use suicide ki taraf dhakel sakta ho ya use gambhir chot pahuncha sakta ho; ya use ya uski family ko property ki kisi gair-kanooni demand poori karne ke liye majboor karne wali harassment [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Pehle hisse ke under aisa bartaav kaafi hai jo aurat ko suicide ki taraf dhakel sakta ho, isliye complaint ke liye kisi chot ke nishaan ki zaroorat nahi.

Yeh aaj bhi auraton ke khilaf crime ki sabse badi single category hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek aur badlaav inhi families ke liye maayne rakhta hai. Abetment of suicide IPC ke Sections 305 aur 306 se BNS ke Sections 107 aur 108 mein gaya, aur 2024 mein police ne auraton ke abetment of suicide ke 4,220 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Agar kisi ke mann mein suicide ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh woh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kar sakta hai; yeh free hai aur din-raat chalta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

## 304B se 80: dowry death

Section 80 kisi aurat ki maut ko "dowry death" tab kehta hai jab shaadi ke saat saal ke andar uski maut jalne se, sharir par chot se ya normal circumstances se hatkar ho, aur maut se kuch hi pehle uske pati ya pati ke relatives ne dowry ke liye uske saath cruelty ya harassment ki ho. Tab law maan leta hai ki maut pati ya usi relative ki wajah se hui, aur saza saat saal se umrkaid tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

2024 mein India mein dowry death ke 5,737 cases record hue, jinme 5,811 victims thin, yaani roz lagbhag 16; yeh 304B IPC aur Section 80 BNS dono ko mila kar gine gaye hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 326A se 124: acid attack

Acid attack ke offences 2013 se hain: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne inhe IPC ke Sections 326A aur 326B ke roop mein banaya tha [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. BNS ne dono ko Section 124 mein jod diya: attack ke liye kam se kam 10 saal se umrkaid tak, saath mein victim ke ilaaj ke liye use diya jaane wala fine, aur acid phenkne ya phenkne ki koshish ke liye paanch se saat saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

2024 mein India mein 207 acid attacks register hue, utne hi jitne 2023 mein, aur 68 attempts alag se [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. May 2026 mein Chief Justice Surya Kant ne court mein kaha ki 2013 ke provisions ka "no deterrent effect" raha, yaani unse attacks ruke nahi [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]]. Is offence se judi duties bhi shift hui hain. Har hospital ko survivor ka turant aur free ilaaj BNSS ke Section 397 ke under karna hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; mana karne wale hospital in-charge ko Section 200 BNS ke under saza ho sakti hai, aur acid attack ki complaint record na karne wala police officer Section 199 ke under crime karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Jo exception bach gaya: Section 63

2013 mein jab Parliament ne rape law dobara likha, toh usne Section 375 ka Exception 2 rehne diya: kisi aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex, agar wife 15 se kam nahi thi, rape nahi tha [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. *Independent Thought v. Union of India* (2017) mein Supreme Court ne exception ko "read down" karke sirf 18 ya usse zyada umar ki wives tak seemit kar diya, aur adult wives ka sawaal khula chhod diya [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

BNS ne in offences ke number badle, aur woh is exception ko khatam bhi kar sakta tha. Usne ise rehne diya. Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki kisi aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex, agar wife 18 se kam nahi hai, rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Alag reh rahi wife ke saath zabardasti sex Section 67 ke under crime hai, par iski saza do se saat saal hai, jo rape ki kam se kam 10 saal ki saza se kaafi kam hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

December 2024 mein sarkar ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki marital rape ko crime banane ka uska koi proposal nahi hai, aur iski jagah 2005 ke Domestic Violence Act aur Section 85 samet BNS ke kuch sections ki taraf ishaara kiya [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. 9 September 2026 ko Supreme Court ki teen judges ki bench ne marital rape cases ko final hearing ke liye list kiya, yeh tay karne ke liye ki exception valid hai ya nahi [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

Jab tak court faisla nahi deti, pati ki zabardasti jhel rahi 18 ya usse zyada umar ki wife ke paas waise hi raaste bachte hain jaise sarkar ne ginaye: Section 85 ke under cruelty ki complaint, ya 2005 ka Act, jo sexual abuse ko domestic violence maanta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Number naye hain. Gap wahi purana hai.

centre-marital-rape-affidavit-alternativ.en:
In an affidavit verified on 3 October 2024, the Union government told the Supreme Court that marital rape is "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue", and that making it rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. Married women, it argued, already have remedies under other criminal provisions and the 2005 Domestic Violence Act [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. Two months later it told Parliament the same thing and named the sections. We tested each remedy against the law's own text: what a wife has to prove, the most a court can give, and what the record will call it. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What the Centre told the Supreme Court

Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says that sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The Centre wants it kept. Yet its own affidavit concedes the central point: "a husband certainly does not have any fundamental right to violate the consent of the wife" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]].

So the dispute is not whether a wife may refuse. It is what the law calls it when her husband overrides her refusal, and how hard it punishes him. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 4.6% of ever-married women aged 18-49 said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## No proposal: the December 2024 answer

In December 2024, Scroll reported, the Union government told the Rajya Sabha that it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape. It pointed instead to the Domestic Violence Act and to four BNS sections: 74, 75, 76 and 85 [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. Here is what each carries, set against rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]:

| Offence | Punishment |
|---|---|
| Cruelty (BNS 85) | Up to 3 years, and a fine |
| Assault to outrage modesty (BNS 74) | 1 to 5 years |
| Sexual harassment (BNS 75) | Up to 3 years |
| Assault to disrobe (BNS 76) | 3 to 7 years |
| Breaking a protection order (Domestic Violence Act, Section 31) | Up to 1 year, a Rs 20,000 fine, or both |
| Rape (BNS 64) | At least 10 years, up to life |

Even the heaviest remedy on the list tops out three years below the minimum for rape.

## Remedy one: cruelty, up to three years

Section 85 punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty with up to three years in prison and a fine. Section 86 defines cruelty as wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to force her or her family to meet unlawful demands for property [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

It is the law wives actually use: police registered 1,20,227 cruelty cases in 2024, the largest category of crimes against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But the definition does not mention sex or consent. A wife must fit forced sex into words written for something else, and if she succeeds, the FIR, the chargesheet and the national crime count will all call it cruelty.

In 2024 courts convicted in 10,689 cruelty cases, 20.1% of the trials they completed, while 16,396 cases ended in compromise and 92.2% of the 9,27,199 before them were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The data do not say how many compromises were reconciliations and how many followed pressure on the woman.

If abuse at home has brought on thoughts of suicide, call Tele-MANAS, the free national mental-health helpline, on 14416 [[tele-manas]].

## Remedies two and three: the 'modesty' sections and the Domestic Violence Act

Sections 74 to 76 were written for assault, harassment and disrobing, and Section 74 frames the harm as an outrage to a woman's "modesty", not a violation of her body [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. If she is injured, voluntarily causing hurt carries at most one year, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The Domestic Violence Act at least names the act: it counts "sexual abuse", any sexual conduct that abuses, humiliates, degrades or violates a woman's dignity, as domestic violence [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. But the forced sex itself is not an offence under the Act. What it offers is a protection order from a magistrate, and the crime it creates is breaking that order, which carries at most one year [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Its criminal side barely moves. Police registered 616 cases under the Act in 2024, 496 of them in Kerala, and of 4,017 such cases before criminal courts, 84 trials ended that year, 22 in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are criminal cases only, so they cannot show how many women won a protection order.

## The word none of them uses

The word is "rape", and it decides three things.

**The sentence.** Rape carries at least 10 years. Rape by a relative, guardian, teacher or anyone in a position of trust or authority over the woman is an aggravated form, punishable up to imprisonment for the rest of the offender's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A husband is the one man in that circle whom the definition leaves out.

**The procedure.** The BNSS gives trials under BNS Sections 64 to 68, 70 and 71 a two-month deadline from the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Cruelty, the modesty sections and the Domestic Violence Act are not on that list.

**The name.** Section 67 shows the law can name the act when it wants to: a husband who has sex with his wife without her consent while they live separately faces 2 to 7 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under one roof, there is no such offence. One Supreme Court ruling already uses the word: in 2022 it read "rape" in the abortion law to include marital rape, so a wife pregnant from forced sex by her husband can seek an abortion up to 24 weeks as a rape survivor, without an FIR [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

The court will now decide whether the exception is valid and whether a husband can be prosecuted while it stands [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. As of 19 November 2026 it had not ruled, and said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Until then, these remedies are what a wife has. They are worth using. They are not the same thing.
centre-marital-rape-affidavit-alternativ.hg:
3 October 2024 ko verify hue ek affidavit mein Union government ne Supreme Court se kaha ki marital rape "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" hai, yaani kanooni se zyada ek samajik mudda, aur ise rape ka darja dena "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" ho sakta hai [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. Uski daleel thi ki shaadishuda auraton ke paas pehle se doosre criminal provisions aur 2005 ke Domestic Violence Act ke remedies hain [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]]. Do mahine baad usne Parliament ko yahi baat kahi, aur sections ke naam bhi gina diye. Humne har remedy ko kanoon ke apne text par parkha: biwi ko kya prove karna padega, court zyada se zyada kya saza de sakti hai, aur record mein ise kya naam milega. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Centre ne Supreme Court se kya kaha

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar biwi 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sexual intercourse ya sexual acts karna rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Centre chahta hai ki yeh exception bana rahe. Phir bhi uska apna affidavit asli baat maan leta hai: "a husband certainly does not have any fundamental right to violate the consent of the wife", yaani pati ko biwi ki consent todne ka koi fundamental right nahi hai [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]].

Matlab jhagda yeh nahi hai ki biwi mana kar sakti hai ya nahi. Jhagda yeh hai ki jab pati uske mana karne ko kuchal de, toh kanoon use kya naam de, aur pati ko kitni sakht saza de. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 18-49 saal ki 4.6% ever-married auraton ne kaha ki unke pati ne unhe physically majboor karke intercourse kiya, jab woh nahi chahti thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## No proposal: December 2024 ka jawab

Scroll ki report ke mutabik, December 2024 mein Union government ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki uske paas marital rape ko crime banane ka koi proposal nahi hai. Iski jagah usne Domestic Violence Act aur BNS ke chaar sections ki taraf ishara kiya: 74, 75, 76 aur 85 [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. Dekhiye har ek mein kitni saza hai, rape ke saamne rakhkar [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]:

| Offence | Saza |
|---|---|
| Cruelty (BNS 85) | 3 saal tak, aur fine |
| Modesty bhang karne ke liye assault (BNS 74) | 1 se 5 saal |
| Sexual harassment (BNS 75) | 3 saal tak |
| Kapde utaarne ke iraade se assault (BNS 76) | 3 se 7 saal |
| Protection order todna (Domestic Violence Act, Section 31) | 1 saal tak, Rs 20,000 fine, ya dono |
| Rape (BNS 64) | Kam se kam 10 saal, life tak |

List ki sabse bhaari remedy ki maximum saza bhi rape ki minimum saza se teen saal kam hai.

## Remedy ek: cruelty, teen saal tak

Section 85 us pati ya uske rishtedar ko teen saal tak ki jail aur fine ki saza deta hai jo kisi aurat ke saath cruelty kare. Section 86 cruelty ko aise define karta hai: jaan-boojhkar kiya gaya aisa bartaav jo use suicide ki taraf dhakel sake ya gambhir chot pahuncha sake, ya use ya uski family ko property ki illegal demand poori karne ke liye harass karna [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Biwiyan asal mein yahi kanoon use karti hain: 2024 mein police ne cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye, jo auraton ke khilaf crimes ki sabse badi category hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Par is definition mein sex ya consent ka zikr tak nahi hai. Biwi ko zabardasti sex ko kisi aur cheez ke liye likhe gaye shabdon mein fit karna padta hai, aur agar woh kamyab ho bhi jaye, toh FIR, chargesheet aur desh ka crime count, sab ise cruelty hi kahenge.

2024 mein courts ne cruelty ke 10,689 cases mein conviction diya, yaani jitne trials poore hue unme se 20.1% mein. Usi saal 16,396 cases compromise par khatam hue, aur courts ke saamne pade 9,27,199 cases mein se 92.2% abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data yeh nahi batata ki inme se kitne compromise sach mein sulah the aur kitne aurat par dabaav ke baad hue.

Agar ghar ki hinsa ki wajah se aapke man mein suicide ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh sarkar ki free national mental health helpline Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye [[tele-manas]].

## Remedy do aur teen: 'modesty' wale sections aur Domestic Violence Act

Sections 74 se 76 assault, harassment aur kapde utaarne ke liye likhe gaye the, aur Section 74 is nuksaan ko aurat ki "modesty" ka apmaan maanta hai, uske shareer ka ullanghan nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Agar use chot lagi ho, toh voluntarily causing hurt mein zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail, Rs 10,000 tak fine, ya dono hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Domestic Violence Act kam se kam is cheez ka naam toh leta hai: yeh "sexual abuse" ko, yaani aisa koi bhi sexual bartaav jo aurat ko zaleel kare, neecha dikhaye, uski dignity ko thes pahunchaye ya uska ullanghan kare, domestic violence maanta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Par zabardasti sex khud is Act mein offence nahi hai. Yeh magistrate se protection order dilwata hai, aur iska crime hai us order ko todna, jisme zyada se zyada ek saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Criminal side par yeh Act mushkil se hilta hai. 2024 mein police ne is Act mein sirf 616 cases register kiye, jinme se 496 Kerala ke the, aur criminal courts ke saamne aise 4,017 cases mein se us saal 84 trials poore hue, jinme se 22 mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh sirf criminal cases hain, isliye in figures se yeh pata nahi chalta ki kitni auraton ko protection order mila.

## Woh shabd jo inme se koi nahi bolta

Woh shabd hai "rape", aur yeh teen cheezein tay karta hai.

**Saza.** Rape mein kam se kam 10 saal ki saza hai. Kisi rishtedar, guardian, teacher ya aurat par trust ya authority rakhne wale kisi bhi insaan ka kiya rape aggravated form hai, jisme offender ki baaki poori zindagi tak jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Is daayre mein pati akela aisa aadmi hai jise definition bahar chhod deti hai.

**Procedure.** BNSS ke mutabik BNS ke Sections 64 se 68, 70 aur 71 ke trials chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar poore hone chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Cruelty, modesty wale sections aur Domestic Violence Act is list mein hain hi nahi.

**Naam.** Section 67 dikhata hai ki kanoon chahe toh is kaam ka naam le sakta hai: jo pati alag reh rahi biwi ke saath uski consent ke bina sex kare, use 2 se 7 saal ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ek hi chhat ke neeche aisa koi offence nahi hai. Supreme Court ka ek faisla yeh shabd pehle se use karta hai: 2022 mein court ne abortion law ke "rape" mein marital rape ko bhi shaamil maana, isliye pati ke zabardasti sex se pregnant hui biwi rape survivor ke roop mein 24 hafte tak abortion maang sakti hai, bina FIR ke [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Ab court decide karegi ki exception valid hai ya nahi, aur jab tak yeh bana hua hai tab tak pati par case chal sakta hai ya nahi [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. 19 November 2026 tak court ne faisla nahi diya tha, aur kaha tha ki woh final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko fix karegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]]. Tab tak biwi ke paas yahi remedies hain. Inhe zaroor use kijiye. Par yeh rape law ke barabar nahi hain.

child-brides-domestic-violence-india.en:
An estimated 640 million girls and women alive today were married as children, and one in three of them lives in India [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]]. That total includes grandmothers married decades ago, but the weddings have not stopped. UNICEF India estimates that at least 1.5 million Indian girls are still married before 18 every year [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]], and in the National Family Health Survey for 2023-24 (NFHS-6, provisional), 20.1% of women aged 20 to 24 had married before 18 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Most reporting on child marriage ends at the wedding. This story follows the girl inside the house, where she becomes a wife, a daughter-in-law and often a mother before the law counts her as an adult.

## 640 million, a third in India

The global figure is huge because it adds up a lifetime of weddings. The present is smaller, and still enormous: UNICEF India puts the share of girls aged 15 to 19 who are currently married at nearly 16% [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]], roughly one in six.

UNICEF links child marriage to two harms that travel together: girls who marry before 18 are more likely to experience domestic violence and less likely to stay in school [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. When a girl leaves school, she loses the one place outside her marital home where an adult who is not family sees her every day, and might notice a bruise, a silence or an empty seat.

## Violence comes early

India's main survey cannot say how many wives under 18 are being hurt: NFHS-5 (2019-21) reports violence by husbands only for women aged 18 to 49 [[nfhs5-india-2021]], so wives of 15, 16 or 17 are missing from it. The nearest yardstick is global. The World Health Organization estimates that 23.3% of ever-married or partnered girls aged 15 to 19 worldwide have already faced physical or sexual violence from a partner, and 16.0% in the past 12 months alone [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Indian data does show when the violence begins. Among currently married women in NFHS-5 who had married only once, 11.2% had faced physical or sexual violence from their husband within two years of the wedding, and 20.9% within five [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For a girl married at 16, those first two years end before she turns 18.

The law on paper is clear. Since the Supreme Court's 2017 judgment in *Independent Thought v. Union of India*, sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita keeps that line: its marital exception covers only wives aged 18 or over [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A wedding does not make a 16-year-old's consent possible. It only makes the crime harder to see.

## Pregnancy without a choice: 17.8% unmet need

In NFHS-5, only 28.1% of currently married girls aged 15 to 19 were using any contraception, and 17.8% had an unmet need for family planning: they wanted to delay or avoid pregnancy but were using nothing [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Among all married women, unmet need was 9.4% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The youngest wives are almost twice as likely to go without the protection they want.

Unmet need measures the gap between what a woman wants and what she can do. For a teenage bride, closing it means asking a husband who may be years older, a mother-in-law waiting for a grandchild, or a health worker who knows the family. Many never get the chance: by age 19, 20.0% of young women in NFHS-5 had already begun childbearing [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Why a child bride rarely reports

Even adult women seldom report violence at home. In NFHS-5, 77.2% of women aged 18 to 49 who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone, and only 11.3% of those abused solely by their current husband ever sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

A wife of 16 has less of everything that makes reporting possible. Consider a hypothetical: she left school after Class 9, has no money of her own and uses her husband's phone. Her parents arranged the marriage and paid for it. Reporting the abuse means accusing her husband of a crime. Reporting the marriage means exposing her own parents, because the law punishes anyone who performs or abets a child marriage [[indiacode-pcma-2006]].

The system rarely reaches her first. Police registered 1,499 cases under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act across India in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], in a country where, by UNICEF India's estimate, at least 1.5 million girls are married every year. Courts that year convicted in 209 such cases and acquitted in 625 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Getting out: annulment, 1098 and a trusted adult

There are exits, and timing decides which one works. This is general information, not legal advice.

**Before the wedding.** Child Helpline 1098 is linked to the emergency number 112 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. In October 2024 the Supreme Court told states to appoint district Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with no other duties, and told magistrates to issue injunctions on their own, especially around "auspicious days" for mass weddings [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

**After the wedding.** A child marriage is voidable at the choice of the person who was a child: she can petition a district court to annul it until two years after she turns 18 [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. If she was lured away, forced or deceived into the marriage, or sold for it, the marriage is void from the start.

**While she is under 18.** Anyone who knows or suspects that a child is being sexually abused must report it to the police under Sections 19 and 21 of the POCSO Act [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]], and a wedding does not turn a 16-year-old into an adult. A teacher cannot promise a married student secrecy, but can promise not to leave her alone with what comes next.

**At any age.** One Stop Centres help women facing violence: 985 were operational as of July 2026, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

Child marriage is still defended as a way to keep a girl safe. The evidence says otherwise, and the law gives her a way out, if someone tells her in time.
child-brides-domestic-violence-india.hg:
Andaaza hai ki aaj zinda 640 million ladkiyon aur auraton ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi, aur inmein se har teesri India mein rehti hai [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]]. Is total mein woh daadi-naani bhi shaamil hain jinki shaadi dashakon pehle hui thi, par aisi shaadiyan ruki nahi hain. UNICEF India ka estimate hai ki aaj bhi har saal kam se kam 1.5 million Indian ladkiyon ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho jaati hai [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]], aur 2023-24 ke National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6, provisional) mein 20 se 24 saal ki 20.1% auraton ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Child marriage par zyada tar reporting shaadi par hi khatam ho jaati hai. Yeh story us ladki ke peeche ghar ke andar jaati hai, jahan woh law ki nazar mein adult banne se pehle hi wife, bahu aur aksar maa ban jaati hai.

## 640 million, inmein ek-tihai India mein

Global figure itna bada isliye hai kyunki yeh ek poori zindagi ki shaadiyon ko jodta hai. Aaj ka number chhota hai, par phir bhi bahut bada: UNICEF India ke mutabik 15 se 19 saal ki lagbhag 16% ladkiyan is waqt married hain [[unicef-india-end-child-marriage]], yaani lagbhag har chhathi ladki.

UNICEF child marriage ko do nuksaanon se jodta hai jo saath-saath chalte hain: 18 se pehle shaadi hone wali ladkiyon ke saath domestic violence ke chances zyada hote hain, aur school mein tike rehne ke chances kam [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Jab ladki school chhodti hai, toh woh sasural ke bahar ki woh akeli jagah kho deti hai jahan family se bahar ka koi adult use roz dekhta hai, aur shayad koi chot, koi chuppi ya koi khaali seat notice kar leta.

## Violence jaldi shuru hoti hai

India ka main survey yeh nahi bata sakta ki 18 se kam umar ki kitni wives ke saath violence ho rahi hai: NFHS-5 (2019-21) pati ki violence ka data sirf 18 se 49 saal ki auraton ke liye deta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]], isliye 15, 16 ya 17 saal ki wives isme hain hi nahi. Sabse kareeb ka paimana global hai. World Health Organization ka estimate hai ki duniya bhar mein 15 se 19 saal ki jo ladkiyan kabhi married ya partnered rahi hain, unmein se 23.3% partner ki physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki hain, aur 16.0% ne pichhle 12 mahino mein hi jheli [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Indian data yeh zaroor dikhata hai ki violence kab shuru hoti hai. NFHS-5 mein jo auratein is waqt married thin aur jinki shaadi sirf ek baar hui thi, unmein se 11.2% ne shaadi ke do saal ke andar pati ki physical ya sexual violence jheli, aur 20.9% ne paanch saal ke andar [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jis ladki ki shaadi 16 mein hui, uske liye yeh pehle do saal uske 18 ki hone se pehle hi khatam ho jaate hain.

Kaagaz par law saaf hai. Supreme Court ke 2017 ke *Independent Thought v. Union of India* judgment ke baad se, 18 se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita bhi yahi line rakhti hai: uska marital exception sirf 18 ya usse zyada umar ki wives par lagta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Shaadi se 16 saal ki ladki ki consent possible nahi ho jaati. Bas crime dikhna mushkil ho jaata hai.

## Bina choice ki pregnancy: 17.8% unmet need

NFHS-5 mein 15 se 19 saal ki currently married ladkiyon mein se sirf 28.1% koi bhi contraception use kar rahi thin, aur 17.8% ki family planning ki unmet need thi: woh pregnancy ko taalna ya rokna chahti thin, par kuch bhi use nahi kar rahi thin [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sabhi married auraton mein unmet need 9.4% thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani sabse kam umar ki wives ke paas woh protection na hone ke chances lagbhag do guna hain jo woh khud chahti hain.

Unmet need us gap ko naapti hai jo ek aurat ki chahat aur uske bas ki baat ke beech hota hai. Ek teenage dulhan ke liye yeh gap bharne ka matlab hai ek aise pati se poochna jo shayad usse kai saal bada ho, ek saas se jo pote-poti ka intezaar kar rahi ho, ya ek health worker se jo poori family ko jaanta ho. Bahut si ladkiyon ko yeh mauka hi nahi milta: NFHS-5 mein 19 saal ki umar tak 20.0% young women childbearing shuru kar chuki thin, yaani maa ban chuki thin ya pehle bachche se pregnant thin [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Child bride shayad hi report kyun karti hai

Adult auratein bhi ghar ki violence ki report kam hi karti hain. NFHS-5 mein, physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 18 se 49 saal ki auraton mein se 77.2% ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya, aur jinhe sirf unke maujooda pati ne abuse kiya, unmein se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi madad maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

16 saal ki wife ke paas woh sab kuch aur bhi kam hota hai jo report karna possible banata hai. Ek hypothetical sochiye: usne Class 9 ke baad school chhod diya, uske paas apna koi paisa nahi, aur woh pati ka phone use karti hai. Shaadi uske maa-baap ne tay ki aur uska kharcha uthaya. Abuse report karne ka matlab hai apne pati par crime ka ilzaam lagana. Shaadi report karne ka matlab hai apne hi maa-baap ko phansana, kyunki law har us insaan ko saza deta hai jo child marriage karwata hai ya usme madad karta hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]].

System uske paas pehle shayad hi pahunchta hai. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke under 1,499 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], us desh mein jahan UNICEF India ke estimate ke hisaab se har saal kam se kam 1.5 million ladkiyon ki shaadi hoti hai. Usi saal courts ne aise 209 cases mein conviction diya aur 625 mein acquittal [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Bahar ka raasta: annulment, 1098 aur ek bharosemand adult

Raaste hain, aur timing tay karti hai ki kaunsa kaam karega. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

**Shaadi se pehle.** Child Helpline 1098 emergency number 112 se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne states se kaha ki har district mein Child Marriage Prohibition Officers appoint karein jinke paas koi aur duty na ho, aur magistrates se kaha ki woh khud se injunction jaari karein, khaas kar mass weddings wale "shubh dinon" ke aas-paas [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

**Shaadi ke baad.** Child marriage us insaan ki choice par "voidable" hai jo shaadi ke waqt bachcha tha: woh 18 ki hone ke do saal baad tak district court mein petition daal kar shaadi annul karwa sakti hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Agar use behla-phusla kar le jaaya gaya, zabardasti ya dhokhe se shaadi karwayi gayi, ya shaadi ke liye becha gaya, toh shaadi shuru se hi void hai.

**Jab tak woh 18 se kam hai.** POCSO Act ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke under, jo bhi jaanta hai ya shak karta hai ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse ho raha hai, use police ko report karna hi hoga [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]], aur shaadi se 16 saal ki ladki adult nahi ban jaati. Teacher kisi married student se secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakti, par yeh promise kar sakti hai ki aage jo bhi hoga, usme use akela nahi chhodegi.

**Kisi bhi umar mein.** One Stop Centres violence jhel rahi auraton ki madad karte hain: July 2026 tak 985 centres chal rahe the, aur 2015 se ab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

Child marriage ko aaj bhi ladki ko "safe" rakhne ka tareeka bataya jaata hai. Evidence kuch aur kehta hai, aur law use bahar ka raasta deta hai, agar koi use waqt par bata de.

cruelty-by-husband-largest-crime-categor.en:
Take every crime against women that Indian police registered in 2024 and sort the list from largest to smallest. The top line is not rape, stalking or kidnapping. It is cruelty by a husband or his relatives: 1,20,227 cases, 27.2% of the 4,41,534 crimes against women recorded that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. On India's own police record, the crime registered most often against women happens inside marriage, at the hands of a husband or his family.

## 27.2%: the largest single category

Here are the four largest categories, with rape for comparison [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]:

| Crime head, 2024 | Cases | Share of crimes against women |
|---|---|---|
| Cruelty by husband or relatives | 1,20,227 | 27.2% |
| Kidnapping and abduction of women | 67,829 | 15.4% |
| POCSO cases with girl victims | 67,809 | 15.4% |
| Assault on women with intent to outrage modesty | 48,303 | 10.9% |
| Rape | 29,536 | 6.7% |

Cruelty cases outnumber assaults on women's modesty, the legal category for molestation, by nearly two and a half times [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and rape cases by about four times. Public debate about women's safety tends to focus on streets, buses and strangers. The police register points somewhere else: to homes, kitchens and in-laws' houses.

## 2020 to 2024: up to 1,40,019, then down

Registered cases climbed from 1,11,549 in 2020 to 1,36,234 in 2021 and 1,40,019 in 2022, when they made up 31.4% of crimes against women [[ncrb-cii-2022]]. They then fell to 1,33,676 in 2023 (29.8%) [[ncrb-cii-2023]] and 1,20,227 in 2024 (27.2%) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the last of those years, all crimes against women fell only 1.5%, from 4,48,211 to 4,41,534 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Cruelty cases fell much faster, by about a tenth.

Does that mean homes became safer? The data cannot say so. A registered case measures a woman who reached a police station and an officer who wrote it down, not the cruelty itself. India's health survey shows how rarely that happens: 77.2% of women who faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone, and of those who did seek help, only 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

2024 was also a changeover year. Offences committed before 1 July were registered under Section 498A of the old Indian Penal Code, later ones under Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and NCRB added the two together [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Our guide to reading India's first crime data under the BNS explains why a year like that needs care.

## Where cases are filed: UP, West Bengal, Telangana

Uttar Pradesh (21,266) and West Bengal (19,330) registered the most cases in 2024. Measured against the number of women, the picture changes. Telangana had the highest rate, 52.8 cases per lakh women, followed by Delhi at 45.3, against a national rate of 17.6. By contrast, Bihar's rate was 3.0 and Tamil Nadu's 2.2 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

NCRB itself warns that states should not be compared purely on crime figures, because higher numbers can reflect better registration. The survey data show why. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 40.1% of ever-married women aged 18-49 in Bihar and 38.1% in Tamil Nadu reported physical or sexual violence by their husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A low cruelty rate there is not a sign of gentle homes. More likely, the violence is not reaching the police.

## The principal-offence rule: when cruelty vanishes from the count

NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence. Its methodology calls this the "principal offence rule" [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. So an FIR that includes both cruelty and a dowry death is counted only as a dowry death.

That matters because, by law, a dowry death starts with cruelty or harassment. Section 80 of the BNS defines it as a woman's death by burns, bodily injury or other abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, after dowry-linked cruelty or harassment [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In 2024 police registered 5,737 such cases, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Each of those cases alleges dowry-linked cruelty or harassment before a death, and none of them appear in the 1,20,227. Our story on dowry deaths looks at those women; the point here is what their cases do to this count. The same logic applies whenever a heavier charge sits in the same FIR. The cruelty figure is a floor, not a ceiling.

## What Section 85 covers
