Section 85 BNS, which replaced Section 498A IPC, punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty with up to three years in prison and a fine. Section 86 defines cruelty in two ways: wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause her grave injury, or harassment to force her or her family to meet unlawful demands for property [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Dowry demands sit in the second part. The first is wider than many people think: it turns on what the conduct is likely to do to her, not only on visible injuries.

A woman does not have to choose only the criminal route. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is mainly a civil law, under which a court can order protection, residence and maintenance. Breaking a protection order is itself an offence, punishable with up to a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

If this is happening to you, keep a private record of dates, messages, medical visits and money demanded, and tell one person you trust. In danger, call 112. If you are struggling to cope or having thoughts of suicide, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and open round the clock. The law calls this a crime, and the numbers say you are far from alone.
cruelty-by-husband-largest-crime-categor.hg:
2024 mein Indian police ne women ke khilaaf jitne crimes register kiye, unki list bana kar bade se chhote tak sort kijiye. Sabse upar rape, stalking ya kidnapping nahi hai. Sabse upar hai pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty: 1,20,227 cases, yaani us saal women ke khilaaf register hue 4,41,534 crimes ka 27.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. India ke apne police record ke hisaab se, women ke khilaaf sabse zyada register hone wala crime shaadi ke andar hota hai, pati ya uske parivaar ke haathon.

## 27.2%: sabse badi single category

Yeh rahin chaar sabse badi categories, aur comparison ke liye rape [[ncrb-cii-2024-snapshots]]:

| Crime head, 2024 | Cases | Women ke khilaaf crimes mein share |
|---|---|---|
| Pati ya relatives ki cruelty | 1,20,227 | 27.2% |
| Women ka kidnapping aur abduction | 67,829 | 15.4% |
| Girl victims wale POCSO cases | 67,809 | 15.4% |
| Modesty bhang karne ke iraade se assault | 48,303 | 10.9% |
| Rape | 29,536 | 6.7% |

Cruelty ke cases molestation, yaani women ki modesty par assault, ke cases se lagbhag dhai guna hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur rape ke cases se lagbhag chaar guna. Women ki safety par debate aksar sadak, bus aur strangers par atak jaati hai. Police register kahin aur ishaara karta hai: ghar, kitchen aur sasural ki taraf.

## 2020 se 2024: 1,40,019 tak chadhe, phir gire

Registered cases 2020 mein 1,11,549 the, 2021 mein 1,36,234 aur 2022 mein 1,40,019, jab yeh women ke khilaaf crimes ka 31.4% the [[ncrb-cii-2022]]. Phir 2023 mein ghatkar 1,33,676 (29.8%) [[ncrb-cii-2023]] aur 2024 mein 1,20,227 (27.2%) reh gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 mein women ke khilaaf kul crimes sirf 1.5% ghate, 4,48,211 se 4,41,534 par aaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin cruelty ke cases kaafi tezi se ghate: lagbhag har das mein se ek case kam hua.

Kya iska matlab hai ki ghar zyada safe ho gaye? Data yeh nahi kehta. Registered case sirf yeh batata hai ki ek aurat police station tak pahunchi aur ek officer ne case likha. Yeh cruelty ki asli ginti nahi hai. India ka health survey dikhata hai ki aisa kitna kam hota hai: physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% women ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya, aur jinhone help maangi unmein se bhi sirf 6.3% police ke paas gayin [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

2024 changeover ka saal bhi tha. 1 July se pehle hue crimes purane Indian Penal Code ke Section 498A mein register hue, uske baad wale Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 85 mein, aur NCRB ne dono ko jod kar gina hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. BNS ke under aaye pehle crime data ko padhne par hamari guide batati hai ki aise saal ke numbers dhyan se kyun padhne chahiye.

## Cases kahan register hote hain: UP, West Bengal, Telangana

2024 mein sabse zyada cases Uttar Pradesh (21,266) aur West Bengal (19,330) mein register hue. Lekin women ki population ke hisaab se dekhein toh picture badal jaati hai. Sabse zyada rate Telangana mein tha, 52.8 cases per lakh women, uske baad Delhi, 45.3. Poore desh ka rate 17.6 tha. Iske ulat, Bihar ka rate 3.0 aur Tamil Nadu ka 2.2 tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

NCRB khud warn karta hai ki states ko sirf crime figures se compare nahi karna chahiye, kyunki zyada numbers ka matlab behtar registration bhi ho sakta hai. Survey data dikhata hai kyun. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein Bihar ki 40.1% aur Tamil Nadu ki 38.1% ever-married women (18-49 saal) ne pati ki physical ya sexual violence report ki [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Wahan cruelty ka kam rate shaant gharon ka sign nahi hai. Zyada chance yeh hai ki violence police tak pahunch hi nahi rahi.

## Principal offence rule: jab cruelty ginti se gayab ho jaati hai

NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam par. Iski methodology ise "principal offence rule" kehti hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Toh agar ek FIR mein cruelty aur dowry death dono hain, toh woh sirf dowry death mein gini jaayegi.

Yeh isliye important hai kyunki law ke hisaab se dowry death ki shuruaat hi cruelty ya harassment se hoti hai. BNS ka Section 80 kehta hai ki shaadi ke saat saal ke andar agar kisi aurat ki maut jalne, chot ya kisi abnormal halaat mein ho, aur usse pehle uske saath dowry ke liye cruelty ya harassment hui ho, toh yeh dowry death hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2024 mein police ne aise 5,737 cases register kiye, yaani roz lagbhag 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In sab cases mein maut se pehle dowry ke liye cruelty ya harassment ka allegation hai, phir bhi inmein se ek bhi case 1,20,227 mein shaamil nahi hai. Dowry deaths par hamari story un women ki baat karti hai; yahan point yeh hai ki unke cases is ginti par kya asar daalte hain. Jab bhi kisi FIR mein isse bhaari charge judta hai, yahi hota hai. Isliye cruelty ka figure minimum hai, maximum nahi.

## Section 85 mein kya aata hai

BNS ka Section 85, IPC ke Section 498A ki jagah aaya hai. Agar pati ya uska koi relative aurat ke saath cruelty kare, toh teen saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai. Section 86 cruelty ko do tarah se define karta hai: jaan-boojhkar aisa behaviour jo aurat ko suicide ki taraf dhakel sakta ho ya use gambhir nuksaan pahuncha sakta ho, ya use ya uske parivaar ko property ki gair-kaanooni maang poori karne ke liye harass karna [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Dowry ki maang doosre hisse mein aati hai. Pehla hissa logon ki soch se bada hai: ismein dekha jaata hai ki behaviour ka aurat par kya asar ho sakta hai, sirf yeh nahi ki body par chot dikhti hai ya nahi.

Aurat ke paas sirf criminal case ka raasta nahi hai. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 zyada tar ek civil law hai, jismein court protection, residence aur maintenance ka order de sakti hai. Protection order todna apne aap mein offence hai, jismein ek saal tak ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Agar yeh aapke saath ho raha hai, toh dates, messages, doctor visits aur maange gaye paison ka private record rakhiye, aur ek bharosemand insaan ko bataiye. Khatra ho toh 112 par call karein. Agar sab sambhaalna mushkil lag raha hai ya suicide ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye. Yeh free hai aur din-raat khula hai. Law ise crime maanta hai, aur numbers bataate hain ki aap akeli nahi hain.

cruelty-complaint-14-day-enquiry-bnss.en:
Imagine a 27-year-old in Bhopal who walks into a police station with a written complaint: months of money demands from her husband's family, threats to send her back to her parents, and a beating she can no longer hide. The officer reads it and says: "This is a family matter. We will enquire first. Come back in two weeks."

Since 1 July 2024, part of that answer can be lawful. Here is what the law now allows, where it stops, and how to use the wait. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The new 14-day window

When the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the old codes on 1 July 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], the BNSS wrote in a waiting period. Under Section 173(3), for a cognizable offence punishable with three years or more but less than seven, the officer in charge may, with prior permission from an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days to see whether there is a prima facie case [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Every condition matters: the offence must fall in that band, a Deputy Superintendent must approve before the enquiry starts, the officer must weigh the nature and gravity of the offence, and the enquiry cannot run past 14 days. The word is also "may": an officer can register the FIR at once.

## Why cruelty falls inside it and rape does not

Section 85 of the BNS punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty with up to three years in prison and a fine. Section 86 defines cruelty to include wilful conduct likely to cause her grave injury, and harassment to force her or her family to meet unlawful demands for property or money. Together they replaced Section 498A of the IPC [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

A maximum of three years puts cruelty inside the enquiry band [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape sits outside it: under Section 64 of the BNS it carries at least ten years, so a rape complaint must be registered when it is made [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

For a wife, marriage can decide which side of that line she lands on. Under Exception 2 to Section 63 of the BNS, sex forced on a wife aged 18 or older by her husband is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; a challenge is listed for final hearing in the Supreme Court [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. In December 2024 the Union government told the Rajya Sabha it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape, pointing instead to the Domestic Violence Act and to BNS sections including Section 85, cruelty [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]].

> The complaint the law will not call rape is steered towards offences that can wait.

## The FIR penalty that leaves cruelty out

Under Section 199 of the BNS, a public servant who fails to record information about rape, sexual assault, acid attack or trafficking faces six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Cruelty is not on that list. An officer who refuses a cruelty complaint outside Section 173(3) still breaks the law, but he risks no such penalty.

That gap covers India's most common crime against women. Police registered 1,20,227 cruelty cases in 2024, 27.2% of the 4,41,534 crimes against women recorded that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Those tables count FIRs, so a complaint parked in an enquiry that never becomes one leaves no trace. Registered cruelty cases fell from 1,33,676 in 2023 to 1,20,227 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. NCRB itself warns that registered crime and actual crime are different things [[ncrb-cii-2024]]; these tables cannot say whether the fall means less cruelty, fewer complaints, or more complaints stalled at the desk.

## Zero FIR and e-FIR during the enquiry

Two BNSS rules still work for her. Under Section 173(1), anyone can report a cognizable offence at any police station, wherever it happened (a Zero FIR), or send it electronically, to be taken on record once she signs it within three days (an e-FIR). She must get a copy of the FIR free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Neither route switches the enquiry window off; that depends on the offence, not the door. What they give her is a record: an emailed or online complaint carries its own date and time. And a woman who has gone back to her parents' town can complain there.

## What to do and record in those 14 days

- **Put it in writing.** Hand in a signed, dated complaint and ask for a stamped receiving copy. If the station will not even accept it, our guide to refused FIRs sets out the escalation ladder.
- **Ask three questions, and note the answers.** Is a preliminary enquiry being held under Section 173(3)? Which officer of Deputy Superintendent rank approved it, and on what date? When do the 14 days end? Without that prior permission there is no lawful enquiry, and the complaint should be recorded.
- **Count the days.** When they end, go back or write to the station and ask for the FIR, or for the enquiry's result in writing.
- **Build a record.** Note each incident, threat and demand with its date; keep messages, voice notes, bank transfers to his family, medical papers and the names of anyone who saw or heard. Store copies with someone you trust.
- **Do not wait on the FIR for safety.** In danger, call 112 [[mha-erss]]. A protection, residence or maintenance order under the 2005 Domestic Violence Act comes from a magistrate, not the FIR [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. A One Stop Centre can help with police, legal aid and a short stay [[wcd-mission-shakti]], and the District Legal Services Authority gives free legal aid [[nalsa]].

For the woman at the desk, the window can mean two more weeks in the same house. Knowing exactly what Section 173(3) allows, and what it does not, is how she stops two weeks from becoming never.
cruelty-complaint-14-day-enquiry-bnss.hg:
Sochiye Bhopal ki ek 27 saal ki ladki ek likhi hui complaint lekar police station pahunchti hai: mahinon se sasural ki taraf se paison ki demands, use maayke waapas bhej dene ki dhamkiyan, aur ek maar-peet jo ab woh chhupa nahi sakti. Officer complaint padhta hai aur kehta hai: "Yeh family matter hai. Pehle enquiry karenge. Do hafte baad aana."

1 July 2024 se is jawab ka ek hissa legal ho sakta hai. Yeh raha ki law ab kya allow karta hai, kahan ruk jaata hai, aur intezaar ke is waqt ka istemaal kaise karein. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Naya 14-day window

Jab 1 July 2024 ko Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) aur Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne purane codes ki jagah li [[ncrb-cii-2024]], toh BNSS ne ek waiting period likh diya. Section 173(3) ke under, aise cognizable offence ke liye jiski saza teen saal ya usse zyada lekin saat saal se kam ho, officer in charge, kam se kam Deputy Superintendent of Police rank ke officer ki pehle se permission lekar, 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakta hai, yeh dekhne ke liye ki prima facie case banta hai ya nahi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Har shart maayne rakhti hai: offence us band mein hona chahiye, enquiry shuru hone se pehle Deputy Superintendent ka approval chahiye, officer ko offence ki nature aur gravity tolni hogi, aur enquiry 14 din se aage nahi chal sakti. Aur law ka shabd hai "may", yaani "kar sakta hai": officer chahe toh FIR turant register kar sakta hai.

## Cruelty iske andar kyun aati hai aur rape kyun nahi

BNS ka Section 85 us husband ya uske relative ko, jo woman ke saath cruelty kare, teen saal tak ki jail aur fine ki saza deta hai. Section 86 cruelty mein jaan-boojh kar kiya gaya aisa bartaav shaamil karta hai jisse use gambhir chot lag sakti ho, aur aisa harassment jo use ya uski family ko property ya paison ki gair-kaanooni demand poori karne ke liye majboor kare. Dono milkar IPC ke Section 498A ki jagah aaye hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Zyada se zyada teen saal ki saza cruelty ko enquiry band ke andar rakh deti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape iske bahar hai: BNS ke Section 64 ke under iski saza kam se kam das saal hai, isliye rape ki complaint usi waqt register honi chahiye jab woh ki jaaye [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Ek wife ke liye, shaadi yeh tay kar sakti hai ki woh is line ke kis taraf khadi hogi. BNS ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke under, 18 saal ya usse badi wife ke saath husband ka zabardasti sex rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; is exception ke khilaaf challenge Supreme Court mein final hearing ke liye listed hai [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. December 2024 mein Union government ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki marital rape ko crime banane ka uska koi proposal nahi hai, aur iske badle Domestic Violence Act aur BNS ke kuch sections ki taraf ishaara kiya, jinme Section 85, yaani cruelty, bhi shaamil hai [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]].

> Jise law rape kehne ko taiyaar nahi, woh complaint un offences ki taraf dhakel di jaati hai jo intezaar kar sakte hain.

## FIR wali saza jisme cruelty shaamil nahi

BNS ke Section 199 ke under, jo public servant rape, sexual assault, acid attack ya trafficking ki information record nahi karta, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Cruelty is list mein nahi hai. Jo officer Section 173(3) ka process follow kiye bina cruelty complaint thukraata hai, woh phir bhi law tod raha hai, lekin use aisi kisi saza ka khatra nahi.

Yeh gap India mein women ke khilaaf sabse common crime ko cover karta hai. 2024 mein police ne cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye, jo us saal women ke khilaaf darj 4,41,534 crimes ka 27.2% the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh tables FIRs ginti hain, isliye jo complaint enquiry mein atki rehti hai aur kabhi FIR nahi banti, uska koi nishaan nahi bachta. Register hue cruelty cases 2023 ke 1,33,676 se ghat kar 2024 mein 1,20,227 ho gaye [[ncrb-cii-2023]]. NCRB khud chetaavni deta hai ki register hua crime aur asal crime do alag cheezein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]; yeh tables nahi bata sakte ki yeh girawat kam cruelty ki wajah se hai, kam complaints ki wajah se, ya isliye ki zyada complaints desk pe hi atak gayi.

## Enquiry ke dauraan Zero FIR aur e-FIR

BNSS ke do rules ab bhi uske kaam aate hain. Section 173(1) ke under koi bhi kisi cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi police station mein kar sakta hai, chahe offence kahin bhi hua ho (Zero FIR), ya use electronically bhej sakta hai, jo tab record pe li jaati hai jab woh teen din ke andar us pe sign kar de (e-FIR). FIR ki copy use free mein milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Inme se koi bhi raasta enquiry window ko band nahi karta; woh offence pe depend karta hai, darwaaze pe nahi. Inse use milta hai ek record: email ya online bheji gayi complaint pe uski apni date aur time hota hai. Aur jo woman apne maayke ke shehar laut aayi hai, woh wahin complaint kar sakti hai.

## Un 14 dinon mein kya karein aur kya record karein

- **Sab kuch likhit mein.** Sign aur date ke saath complaint dijiye aur stamp lagi receiving copy maangiye. Agar station complaint lene se hi mana kar de, toh refused FIRs pe hamari guide mein escalation ki poori seedhi di gayi hai.
- **Teen sawaal poochiye aur jawab note kijiye.** Kya Section 173(3) ke under preliminary enquiry ho rahi hai? Deputy Superintendent rank ke kis officer ne ise approve kiya, aur kis date ko? 14 din kab khatam honge? Agar pehle se permission nahi hai, toh koi legal enquiry nahi hai, aur complaint record honi chahiye.
- **Din giniye.** Jab 14 din khatam hon, station waapas jaiye ya likh kar FIR maangiye, ya enquiry ka result likhit mein maangiye.
- **Record banaiye.** Har incident, dhamki aur demand ko date ke saath likhiye; messages, voice notes, uski family ko gaye bank transfers, medical papers aur dekhne ya sunne walon ke naam sambhaal ke rakhiye. Copies kisi trusted insaan ke paas rakhiye.
- **Safety ke liye FIR ka intezaar mat kijiye.** Khatra ho toh 112 pe call kijiye [[mha-erss]]. 2005 ke Domestic Violence Act ke under protection, residence ya maintenance order magistrate deta hai, FIR nahi [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. One Stop Centre police, legal aid aur kuch din rukne ki jagah mein madad kar sakta hai [[wcd-mission-shakti]], aur District Legal Services Authority free legal aid deti hai [[nalsa]].

Desk pe khadi woman ke liye yeh window usi ghar mein do hafte aur bitaane ka matlab ho sakti hai. Section 173(3) asal mein kya allow karta hai aur kya nahi, yeh theek se jaanna hi woh tareeka hai jisse do hafte "kabhi nahi" mein na badlein.

disabled-women-abuse-at-home.en:
Imagine a 30-year-old deaf woman in a small town who uses home signs only her family understands. Her brother collects her disability pension. Her sister-in-law bathes her. At the doctor's, the bank and the ration shop, everyone talks to them, not to her. When her brother hits her, the people who would have to notice, translate or report it are the people in the room.

Violence at home is hard to report for any woman. For a disabled woman who depends on her family for food, medicine, movement or words, the person she would report is often the person she would need in order to report.

## 'Beaten at home': the Odisha survey

In 2018, Human Rights Watch (HRW) found no national data on violence against women and girls with disabilities in India: neither the National Family Health Survey nor the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) broke its figures down by disability [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. So HRW cited a 2004 survey of 729 respondents across 12 districts of Odisha. Nearly all the disabled women and girls it surveyed had been beaten at home, and 25% of women with intellectual disabilities had been raped [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

The survey is old, covers one state, and reached HRW second-hand. That is part of the finding: fourteen years on, it was still what a major human-rights report had to cite. And the place it names is not a dark road. It is home.

## When the abuser is the caregiver

The abuser can be a husband, but also a parent, a brother, a sister-in-law or a paid carer: whoever bathes her, lifts her, handles her money or speaks for her. Dependence shapes the abuse. It can look like food or medicine withheld, a wheelchair, hearing aid or phone taken away, a locked door, a pension spent by someone else, or a pregnancy decided for her.

Dependence also shapes the silence. To report, she may need the abuser's help to travel, to dial a number or to be understood. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes notes that women whose disabilities affect how they communicate are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. When the interpreter is the abuser, the complaint never leaves the house.

## Section 92: crimes written for the home

The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 has offences that read like a description of abuse by family. Under Section 92(d), anyone in a position to dominate the will of a disabled woman or child who uses that position to exploit her sexually faces six months to five years in prison and a fine [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. "A position to dominate the will" describes a carer, a guardian or a relative she depends on.

Under Section 92(f), anyone who performs or directs a procedure that ends a disabled woman's pregnancy without her express consent faces the same punishment. The one exception is a severe case of disability, with a registered doctor's opinion and the guardian's consent [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. That exception hands her choice to a guardian, who may be the very relative she needs protection from. Our explainer on abortion law and disability covers her rights.

Clause (d) is limited to women and children, but Section 92 is wider: clause (b), for example, punishes assaulting or using force on any disabled person with intent to dishonour them, so disabled men and boys are covered too [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Rape of a disabled woman is charged separately, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), as aggravated rape with at least ten years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## 56 cases, and no disability column

In 2024, the first year NCRB counted this law, police across India registered 56 cases under the entire RPwD Act, for every offence in it [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The 2011 Census counted 26.8 million disabled people, 2.21% of the population, against a WHO-World Bank global estimate of 15% [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. Whichever figure is closer to the truth, 56 cases measures how rarely this law reaches a police station, not how often disabled women are abused.

The rest of the data cannot see her. Beyond this law, NCRB records disability in one place, the aggravated rape clause, under which police recorded 144 of 29,536 rape cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For other crimes it does not record whether the victim was disabled. A disabled woman beaten by her brother, or harassed for dowry by her in-laws, enters the tables, if at all, as one more case of hurt or cruelty. A problem nobody counts is a problem nobody is asked to reduce.

## Making a complaint possible: police must come to her

The law already accepts that she may not be able to reach a police station. Under Section 179(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), police investigating a case cannot require a woman or a mentally or physically disabled person to come anywhere other than where she lives, though she may choose to go to the station [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. For a sexual offence, Section 173(1) goes further: her complaint must be recorded at her home or a place of her choice, with an interpreter or special educator, on video [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. When the abuser lives at home, "a place of her choice" matters.

The complaint need not come from her family: anyone can report a cognizable offence to the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. And the 2005 Domestic Violence Act offers a civil route that does not wait for a criminal case: protection, residence and maintenance orders, with a Protection Officer whose failure to do his duty is itself an offence [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

If you are a neighbour, teacher, health worker or relative, speak to her directly, in her language or in sign, away from the person who controls her care. If she is in danger, call 112 [[mha-erss]].
disabled-women-abuse-at-home.hg:
Ek chhote shehar ki 30 saal ki deaf woman ke baare mein sochiye, jo ghar ke aise signs se baat karti hai jo sirf uski family samajhti hai. Uski disability pension uska bhai uthata hai. Uski bhabhi use nehlati hai. Doctor ke paas, bank mein aur ration ki dukaan pe sab unse baat karte hain, usse nahi. Jab uska bhai use maarta hai, toh jinhe yeh notice karna hai, translate karna hai ya report karna hai, woh wahi log hain jo us kamre mein maujood hain.

Ghar ki violence report karna kisi bhi woman ke liye mushkil hai. Jo disabled woman khane, dawai, chalne-phirne ya apni baat kehne ke liye family pe nirbhar hai, uske liye aksar jis insaan ki report karni hai, report karne ke liye bhi usi ki zaroorat padti hai.

## 'Ghar mein maar': Odisha ka survey

2018 mein Human Rights Watch (HRW) ko India mein disabled women aur ladkiyon ke khilaaf violence ka koi national data nahi mila: na National Family Health Survey, na National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) apne figures disability ke hisaab se alag karke dikhata tha [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. Isliye HRW ne Odisha ke 12 districts mein 729 logon pe hue 2004 ke ek survey ka hawala diya. Survey mein lagbhag sabhi disabled women aur ladkiyon ko ghar mein maara-peeta gaya tha, aur intellectual disability wali 25% women ka rape hua tha [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

Survey purana hai, ek hi state ka hai, aur HRW tak second-hand pahuncha. Yeh bhi finding ka hissa hai: chaudah saal baad bhi ek bade human rights report ko yahi survey quote karna pada. Aur jis jagah ki yeh survey baat karta hai, woh koi andhera raasta nahi. Woh ghar hai.

## Jab abuser hi caregiver ho

Abuser husband ho sakta hai, lekin maa-baap, bhai, bhabhi ya paid carer bhi: koi bhi jo use nehlata hai, uthata hai, uske paise sambhaalta hai ya uski taraf se bolta hai. Nirbharta abuse ki shakal tay karti hai. Isme khana ya dawai rok dena, wheelchair, hearing aid ya phone chheen lena, darwaaza band kar dena, uski pension pe kisi aur ka kabza, ya uski pregnancy ka faisla uske bina le lena shaamil ho sakta hai.

Nirbharta chuppi ki shakal bhi tay karti hai. Report karne ke liye use kahin jaane, number dial karne ya apni baat samjhane mein abuser ki hi madad chahiye ho sakti hai. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes handbook kehti hai ki jin women ki disability unke communication ko affect karti hai, woh sexual violence ke saamne khaas taur pe vulnerable hoti hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Jab interpreter hi abuser ho, toh complaint ghar se bahar nikalti hi nahi.

## Section 92: ghar ke liye likhe gaye crimes

Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 mein aise offences hain jo family ke abuse ka hi bayaan lagte hain. Section 92(d) ke under, jo koi bhi kisi disabled woman ya child ki marzi pe haavi hone ki position mein hai aur us position ka istemaal uska sexual exploitation karne ke liye karta hai, use chhe mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. "Marzi pe haavi hone ki position" ek carer, guardian ya us relative ka bayaan hai jis pe woh nirbhar hai.

Section 92(f) ke under, jo koi bhi disabled woman ki express consent ke bina uski pregnancy khatam karne wala procedure karta hai ya karwata hai, use wahi saza ho sakti hai. Ek hi exception hai: disability ka severe case, registered doctor ki opinion aur guardian ki consent ke saath [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Yeh exception uska faisla ek guardian ke haath mein de deta hai, jo shayad wahi relative ho jisse use protection chahiye. Abortion law aur disability pe hamara explainer uske rights detail mein batata hai.

Clause (d) sirf women aur children tak seemit hai, lekin Section 92 isse bada hai: jaise clause (b) kisi bhi disabled person pe use bezzat karne ke iraade se hamla karne ya force use karne ki saza deta hai, isliye disabled mard aur ladke bhi cover hote hain [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]]. Disabled woman ka rape alag se Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke under aggravated rape ke roop mein charge hota hai, jisme kam se kam das saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## 56 cases, aur disability ka koi column nahi

2024 mein, jab NCRB ne pehli baar is law ke cases gine, police ne poore India mein poore RPwD Act ke under sirf 56 cases register kiye, uske har offence ko milakar [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2011 Census ne 26.8 million logon ko disabled gina, yaani population ka 2.21%, jabki WHO-World Bank ka global estimate 15% hai [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. Inme se jo bhi figure sach ke zyada kareeb ho, 56 cases yeh dikhate hain ki yeh law kitni kam baar police station tak pahunchta hai, yeh nahi ki disabled women kitna abuse jhelti hain.

Baaki data use dekh hi nahi paata. Is law ke alawa NCRB disability sirf ek jagah record karta hai, aggravated rape wale clause mein, jiske under police ne 2024 mein 29,536 rape cases mein se sirf 144 darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Baaki crimes mein woh yeh record nahi karta ki victim disabled thi ya nahi. Bhai ke haathon pitne wali ya sasural mein dahej ke liye pareshan ki jaane wali disabled woman tables mein, agar pahunchti bhi hai, toh hurt ya cruelty ka bas ek aur case ban kar. Jis problem ko koi ginta nahi, use kam karne ka jawab bhi koi kisi se nahi maangta.

## Complaint mumkin banana: police ko uske paas aana hoga

Law pehle se maanta hai ki ho sakta hai woh police station tak na pahunch paaye. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 179(1) ke under, kisi case ki investigation karne wali police kisi woman ya mentally ya physically disabled person ko uske rehne ki jagah ke alawa kahin aur aane pe majboor nahi kar sakti, haan woh chahe toh khud station ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Sexual offence ke case mein Section 173(1) aur aage jaata hai: uski complaint uske ghar pe ya uski chuni hui jagah pe, interpreter ya special educator ki maujoodgi mein, video pe record honi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jab abuser ghar mein hi rehta ho, toh "uski chuni hui jagah" bahut maayne rakhti hai.

Complaint family se hi aaye, yeh zaroori nahi: koi bhi cognizable offence ki report police ko kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Aur 2005 ka Domestic Violence Act ek civil raasta deta hai jo criminal case ka intezaar nahi karta: protection, residence aur maintenance orders, aur ek Protection Officer jiska apni duty na nibhana khud ek offence hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Agar aap padosi, teacher, health worker ya relative hain, toh usse seedhe baat kijiye, uski bhasha ya sign mein, us insaan se door jo uski care control karta hai. Agar woh khatre mein hai, toh 112 pe call kijiye [[mha-erss]].

domestic-violence-act-616-criminal-cases.en:
In 2024, police across India registered 616 criminal cases under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. Kerala alone registered 496 of them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The same year, police registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives, the single largest category of crimes against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Read as a measure of domestic violence, the first number makes no sense. It was never meant to be one. This explainer sets out what the Act was built to do, why its criminal count is small and lopsided, and what it cannot replace. It is general information, not legal advice.

## A civil law by design

Most laws on violence start with a crime and a punishment. The 2005 Act starts with a woman and a magistrate. It lets her ask a court for orders, and it creates only two offences: breaking a protection order (Section 31), and a Protection Officer failing to do their duty (Section 33). Each carries up to one year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

So a police case under the Act usually means a magistrate had passed an order and someone broke it. That is why the national count stays small: 446 cases in 2020, 507 in 2021, 468 in 2022, 632 in 2023 and 616 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB counts only these police cases, not how many women applied to a magistrate or how many orders were granted [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The Act's main work happens in courtrooms the crime data never see.

## Protection, residence, money: what a magistrate can order

The Act's remedies are civil orders from a magistrate. A protection order tells the abuser to stop the violence. A residence order deals with her right to stay in the home. A maintenance order makes him pay [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. A breach of a protection order, including an interim one, is the offence that turns the case into a police matter [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

That design fits where women actually turn. In NFHS-5, of women who sought help after physical or sexual violence, 60.9% went to their own family and only 6.3% to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For a woman who needs the violence to stop and a roof over her head, an order can matter more than an arrest. Our guide to protection orders explains how to apply.

## Sexual abuse counts as domestic violence

The Act's definition of domestic violence includes sexual abuse: any conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates a woman's dignity [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. A wife forced into sex by her husband can ask a magistrate for protection.

That is where her remedy stops. Under Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), sex forced on a wife aged 18 or older is not rape; if the couple live separately, it is a lesser offence carrying two to seven years, below the ten-year minimum for rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In NFHS-5, 6.3% of ever-married women aged 18 to 49 reported sexual violence by their husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 496 of 616: Kerala and the rest

Kerala registered about four in five of the Act's cases; every other state and union territory together registered 120 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That does not mean Kerala has the most domestic violence. In the provisional NFHS-6 fact sheets for 2023-24, 17.7% of ever-married women in Kerala reported spousal violence, against 36.1% in Bihar and 22.3% nationally [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

The 496 look more like a recording pattern. Kerala's police also registered the most cases of sexual harassment at office premises (89) and in public transport (100) of any state in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB says higher numbers can come from citizen-centric police initiatives, and that comparing states on its data alone "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. The data cannot say whether Kerala's magistrates grant more orders, its women report more breaches, or its police register breaches others turn away. Elsewhere, a broken order that never becomes an FIR looks, in the statistics, exactly like an order that was obeyed.

Even registered cases rarely end. Of 4,017 criminal cases under the Act before courts in 2024, trials were completed in 84 and 22 ended in conviction; 3,912 (97.4%) were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## What the Act cannot replace

In December 2024 the Union government told the Rajya Sabha it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape, pointing instead to the 2005 Act and BNS Sections 74, 75, 76 and 85, on outraging modesty, sexual harassment, disrobing and cruelty [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. In an October 2024 affidavit to the Supreme Court, it had called marital rape "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" and warned that making it rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]].

The Act cannot do that job. It does not punish forced sex; it punishes disobeying a court order, with at most a year in prison [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. It works only after a woman has reached a magistrate and won an order, and outside one state its criminal side barely exists. Cruelty under Section 85 BNS carries up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]], but cruelty is not rape. A three-judge Supreme Court bench posted the marital rape cases for final hearing on 9 September 2026; no verdict had been reported by November 2026 [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

For what it is, the Act deserves far more use. A Protection Officer, a One Stop Centre or the Women Helpline can help you start: 985 One Stop Centres were operating by July 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]], with police, medical and legal help under one roof [[wcd-mission-shakti]], and District Legal Services Authorities give free legal aid [[nalsa]]. What the Act cannot be is a reason to leave rape inside marriage outside the criminal law.
domestic-violence-act-616-criminal-cases.hg:
2024 mein poore India mein police ne Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 ke under 616 criminal cases register kiye. Inme se 496 akele Kerala mein darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal police ne pati ya uske rishtedaron ki cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye, jo auraton ke khilaf crimes ki sabse badi category hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Agar pehle number ko domestic violence ka paimaana maano, toh woh bematlab lagta hai. Woh kabhi paimaana tha hi nahi. Yeh explainer batata hai ki yeh Act kis kaam ke liye bana tha, uske criminal cases itne kam aur itne ek-tarfa kyun hain, aur woh kiski jagah nahi le sakta. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Design se ek civil law

Hinsa ke zyada tar laws ek crime aur ek saza se shuru hote hain. 2005 ka Act ek aurat aur ek magistrate se shuru hota hai. Yeh aurat ko court se orders maangne deta hai, aur sirf do offences banata hai: protection order todna (Section 31), aur Protection Officer ka apni duty na nibhana (Section 33). Dono mein ek saal tak jail, Rs 20,000 tak fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Matlab is Act ke under police case ka aam taur par ek hi matlab hota hai: magistrate ne order diya tha aur kisi ne use tod diya. Isiliye national count chhota rehta hai: 2020 mein 446 cases, 2021 mein 507, 2022 mein 468, 2023 mein 632 aur 2024 mein 616 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB sirf yahi police cases ginta hai, yeh nahi ki kitni auraton ne magistrate ke paas application di ya kitne orders mile [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Act ka asli kaam un courtrooms mein hota hai jo crime data ko kabhi dikhte hi nahi.

## Protection, ghar, paisa: magistrate kya order de sakta hai

Is Act ke remedies magistrate ke civil orders hain. Protection order abuser ko hinsa band karne ko kehta hai. Residence order ghar mein rehne ke uske haq se juda hai. Maintenance order use paisa dene par majboor karta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Protection order, chahe interim hi kyun na ho, todna hi woh offence hai jo case ko police ka maamla bana deta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Yeh design wahan fit baithta hai jahan auratein sach mein madad ke liye jaati hain. NFHS-5 mein, physical ya sexual violence ke baad madad maangne wali auraton mein se 60.9% apni family ke paas gayi aur sirf 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jis aurat ko bas hinsa ka rukna aur sar par chhat chahiye, uske liye ek order arrest se zyada maayne rakh sakta hai. Protection orders par hamari guide batati hai ki apply kaise karein.

## Sexual abuse bhi domestic violence hai

Act ki domestic violence ki definition mein sexual abuse shaamil hai: sexual nature ka koi bhi aisa vyavhaar jo aurat ki dignity ko abuse kare, humiliate kare, neecha dikhaye ya kisi aur tarah thes pahunchaye [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Jis biwi ke saath pati zabardasti sex karta hai, woh magistrate se protection maang sakti hai.

Uski remedy yahin khatam ho jaati hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke under, 18 saal ya usse badi biwi ke saath zabardasti sex rape nahi hai; agar couple alag reh raha hai, toh yeh ek halka offence hai jisme do se saat saal ki saza hai, jo rape ki kam se kam das saal ki saza se neeche hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. NFHS-5 mein 18 se 49 saal ki ever-married auraton mein se 6.3% ne pati ki sexual violence report ki [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 616 mein se 496: Kerala aur baaki desh

Act ke har paanch mein se lagbhag chaar cases Kerala ne register kiye; baaki saare states aur union territories ne milkar 120 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki Kerala mein sabse zyada domestic violence hai. 2023-24 ki provisional NFHS-6 fact sheets mein Kerala ki 17.7% ever-married auraton ne spousal violence report ki, jabki Bihar mein 36.1% aur poore desh mein 22.3% ne [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

496 ka number recording ka pattern zyada lagta hai. 2024 mein office premises par sexual harassment (89) aur public transport mein sexual harassment (100) ke sabse zyada police cases bhi Kerala police ne hi darj kiye, kisi bhi state se zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB kehta hai ki zyada numbers citizen-centric police initiatives ka nateeja ho sakte hain, aur sirf uske data par states ki tulna "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Data yeh nahi bata sakta ki Kerala ke magistrates zyada orders dete hain, wahan ki auratein zyada ullanghan report karti hain, ya wahan ki police woh cases darj karti hai jinhe doosri jagah lauta diya jaata hai. Baaki jagah, ek toota hua order jo kabhi FIR nahi banta, statistics mein bilkul us order jaisa dikhta hai jiska paalan hua.

Jo cases darj hote hain, woh bhi shayad hi khatam hote hain. 2024 mein courts ke saamne Act ke 4,017 criminal cases the; 84 mein trial poora hua aur 22 mein conviction hua; 3,912 (97.4%) saal ke end mein pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Act kiski jagah nahi le sakta

December 2024 mein Union government ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki marital rape ko crime banane ka uska koi proposal nahi hai, aur iski jagah 2005 ke Act aur BNS ke Sections 74, 75, 76 aur 85 ki taraf ishaara kiya, jo modesty bhang karne, sexual harassment, kapde utaarne ke iraade se hamle aur cruelty se jude hain [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. October 2024 ke ek Supreme Court affidavit mein usne marital rape ko "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" kaha tha, aur warning di thi ki ise rape banana "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" ho sakta hai [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]].

Act yeh kaam nahi kar sakta. Woh zabardasti sex ki saza nahi deta; woh court ka order na maanne ki saza deta hai, zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Woh tabhi kaam karta hai jab aurat magistrate tak pahunch kar order le aaye, aur ek state ke bahar uska criminal hissa lagbhag hai hi nahi. Section 85 BNS ke under cruelty mein teen saal tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], lekin cruelty rape nahi hai. Supreme Court ki teen judges ki bench ne 9 September 2026 ko marital rape cases ko final hearing ke liye list kiya; November 2026 tak koi verdict report nahi hua tha [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

Jis kaam ke liye yeh Act bana hai, uske liye iska istemaal kahin zyada hona chahiye. Protection Officer, One Stop Centre ya Women Helpline se shuruaat ho sakti hai: July 2026 tak 985 One Stop Centres chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]], jahan ek hi chhat ke neeche police, medical aur legal madad milti hai [[wcd-mission-shakti]], aur District Legal Services Authorities free legal aid deti hain [[nalsa]]. Yeh Act jo nahi ban sakta, woh hai shaadi ke andar hone wale rape ko criminal law se bahar rakhne ka bahana.

domestic-violence-not-only-villages-myth.en:
"That happens in villages." "Not in educated families." "Not in our society." Most of us have heard it, often in a city flat, sometimes a few walls away from the woman it describes. The newest national survey answers it with a number. In NFHS-6 (2023-24), 17.5% of ever-married women aged 18 to 49 in urban India said a husband had been physically or sexually violent towards them [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. That is more than one in six. In cities, violence by husbands is not absent. It is quieter.

## The myth: it happens in villages

Like most lasting myths, this one starts from something true. Women in rural India report more violence by husbands. In the same survey the rural figure was 24.4%, against 17.5% in cities [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. The previous round, which also counted emotional violence, found the same pattern: 34% of rural women and 27% of urban women [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The rounds measure different things, so this is not a trend, but both point the same way.

The problem is what the myth does with that truth. It turns "less common" into "does not happen here". A gap between nearly one in four and more than one in six is a gap between bad and bad. The "educated families" version fails the same way. In NFHS-5, women whose husbands had 12 or more years of schooling reported physical, sexual or emotional violence by them half as often as women whose husbands had no schooling, 22% against 43% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Half is not zero. And the myth has a cost: it makes a city woman's account sound unlikely to her parents, her neighbours, her colleagues, and sometimes to herself.

## 17.5%: more than one in six

The NFHS-6 figure counts women aged 18 to 49 who have ever married and have ever faced physical or sexual violence from a husband [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. The fact sheets are provisional, and Manipur was not surveyed. They also record only what women were willing to tell a surveyor. Another story in this magazine asks whether the national fall from 29.2% to 22.3% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]] means less violence or less telling.

Consider a hypothetical. A 30-year-old in a Pune high-rise, a commerce graduate who left her job when her son was born. Her husband is polite in the lift and generous at society festivals. He also decides what she spends, reads her messages and has hit her more than once. Nobody hears through the concrete. When she hints at it, her mother says every marriage has fights. Nothing about her life fits the picture most people carry of a beaten wife. That is exactly why nobody asks.

## Delhi's 45.3 and the metro tables

Police records point the same way. In 2024 Delhi registered 45.3 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives for every lakh women, the second-highest rate in India after Telangana's 52.8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Delhi also had the highest rate of registered crime against women of any state or Union Territory, 130.7 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]], as it did in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

India's 19 metropolitan cities, those with more than 20 lakh people at the 2011 Census, registered 50,584 crimes against women in 2024. The highest rates were in Jaipur (199.0 per lakh women), Lucknow (186.0), Indore (181.5) and Delhi (176.8); the lowest in Chennai (25.4) and Kolkata (28.8) [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These tables count every crime against women, not only violence at home. Nationally, though, cruelty by a husband or relatives is the largest single category, 27.2% of all cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Read them with two warnings. NCRB divides city cases by 2011 Census population, so city rates cannot be compared with state rates [[ncrb-cii-2024]]; that is why Delhi shows 130.7 in one table and 176.8 in the other. And NCRB says more crime registered in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Either way, the myth loses. If high city numbers mean more violence, cities are not safe. If they mean more reporting, they show what surfaces when women can reach a police station that listens. A low number proves nothing either: Chennai, the metro with the lowest rate, is the capital of Tamil Nadu, where 28.5% of ever-married women told NFHS-6 a husband had been physically or sexually violent [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## Why urban violence stays hidden

Most violence by husbands is never reported anywhere. In NFHS-5, 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told anyone. Of those who sought help, 60.9% went to their own family and only 6.3% to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Among women hurt only by their current husband, just 11.3% ever sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. These are national figures, but cities add their own locks.

A closed flat, with neighbours who barely know each other's names, can give violence privacy. Status can add pressure: the husband's job, the child's school, the family's name in the building. And money can narrow the exits. In 2023-24 only 28.0% of urban women aged 15 and above were in the labour force, working or looking for work, against 47.6% of rural women [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].

Even public money looks outward. Under the Nirbhaya Fund, Safe City projects in eight cities, including Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Lucknow, aim to make public places safer [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. By July 2026 they had received Rs 1,686.73 crore from the fund, more than the Rs 1,299.10 crore for One Stop Centres, which help women facing violence [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Safer streets matter. But in NFHS-5, 82% of ever-married women who had faced sexual violence named their current husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Truth: no postcode is safe

Violence by husbands is less common in Indian cities than in villages, and still common enough that almost any office floor, school parents' group or housing-society WhatsApp group includes women who have faced it. Safety at home does not come with a pin code, a degree or a salary.

Watchfulness in a city looks the same as anywhere: notice, ask, believe, and know where help is. By July 2026, 985 One Stop Centres were running across India and had helped over 15.20 lakh women since 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Save 112 and the Women Helpline number in your phone. And the next time someone says "not in our society", tell them about the 17.5%.
domestic-violence-not-only-villages-myth.hg:
"Yeh sab gaon mein hota hai." "Padhe-likhe gharon mein nahi." "Hamare yahan nahi." Yeh baat hum sabne suni hai, aksar kisi shehar ke flat mein, kabhi-kabhi usi aurat se bas do deewar door jiske baare mein yeh baat hai. Sabse naye national survey ne iska jawaab ek number mein diya hai. NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein shehron ki 18 se 49 saal ki 17.5% married women (yaani jinki kabhi bhi shaadi hui ho) ne bataya ki pati ne unke saath physical ya sexual violence ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yaani chhe mein se ek se zyada. Shehron mein pati ki violence gayab nahi hai. Bas uski aawaz kam aati hai.

## Myth: yeh toh gaon mein hota hai

Zyadatar purane myths ki tarah, iski jad mein bhi thoda sach hai. Gaon ki auratein pati ki violence zyada report karti hain. Isi survey mein gaon ka number 24.4% tha, aur shehron ka 17.5% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Pichhle round mein, jismein emotional violence bhi gini gayi thi, yahi pattern tha: gaon ki 34% aur shehron ki 27% auraton ne pati ki violence batayi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Dono rounds alag cheezein naapte hain, isliye ise trend mat samjhiye. Par dono ek hi taraf ishaara karte hain.

Problem yeh hai ki myth is sach ke saath kya karta hai. Woh "kam hota hai" ko "yahan hota hi nahi" bana deta hai. Lagbhag chaar mein se ek aur chhe mein se ek se zyada ka farq, bure aur bure ka farq hai. "Padhe-likhe gharon" wali baat bhi isi tarah fail hoti hai. NFHS-5 mein jin auraton ke pati ne 12 saal ya usse zyada padhai ki thi, unhone pati ki physical, sexual ya emotional violence un auraton se aadhi baar batayi jinke pati bilkul nahi padhe the: 22% vs 43% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aadha, zero nahi hota. Aur is myth ki keemat bhi hai. Shehar ki koi aurat apni baat kahe, toh woh kisi ko sach nahi lagti: na parents ko, na padosiyon ko, na colleagues ko, aur kabhi-kabhi khud use bhi nahi.

## 17.5%: chhe mein se ek se zyada

NFHS-6 ka yeh number 18 se 49 saal ki un auraton ko ginta hai jinki kabhi shaadi hui aur jinhone kabhi bhi pati se physical ya sexual violence jheli [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yeh fact sheets abhi provisional hain, final nahi. Manipur mein survey nahi hua. Aur yeh utna hi dikhati hain jitna auraton ne surveyor ko bataya. Is magazine ki ek aur story yahi poochhti hai: India ka number 29.2% se 22.3% par aaya [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], toh kya violence ghati, ya batana ghata?

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Pune ki kisi high-rise mein 30 saal ki ek aurat. Commerce graduate hai, beta hua toh job chhod di. Uska pati lift mein sabse tameez se baat karta hai aur society ke festivals mein khul kar chanda deta hai. Par ghar mein wahi decide karta hai ki woh kitna kharch karegi, uske messages padhta hai, aur ek se zyada baar us par haath utha chuka hai. Concrete ki deewaron ke paar koi aawaz nahi jaati. Woh maa se ishaare mein kuch kehti hai, toh jawaab milta hai: "Jhagde toh har shaadi mein hote hain." Uski zindagi mein kuch bhi waisa nahi jaisi tasveer log "pitne wali biwi" ki banate hain. Isiliye koi poochhta bhi nahi.

## Delhi ka 45.3 aur metros ki tables

Police records bhi yahi kehte hain. 2024 mein Delhi mein har ek lakh auraton par pati ya uske rishtedaron ki cruelty ke 45.3 cases darj hue. Yeh India mein doosra sabse ooncha rate tha, Telangana ke 52.8 ke baad [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Auraton ke khilaaf har tarah ke crime ke rate mein Delhi saare states aur Union Territories mein sabse upar rahi: har ek lakh auraton par 130.7 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2023 mein bhi Delhi hi sabse upar thi [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

India ke 19 metropolitan cities mein, jinki aabadi 2011 Census mein 20 lakh se zyada thi, 2024 mein auraton ke khilaaf 50,584 crimes darj hue. Sabse ooncha rate Jaipur mein tha (har ek lakh auraton par 199.0), phir Lucknow (186.0), Indore (181.5) aur Delhi (176.8). Sabse kam rate Chennai (25.4) aur Kolkata (28.8) mein tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh tables auraton ke khilaaf har crime ginti hain, sirf ghar ki violence nahi. Par poore desh mein sabse bada hissa pati ya rishtedaron ki cruelty ka hi hai: saare cases ka 27.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In numbers ko do warnings ke saath padhiye. Pehli: NCRB shehron ke cases ko 2011 Census ki aabadi se divide karta hai, isliye shehar ke rate ko state ke rate se compare nahi kar sakte [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isiliye Delhi ek table mein 130.7 dikhti hai aur doosri mein 176.8. Doosri: NCRB khud kehta hai ki kisi shehar mein zyada crime darj hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki woh shehar zyada unsafe hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

Dono hi surat mein myth haarta hai. Agar shehar ke oonche numbers ka matlab zyada violence hai, toh shehar safe nahi hain. Agar unka matlab zyada reporting hai, toh woh dikhate hain ki jab auratein aise police station tak pahunchti hain jo unki sunta hai, tab kya saamne aata hai. Aur kam number bhi kuch prove nahi karta. Chennai ka rate sabse kam hai, par Chennai Tamil Nadu ki capital hai, jahan NFHS-6 mein 28.5% married women ne pati ki physical ya sexual violence batayi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## Shehar ki violence chhupi kyun rehti hai

Pati ki zyadatar violence kahin darj hi nahi hoti. NFHS-5 mein jin auraton ne physical ya sexual violence jheli, unmein se 77.2% ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya. Jinhone madad maangi, unmein se 60.9% apni family ke paas gayin, aur police ke paas sirf 6.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jin auraton ko sirf current pati ne hurt kiya tha, unmein se bas 11.3% ne kabhi madad maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh poore desh ke numbers hain, par shehar in par apne taale aur laga dete hain.

Band flat, jahan padosi ek-doosre ka naam tak mushkil se jaante hain, violence ko parda de sakta hai. Phir izzat ka pressure ho sakta hai: pati ki job, bachche ka school, building mein family ka naam. Aur paisa nikalne ke raaste chhote kar sakta hai. 2023-24 mein shehron ki 15 saal aur usse zyada umar ki sirf 28.0% auratein labour force mein thin (yaani kaam kar rahi thin ya kaam dhoondh rahi thin), jabki gaon ki auraton mein yeh number 47.6% tha [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].

Sarkari paisa bhi bahar ki taraf hi dekhta hai. Nirbhaya Fund se aath shehron mein Safe City projects chal rahe hain, jinmein Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai aur Lucknow shaamil hain, aur inka maqsad public jagahon ko safe banana hai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. July 2026 tak inhe is fund se Rs 1,686.73 crore mil chuke the, jabki violence jhel rahi auraton ki madad karne wale One Stop Centres ko isse kam, Rs 1,299.10 crore mile [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Sadkein safe hon, yeh zaroori hai. Par NFHS-5 mein sexual violence jhel chuki married women mein se 82% ne apne current pati ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Sach: koi pin code safe nahi

India ke shehron mein pati ki violence gaon se kam hai, par itni kam bhi nahi ki use ignore kiya jaaye. Lagbhag har office floor, school ke parents group ya society ke WhatsApp group mein aisi auratein hongi jinhone ise jhela hai. Ghar ki safety pin code, degree ya salary ke saath nahi aati.

Shehar mein nazar rakhna bhi waisa hi hai jaisa kahin aur: dhyaan dijiye, poochhiye, bharosa kijiye, aur pata rakhiye ki madad kahan milti hai. July 2026 tak India mein 985 One Stop Centres chal rahe the, aur 2015 se tab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. 112 aur Women Helpline ka number phone mein save kar lijiye. Aur agli baar koi kahe "hamare yahan aisa nahi hota", toh use 17.5% ke baare mein bataiye.

domestic-violence-survey-vs-police-state.en:
Imagine two women, one in Hyderabad and one in Patna, each hit by her husband. The hypothetical is ours; the numbers are not. The woman in Patna lives in the state where the newest national survey found the highest share of ever-married women reporting violence by a husband: 36.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yet in 2024, Bihar's police registered 3.0 cases of cruelty by a husband or relatives for every lakh women, while Telangana's registered 52.8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. If either woman's complaint ever reaches a police register, it is far more likely to be the one in Hyderabad.

## Two maps of the same crime

India measures violence by husbands in two ways. The National Family Health Survey asks women directly. In NFHS-6 (2023-24), 22.3% of ever-married women aged 18 to 49 said a husband had been physically or sexually violent [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) counts something else: complaints that became FIRs for cruelty by a husband or relatives, under Section 85 BNS or the old Section 498A IPC. In 2024 that came to 1,20,227 cases, or 17.6 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

One counts what women tell surveyors. The other counts what police wrote down. Set state against state and the two maps barely resemble each other.

| State | Ever-married women reporting violence by a husband (NFHS-6, 2023-24) | Cruelty cases per lakh women (police, 2024) |
|---|---|---|
| Bihar | 36.1% | 3.0 |
| Telangana | 30.8% | 52.8 |
| Tamil Nadu | 28.5% | 2.2 |
| India | 22.3% | 17.6 |

Survey figures are from the NFHS-6 fact sheets [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]; police rates from Crime in India 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Telangana and Delhi: when high registration can be a good sign

Telangana tops the police map at 52.8 cruelty cases per lakh women, with Delhi second at 45.3 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Read naively, these are India's most violent homes. The survey only partly agrees: Telangana is second on its map, at 30.8%, behind Bihar [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. High on the survey and high in the register is the pattern you would expect where violence is common and women's complaints reach the police.

NCRB itself warns that more crime registered in a place "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Research agrees: when all-women police stations opened in Indian cities, police reports of crimes against women rose 29%, mainly domestic violence, with no change in killings of women [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. Another story in this magazine follows that evidence in detail. The lesson for this map: a high police rate can mean more reporting, not more violence.

A high number is not proof of good policing. An FIR is only the first step. But no woman gets justice from a complaint that was never written down.

## Bihar: dowry gets an FIR, beatings rarely do

Bihar tops the survey map, and its police register tells a different story. More than a third of its ever-married women, 36.1%, told NFHS-6 that a husband had been violent [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Its police registered cruelty at 3.0 cases per lakh women, against 17.6 nationally [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Bihar's police do register crimes against women: 27,359 cases in 2024, up 19.2% in a year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bihar recorded 1,078 dowry deaths and 3,780 cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act, second only to Uttar Pradesh on both counts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The pattern raises a hard question: does the system act mainly when a woman dies or dowry is involved, and not when she is beaten?

Part of the answer is counting. NCRB records each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so an FIR for both dowry death and cruelty appears only as a dowry death [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Some of Bihar's cruelty hides inside its dowry figures. That cannot fully explain why a state where more than a third of ever-married women report violence produces so few cruelty cases.

Tamil Nadu shows the same split. Its registered crimes against women rose 27.1% in 2024, yet its cruelty rate was 2.2 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]], while 28.5% of its ever-married women reported violence in NFHS-6 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## NFHS-5 to NFHS-6: how the ranking moved

One survey round can mislead, so compare two. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), the highest shares of ever-married women reporting physical or sexual violence by a husband were in Karnataka (44.4%), Bihar (40.1%), Manipur (39.6%), Tamil Nadu (38.1%) and Telangana (37.2%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In NFHS-6, Bihar (36.1%), Telangana (30.8%), Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu (28.5% each) lead [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Bihar, Telangana and Tamil Nadu stay near the top in both rounds, and that consistency is what makes their police gaps meaningful. Karnataka is the opposite case: it fell from 44.4% to 14.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], a swing that experts quoted by Deccan Herald doubt [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]] and the subject of a separate investigation in this magazine. Manipur was not surveyed in NFHS-6.

The low end matters too. Nagaland reported 6.5% in NFHS-5 [[nfhs5-india-2021]] and had India's lowest rate of registered crime against women of any kind in 2024, 5.1 per lakh [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When the survey and the register are both low, violence may genuinely be lower. When only the police map is low, as in Bihar and Tamil Nadu, silence, or complaints that never become FIRs, is the likelier explanation.

## Check your own state

It takes about ten minutes.

1. Open your state's NFHS-6 fact sheet and find the line for ever-married women aged 18 to 49 who have ever experienced spousal violence. The national figure is 22.3% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].
2. Open NCRB's Crime in India 2024, Volume I, at Table 3A.2(i). Under "Cruelty by Husband or his relatives", read across your state's row: IPC cases, BNS cases, total, victims and the rate per lakh women. The national rate is 17.6 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
3. Place your state: high on both maps, high on the survey but low in the register, or low on both.
4. Check NFHS-5 as well. If the survey figure swung wildly between rounds, treat both with care.

Then ask the question this map is built for. If women in your state tell surveyors about violence and the police register stays nearly empty, where are their complaints going? Our walkthrough of NCRB's tables shows the same method for rape data.
domestic-violence-survey-vs-police-state.hg:
Sochiye, do auratein hain: ek Hyderabad mein, ek Patna mein. Dono ko unke pati ne maara. Yeh example hamara hai, par numbers asli hain. Patna wali aurat us state mein rehti hai jahan sabse naye national survey mein sabse zyada married women ne pati ki violence ki baat batayi: 36.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Phir bhi 2024 mein Bihar police ne har ek lakh auraton par pati ya rishtedaaron ki cruelty ke sirf 3.0 cases darj kiye, jabki Telangana police ne 52.8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Agar in dono mein se kisi ki complaint police register tak pahunchti hai, toh iske chances kahin zyada Hyderabad wali ke hain.

## Ek hi crime ke do maps

India pati ki violence ko do tarah se naapta hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS) seedhe auraton se poochhta hai. NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 18 se 49 saal ki 22.3% married women (yaani jinki kabhi bhi shaadi hui ho) ne bataya ki pati ne unke saath physical ya sexual violence ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) kuch aur ginta hai: woh complaints jo pati ya rishtedaaron ki cruelty ki FIR bani, BNS ke Section 85 ya purane IPC ke Section 498A ke tahat. 2024 mein aise 1,20,227 cases darj hue, yaani har lakh auraton par 17.6 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ek number batata hai ki auraton ne surveyor ko kya bataya. Doosra batata hai ki police ne kya likha. States ko aamne-saamne rakhiye, toh dono maps ek-doosre se bilkul match nahi karte.

| State | Pati ki violence batane wali married women (NFHS-6, 2023-24) | Har lakh auraton par cruelty cases (police, 2024) |
|---|---|---|
| Bihar | 36.1% | 3.0 |
| Telangana | 30.8% | 52.8 |
| Tamil Nadu | 28.5% | 2.2 |
| India | 22.3% | 17.6 |

Survey ke numbers NFHS-6 ki fact sheets se hain [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], aur police ke numbers Crime in India 2024 se [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Telangana aur Delhi: jab zyada cases darj hona achha sign ho sakta hai

Police ke map mein Telangana sabse upar hai: har lakh auraton par cruelty ke 52.8 cases. Doosre number par Delhi hai, 45.3 ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Upar-upar se dekhein toh lagega ki sabse violent ghar yahin hain. Survey is baat se sirf kuch had tak sahmat hai: uske map mein Telangana doosre number par hai, 30.8% ke saath, aur pehle number par Bihar hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Survey mein bhi upar aur register mein bhi upar: yahi pattern wahan dikhna chahiye jahan violence aam hai aur auraton ki complaint police tak pahunchti hai.

NCRB khud warning deta hai ki kisi jagah zyada crime darj hona "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe", yaani us jagah ke kam safe hone ka sign nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Research bhi yahi kehti hai: Indian shehron mein jab all-women police stations khule, toh auraton ke khilaaf crime ki police reports 29% badh gayin, zyada tar domestic violence ki, jabki auraton ki hatyaon mein koi badlav nahi aaya [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. Hamari ek aur story is research ko detail mein batati hai. Is map ke liye lesson yeh hai: police ki oonchi rate ka matlab zyada violence nahi, zyada reporting bhi ho sakta hai.

Zyada cases ka matlab yeh bhi nahi ki policing achhi hai. FIR sirf pehla kadam hai. Lekin jo complaint kabhi likhi hi nahi gayi, usse kisi aurat ko insaaf nahi milta.

## Bihar: dowry par FIR hoti hai, maar-peet par kam hi

Survey ke map par Bihar sabse upar hai, aur police ka register kuch aur hi kahani batata hai. Wahan ki ek-tihaai se zyada married women ne, yaani 36.1% ne, NFHS-6 ko bataya ki pati ne violence ki [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Lekin wahan ki police ne har lakh auraton par cruelty ke sirf 3.0 cases darj kiye, jabki national average 17.6 hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Aisa nahi hai ki Bihar police auraton ke khilaaf crime darj hi nahi karti: 2024 mein wahan aise 27,359 cases darj hue, ek saal mein 19.2% zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bihar mein dowry death ke 1,078 cases darj hue aur Dowry Prohibition Act ke tahat 3,780 cases, aur dono mein Bihar Uttar Pradesh ke baad doosre number par hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh pattern ek kadwa sawaal uthata hai: kya system tabhi harkat mein aata hai jab kisi aurat ki maut ho jaaye ya dowry ka maamla ho, aur tab nahi jab use peeta jaaye?

Iska ek hissa ginti ka tareeka hai. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious crime ke naam par, isliye jis FIR mein dowry death aur cruelty dono hon, woh sirf dowry death mein gini jaati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Matlab Bihar ki kuch cruelty dowry ke numbers mein chhupi hai. Lekin isse poori baat samajh nahi aati: jis state mein ek-tihaai se zyada married women violence ki baat batati hain, wahan cruelty ke itne kam cases kyun bante hain?

Tamil Nadu mein bhi yahi farq dikhta hai. 2024 mein wahan auraton ke khilaaf darj crime 27.1% badh gaye, phir bhi cruelty ki rate har lakh auraton par sirf 2.2 thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jabki NFHS-6 mein wahan ki 28.5% married women ne pati ki violence ki baat batayi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## NFHS-5 se NFHS-6: ranking kaise badli

Kisi survey ka ek round dhokha de sakta hai, isliye do rounds mila kar dekhiye. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein pati ki physical ya sexual violence batane wali married women sabse zyada Karnataka (44.4%), Bihar (40.1%), Manipur (39.6%), Tamil Nadu (38.1%) aur Telangana (37.2%) mein thin [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. NFHS-6 mein sabse aage Bihar (36.1%), Telangana (30.8%), aur Uttar Pradesh aur Tamil Nadu (dono 28.5%) hain [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Bihar, Telangana aur Tamil Nadu dono rounds mein upar bane rahe, aur isi wajah se inke police wale gap ka matlab banta hai. Karnataka ulta case hai: wahan number 44.4% se gir kar 14.1% ho gaya [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Deccan Herald se baat karne wale experts ko is swing par shak hai [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]], aur is par hamari ek alag investigation hai. Manipur mein toh NFHS-6 hua hi nahi.

Sabse neeche wale states bhi kuch batate hain. NFHS-5 mein Nagaland ka number 6.5% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]], aur 2024 mein auraton ke khilaaf kisi bhi tarah ke darj crime ki sabse kam rate bhi Nagaland mein thi: har lakh par 5.1 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab survey aur register dono mein number kam ho, toh ho sakta hai ki violence sach mein kam ho. Jab sirf police ka number kam ho, jaise Bihar aur Tamil Nadu mein, toh wajah zyada tar chuppi hoti hai, ya aisi complaints jo kabhi FIR nahi ban paatin.

## Apne state ka haal khud check kijiye

Ismein kareeb das minute lagte hain.

1. Apne state ki NFHS-6 fact sheet kholiye aur 18 se 49 saal ki un married women wali line dhoondhiye jinhone kabhi pati ki violence jheli ("ever experienced spousal violence"). National number 22.3% hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].
2. NCRB ki Crime in India 2024, Volume I kholiye aur Table 3A.2(i) par jaiye. "Cruelty by Husband or his relatives" ke neeche apne state ki row padhiye: IPC cases, BNS cases, total, victims aur har lakh auraton par rate. National rate 17.6 hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
3. Ab apne state ko in mein se ek box mein rakhiye: dono maps mein upar; survey mein upar par register mein neeche; ya dono mein neeche.
4. NFHS-5 bhi dekhiye. Agar do rounds ke beech survey ka number bahut zyada uchhla ya gira hai, toh dono ko dhyaan se padhiye.

Phir woh sawaal poochhiye jiske liye yeh map bana hai. Agar aapke state ki auratein survey mein violence ki baat batati hain aur police ka register lagbhag khaali rehta hai, toh unki complaints kahan ja rahi hain? NCRB ki tables padhne par hamari guide yahi tareeka rape ke numbers ke liye samjhati hai.

domestic-workers-harassment-employer-hom.en:
A domestic worker's office has no HR department, no colleagues and often no written contract. It is someone else's home, and the man she would complain about may be the employer, or his son, brother or father. Indian law has had an answer on paper since 2013: the POSH Act counts "a dwelling place or a house" as a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Here is how she can use it, and where the system fails her.

## Behind someone else's door

Consider a woman in her thirties who cooks in four flats in a Delhi housing society. In one of them, a man in the family has started making sexual remarks whenever she is alone in the kitchen. There is no complaints desk down the corridor: the household is her employer. If she objects, she may lose the job, and word may travel to the other three families. It is her word against his.

Harassment in a home happens where nobody else is watching, to women whose income depends on the family they would accuse. The journey adds a second risk. In a Jagori survey of 270 women domestic workers in Delhi-NCR, carried out between May and November 2024, 45% felt very unsafe in the city at night and a further 17% somewhat unsafe, and those earning under Rs 5,000 a month spent about 20% of their income on commuting [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]].

## The law: a home is a workplace

The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (the POSH Act) defines "workplace" widely: offices, but also hospitals, sports venues, transport the employer provides and private homes. It protects "a woman of any age who is employed in such a dwelling place or house" [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

An office complaint goes to the employer's Internal Committee. A house has none, so the complaint goes to a Local Committee, which the District Officer must set up in every district for workplaces with fewer than ten workers or where the complaint is against the employer [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Then the path splits. An office worker's committee holds its own inquiry, to be finished within 90 days [[indiacode-posh-2013]]. A domestic worker's Local Committee must instead forward her complaint to the police within seven days if it finds a prima facie case [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. That becomes a criminal case under what is now Section 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), on words or gestures meant to insult a woman's modesty. Sexual harassment itself carries up to three years under Section 75, or one year for sexually coloured remarks [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. She must complain within three months of the incident, a limit the committee can extend by three more months [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

For a domestic worker, the POSH Act is mainly a route to the police, with a committee as the first stop.

## 512 police cases, and one in four in a Delhi-NCR survey

How often does this happen? Police data cannot say. When the BNS came into force on 1 July 2024, the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) added a category for work premises other than offices: "shops, malls, factories, home etc." It recorded 512 cases there in the second half of 2024, against 388 at office premises over the whole year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Those 512 cases mix homes with shops and factories and cover six months, so nobody can tell how many domestic workers went to the police. They are a small slice of a small total: of 15,609 sexual harassment cases registered in 2024, 12,592, or 81%, were filed under "other places" [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In Jagori's survey, 24% of the 270 women had experienced sexual harassment in the previous two years [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. That figure is not limited to employers' homes, and one region's sample cannot be scaled up to India. But set beside a national police count in the hundreds, it suggests that most harassment of domestic workers never becomes a case.

## Domestic servitude and trafficking

For some women and girls, the house is a trap. Of 5,839 trafficking victims rescued in India in 2024, 105 had been trafficked for domestic servitude, alongside 2,347 for sexual exploitation for prostitution and 1,493 for forced labour [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB does not split these purposes by age.

Trafficking for exploitation carries 7 to 10 years under Section 143 of the BNS, at least 10 for a child, and the victim's consent is irrelevant [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yet courts convicted in just 43 of the 586 trafficking cases whose trials ended in 2024, a rate of 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

From outside, servitude can look like ordinary work. Warning signs: a worker who is never allowed out alone, is not paid, has had her phone or identity papers taken, or says she owes money to the agent who brought her.

## How a domestic worker can complain

- **Go to the Local Committee.** Within three months, give it a written complaint. If it finds a prima facie case, it must forward it to the police within seven days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- **Or go to the police directly.** Sexual harassment is a crime in itself [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and you can report it at any police station, whichever area the house is in [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Online,** the Ministry of Women and Child Development runs SHe-Box for workplace sexual harassment complaints [[shebox]].

The weak link is the committee. On 3 December 2024 the Supreme Court ordered every state to notify a District Officer for each district by 31 December 2024 and to set up Local Committees by 31 January 2025 [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. By May 2025 every state had appointed District Officers, but whether Local Committees were in place was unclear in Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand and Kerala, and several states gave no information on the district survey [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. Jharkhand reported committees in 22 of its 24 districts. Delhi, where Jagori found one in four of the domestic workers it surveyed had been harassed, was among the four.

This is general information, not legal advice. If your district's committee cannot be found, the police, the Women Helpline and the 112 emergency number still work, and the law still treats the house where a woman is employed as her workplace.
domestic-workers-harassment-employer-hom.hg:
Domestic worker ke office mein na HR department hota hai, na colleagues, aur aksar koi likhit contract bhi nahi. Uska office kisi aur ka ghar hota hai, aur jis aadmi ki woh complaint karegi, woh employer khud ho sakta hai, ya uska beta, bhai ya pita. Indian law ke paas 2013 se kaagaz par iska jawab hai: POSH Act "a dwelling place or a house" ko bhi workplace maanta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Yeh explainer batata hai ki woh is law ka istemaal kaise kar sakti hai, aur system kahan use akela chhod deta hai.

## Kisi aur ke darwaze ke peeche

Sochiye, tees ki umr paar kar chuki ek aurat Delhi ki ek housing society ke chaar flats mein khana banati hai. Unmein se ek flat mein, family ka ek aadmi jab bhi woh kitchen mein akeli hoti hai, sexual remarks karne laga hai.
