Corridor ke aakhir mein koi complaint desk nahi hai: ghar wale hi uske employer hain. Agar woh virodh karti hai, toh naukri ja sakti hai, aur baat baaki teen families tak bhi pahunch sakti hai. Saboot ke naam par sirf uski baat hai, us aadmi ki baat ke khilaaf.

Ghar ke andar harassment wahan hota hai jahan koi aur dekh nahi raha hota, aur un auraton ke saath hota hai jinki kamaai usi family par tiki hai jis par unhe ilzaam lagana hoga. Raasta ek doosra khatra jodta hai. May se November 2024 ke beech hue Jagori ke survey mein Delhi-NCR ki 270 women domestic workers mein se 45% ne kaha ki raat ko shehar mein woh bahut unsafe mehsoos karti hain, aur 17% ne kaha thoda unsafe; saath hi Rs 5,000 mahine se kam kamaane wali workers apni kamaai ka lagbhag 20% sirf aane-jaane par kharch karti thin [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]].

## Law: ghar bhi workplace hai

Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, yaani POSH Act, "workplace" ki definition kaafi badi rakhta hai: offices, lekin saath hi hospitals, sports venues, employer ka diya hua transport aur private ghar bhi. Yeh "a woman of any age who is employed in such a dwelling place or house" ko protect karta hai, yaani aise ghar mein kaam karne wali kisi bhi umr ki aurat ko [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Office mein complaint employer ki Internal Committee ke paas jaati hai. Ghar mein aisi koi committee nahi hoti, isliye complaint Local Committee ke paas jaati hai. Har district mein District Officer ko yeh committee banani hoti hai, un workplaces ke liye jahan das se kam workers hain ya jahan complaint employer ke hi khilaaf hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Yahan se raasta alag ho jaata hai. Office worker ki committee khud inquiry karti hai, jo 90 din mein poori honi chahiye [[indiacode-posh-2013]]. Domestic worker ke case mein Local Committee ko prima facie case milne par uski complaint saat din ke andar police ko bhejni hoti hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Isse Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 79 ke tahat criminal case banta hai, jo aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabdon ya ishaaron par hai. Sexual harassment par khud Section 75 ke tahat teen saal tak ki saza hai, aur sexually coloured remarks par ek saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Complaint ghatna ke teen mahine ke andar karni hoti hai; committee yeh limit teen mahine aur badha sakti hai [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

Yaani domestic worker ke liye POSH Act asal mein police tak pahunchne ka raasta hai, jiska pehla padaav ek committee hai.

## 512 police cases, aur Delhi-NCR survey mein chaar mein se ek

Aisa kitni baar hota hai? Police data yeh nahi bata sakta. 1 July 2024 ko jab BNS laagu hua, toh National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ne offices ke alawa doosre work premises ki ek nayi category jodi: "shops, malls, factories, home etc." 2024 ke doosre half mein is category mein 512 cases record hue, jabki poore saal mein office premises par 388 cases the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In 512 cases mein ghar, shops aur factories sab mile hue hain, aur yeh sirf chhe mahine ke hain, isliye inse koi nahi bata sakta ki kitni domestic workers police tak gayin. Aur yeh ek chhote total ka bhi chhota hissa hain: 2024 mein register hue sexual harassment ke 15,609 cases mein se 12,592, yaani 81%, "other places" mein darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Jagori ke survey mein 270 auraton mein se 24% ne pichhle do saal mein sexual harassment jhela tha [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. Yeh figure sirf employers ke gharon tak seemit nahi hai, aur ek region ke sample ko poore India par laagu nahi kiya ja sakta. Lekin jab national police count sirf saikdon mein ho, toh yeh ishaara karta hai ki domestic workers ke saath hone wala zyada tar harassment kabhi case nahi banta.

## Domestic servitude aur trafficking

Kuch auraton aur ladkiyon ke liye ghar ek jaal ban jaata hai. 2024 mein India mein trafficking se rescue kiye gaye 5,839 logon mein se 105 ko domestic servitude ke liye traffic kiya gaya tha, jabki 2,347 ko prostitution ke liye sexual exploitation aur 1,493 ko forced labour ke liye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB in maqsadon ko umr ke hisaab se alag nahi karta.

BNS ke Section 143 ke tahat exploitation ke liye trafficking par 7 se 10 saal ki saza hai, bachche ke case mein kam se kam 10 saal, aur victim ki consent ka koi matlab nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Phir bhi 2024 mein jin 586 trafficking cases ka trial poora hua, unmein se sirf 43 mein conviction hua, yaani 7.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Bahar se servitude aam kaam jaisa dikh sakta hai. Warning signs: worker jise kabhi akele bahar nahi jaane diya jaata, jise paise nahi milte, jiska phone ya identity papers le liye gaye hain, ya jo kehti hai ki use laane wale agent ka paisa us par baaki hai.

## Domestic worker complaint kaise kar sakti hai

- **Local Committee ke paas jaiye.** Teen mahine ke andar use likhit complaint dijiye. Prima facie case milne par committee ko saat din ke andar complaint police ko bhejni hogi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- **Ya seedhe police ke paas jaiye.** Sexual harassment apne aap mein ek crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur aap ise kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakti hain, chahe ghar kisi bhi area mein ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Online,** Ministry of Women and Child Development workplace par sexual harassment ki complaints ke liye SHe-Box chalata hai [[shebox]].

Sabse kamzor kadi committee hi hai. 3 December 2024 ko Supreme Court ne har state ko order diya ki 31 December 2024 tak har district ke liye District Officer notify kare aur 31 January 2025 tak Local Committees banaye [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. May 2025 tak har state ne District Officers appoint kar diye the, lekin Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand aur Kerala mein yeh saaf nahi tha ki Local Committees bani hain ya nahi, aur kai states ne district survey ki koi jaankari hi nahi di [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. Jharkhand ne apne 24 mein se 22 districts mein committees hone ki report di. Delhi, jahan Jagori ne paaya ki survey ki gayi chaar mein se ek domestic worker ke saath harassment hua tha, inhi chaar mein tha.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Agar aapke district ki committee nahi mil rahi, toh police, Women Helpline aur 112 emergency number ab bhi kaam karte hain, aur law ab bhi us ghar ko aurat ka workplace maanta hai jahan woh kaam karti hai.

dowry-deaths-missed-warnings-review.en:
Consider a hypothetical. In the second year of her marriage, a woman phones her mother, twice, about her in-laws' demands for money. Her parents tell her to adjust. Once, she goes to the police station and is sent home after a "counselling" session. After she dies, each of those calls becomes evidence in a dowry-death case. The file goes to court, and nobody asks the question that could protect the next woman: who knew, and what did they do?

India registered 5,737 dowry-death cases in 2024, with 5,811 victims, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. No published national figure shows how many of those women had already asked someone for help.

## Cruelty 'soon before her death': a history in every case

Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (earlier Section 304B IPC) defines a dowry death as a woman's death by burns, bodily injury or in abnormal circumstances within 7 years of marriage, where it is shown that "soon before her death" her husband or his relatives subjected her to cruelty or harassment over dowry. They are then deemed to have caused her death, and the punishment is 7 years to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The warning is built into the crime: without earlier cruelty, there is no dowry death. Each of the 5,737 cases was registered on the allegation that harassment came first. Prosecutors must prove that history in court; no published national review uses it to ask what was missed.

The statistics then erase the history. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so an FIR that includes both dowry death and cruelty is counted only as a dowry death [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. A cruelty complaint she filed months earlier sits in another column, often another year, with nothing linking the two.

## 22-37%: what other countries found

Some countries have looked. Data from France (2019-2022), South Africa (2020-2021) and Colombia (2014-2017) show that between 22% and 37% of women killed by their intimate partners had previously reported physical, sexual or psychological violence by that partner. UNODC and UN Women say this suggests many such killings are preventable [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

The comparison has limits: three countries, partner killings only, while Indian dowry deaths also implicate in-laws. No comparable Indian figure has been published. The 22-37% is not India's number; it is a reason to find India's own.

## What the numbers cannot tell us

Police registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], but no published national data show how many women who later died were among them.

Under the 2005 Domestic Violence Act a magistrate can pass a protection order, and breaching one is punishable with up to 1 year in prison or a Rs 20,000 fine [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. NCRB counts only police-registered criminal cases under the Act: 616 in all of India in 2024, 496 of them from Kerala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Applications for protection orders are not counted. So the published data cannot say how many women who died had held an order, or had one broken.

By July 2026, 985 One Stop Centres were operating, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. That figure counts women assisted, not what happened to them afterwards.

And most warnings never reach an office. Only 14.1% of women who faced physical or sexual violence ever sought help; 77.2% never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Of those who did seek help, 60.9% turned to their own family and only 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The first warning usually lands in her parents' home, not a police station.

Reporting alone is not protection. A 2021 working paper found that opening all-women police stations in Indian cities was associated with a 29% rise in police reports of crimes against women, mostly domestic violence, with no change in femicide [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. More women walked in; the number of women killed did not move. What happens after a report is the part the published data do not show.

## A missed-warnings review: how it would work

Imagine a district panel that meets after every dowry death. It should also take the 701 murders recorded with dowry as the motive in 2024, counted apart from dowry deaths, and abetment-of-suicide cases in which a husband or in-laws are accused; police registered 4,220 cases of abetment of women's suicide that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Chaired by someone independent of the police, such as the district legal services authority, it would bring the police, the Protection Officer under the Domestic Violence Act, the One Stop Centre, the hospital and a women's rights group to one table, and ask four questions:

- **Where did she go?** Her parents, a police help desk, a centre, a hospital, a magistrate.
- **What did each one do?** Register an FIR, or send her home to "compromise"? Seek a protection order? Call her back?
- **What was missing?** Shelter, money, a lawyer, a safe home to return to.
- **What changes now?** One written recommendation per agency, published as an anonymised district summary.

The review would not decide guilt; the trial does that. It would never name the woman or her family. And it would ask what the system did with her warning, never why she did not leave.

Over a few years, district summaries would show what no single trial can: the station that sends women back, the centre that never follows up, the order nobody enforces. That pattern is what a review could break.

## What families, police and centres can do now

Families: when a daughter or sister calls about dowry demands, treat it as a warning, not something to "adjust" to. Note the dates, keep the messages and offer her a way home. Police: register the cruelty complaint instead of counselling her back. Centres and Protection Officers: call back the women who came in, and record what happened next.

If you or someone you know is thinking about suicide, call Tele-MANAS on 14416 [[tele-manas]].
dowry-deaths-missed-warnings-review.hg:
Ek hypothetical sochiye. Shaadi ke doosre saal mein ek aurat apni maa ko do baar phone karti hai, sasural walon ki paison ki demands ke baare mein. Maa-baap kehte hain, adjust karo. Ek baar woh police station jaati hai, aur ek "counselling" session ke baad use ghar wapas bhej diya jaata hai. Uski maut ke baad yeh saari calls ek dowry death case mein evidence ban jaati hain. File court pahunchti hai, aur koi woh sawaal nahi poochta jo agli aurat ko bacha sakta hai: kise pata tha, aur unhone kya kiya?

India mein 2024 mein dowry death ke 5,737 cases register hue, jinme 5,811 victims thin, yaani roz lagbhag 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme se kitni auratein pehle hi kisi se madad maang chuki thin, yeh koi published national figure nahi batata.

## 'Maut se kuch hi pehle' cruelty: har case mein ek history

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 80 (pehle IPC ka Section 304B) ise dowry death kehta hai jab kisi aurat ki maut shaadi ke 7 saal ke andar jalne se, body par chot se ya abnormal haalat mein ho, aur yeh dikhaya jaye ki "maut se kuch hi pehle" uske pati ya pati ke relatives ne dowry ke liye uske saath cruelty ya harassment ki thi. Tab maana jaata hai ki maut ke zimmedaar wahi hain, aur saza 7 saal se lekar life imprisonment tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Warning is crime ki definition mein hi likhi hai: pehle ki cruelty ke bina koi dowry death nahi hoti. 5,737 mein se har case is allegation par register hua ki harassment pehle hua tha. Prosecution ko court mein yeh history prove karni padti hai; lekin koi published national review is history se yeh nahi poochta ki kya chhoot gaya.

Phir statistics yeh history mita dete hain. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke under, isliye jis FIR mein dowry death aur cruelty dono hon, woh sirf dowry death gini jaati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Usne mahino pehle jo cruelty complaint ki thi, woh kisi aur column mein padi rehti hai, aksar kisi aur saal mein, aur dono ko jodne wala kuch nahi hota.

## 22-37%: doosre deshon ko kya mila

Kuch deshon ne yeh dekha hai. France (2019-2022), South Africa (2020-2021) aur Colombia (2014-2017) ka data dikhata hai ki intimate partner ke haathon maari gayi auraton mein se 22% se 37% ne pehle hi us partner ki physical, sexual ya psychological violence report ki thi. UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik isse lagta hai ki aisi kai hatyayein roki ja sakti hain [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

Is comparison ki limits hain: sirf teen desh, sirf partner ke haathon hui hatyayein, jabki India ki dowry deaths mein sasural wale bhi accused hote hain. India ka koi comparable figure publish nahi hua hai. 22-37% India ka number nahi hai; yeh India ka apna number dhoondhne ki wajah hai.

## Numbers humein kya nahi bata sakte

Police ne 2024 mein pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], lekin koi published national data nahi batata ki baad mein jin auraton ki maut hui, unme se kitni in cases mein thin.

2005 ke Domestic Violence Act ke under magistrate protection order de sakta hai, aur use todne par 1 saal tak ki jail ya Rs 20,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. NCRB is Act ke under sirf police mein register hue criminal cases ginta hai: 2024 mein poore India mein 616, jinme se 496 Kerala se the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Protection order ki applications gini hi nahi jaatin. Isliye published data yeh nahi bata sakta ki jin auraton ki maut hui, unme se kitnon ke paas protection order tha, ya kitnon ka order toda gaya.

July 2026 tak 985 One Stop Centres chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Yeh figure madad paane wali auraton ki ginti hai, yeh nahi ki unke saath baad mein kya hua.

Aur zyada tar warnings kabhi kisi office tak pahunchti hi nahi. Physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali auraton mein se sirf 14.1% ne kabhi madad maangi; 77.2% ne na madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jinhone madad maangi, unme se 60.9% apni hi family ke paas gayin aur sirf 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Pehli warning aksar uske maayke mein pahunchti hai, police station mein nahi.

Sirf report karna protection nahi hai. 2021 ke ek working paper mein paaya gaya ki Indian shehron mein all-women police stations khulne ke saath auraton ke khilaf crimes ki police reports mein 29% ki badhat hui, zyada tar domestic violence ki, lekin femicide mein koi badlav nahi aaya [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. Zyada auratein aage aayin; maari jaane wali auraton ki ginti wahi rahi. Report ke baad kya hota hai, yahi woh hissa hai jo published data mein nahi dikhta.

## Missed-warnings review: yeh kaise kaam karega

Sochiye ek district panel jo har dowry death ke baad baithta hai. Use 2024 mein dowry motive ke saath record hue 701 murders bhi dekhne chahiye, jo dowry deaths se alag gine jaate hain, aur abetment of suicide ke woh cases bhi jinme pati ya sasural wale accused hain; us saal police ne auraton ke suicide ke abetment ke 4,220 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Iski chairperson police se independent ho, jaise district legal services authority, aur yeh panel police, Domestic Violence Act ke Protection Officer, One Stop Centre, hospital aur ek women's rights group ko ek table par laaye, aur chaar sawaal poochhe:

- **Woh kahan gayi thi?** Maa-baap, police help desk, centre, hospital, magistrate.
- **Har ek ne kya kiya?** FIR register ki, ya use "compromise" ke liye ghar bhej diya? Protection order ke liye apply kiya? Use dobara call kiya?
- **Kya kami thi?** Shelter, paise, vakeel, wapas jaane ke liye ek safe ghar.
- **Ab kya badlega?** Har agency ke liye ek likhit recommendation, jo anonymised district summary ke roop mein publish ho.

Review guilt tay nahi karega; woh kaam trial ka hai. Yeh kabhi us aurat ya uski family ka naam nahi lega. Aur yeh poochega ki system ne uski warning ke saath kya kiya, yeh kabhi nahi ki woh chhod kar kyun nahi gayi.

Kuch saalon mein district summaries woh dikhayengi jo koi ek trial nahi dikha sakta: woh thana jo auraton ko wapas bhej deta hai, woh centre jo kabhi follow-up nahi karta, woh order jise koi lagu nahi karta. Review isi pattern ko tod sakta hai.

## Families, police aur centres abhi kya kar sakte hain

Families: jab beti ya behen dowry demands ke baare mein call kare, toh use warning samjhiye, "adjust karne" wali baat nahi. Dates note kijiye, messages sambhaal kar rakhiye aur use ghar wapas aane ka raasta dijiye. Police: cruelty complaint register kijiye, counselling karke use wapas mat bhejiye. Centres aur Protection Officers: jo auratein aayi thin unhe dobara call kijiye, aur record rakhiye ki aage kya hua.

Agar aap ya aapka koi jaanne wala suicide ke baare mein soch raha hai, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye [[tele-manas]].

dowry-deaths-sixteen-women-a-day.en:
In 2024, police in India registered 5,737 dowry deaths and counted 5,811 women as victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is about 16 a day. Each case is, in law, a woman who died within seven years of her wedding after her husband or his relatives harassed her or treated her with cruelty over dowry [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. India made giving and taking dowry a crime in 1961 [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Sixty-three years on, the count is falling, but slowly, and it is not the full count.

## 16 a day: what the number measures

"Dowry death" is a legal category, not a description. Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which took over from Section 304B of the IPC on 1 July 2024, applies when a woman dies of burns, bodily injury or "otherwise than under normal circumstances" within seven years of marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death she faced cruelty or harassment linked to a demand for dowry. The punishment is seven years to life in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

So 5,737 is not "every woman killed over dowry". It is the number of deaths that police registered under this one heading. The UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) notes that the provision "may apply in any unnatural death of a woman within seven years of marriage", so the category can include deaths that are not murders in the narrow sense [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]]. What every case shares is the harassment that came first. By the law's own definition, each of these deaths followed dowry harassment, so in every case there was a warning before the death.

## From 6,966 to 5,737: a slow decline

Registered dowry deaths have fallen every year since 2020. So have murders in which police recorded dowry as the motive, which NCRB counts in a separate table [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| Year | Dowry deaths registered | Murders with dowry as the motive |
|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 6,966 | 1,171 |
| 2021 | 6,753 | 952 |
| 2022 | 6,450 | 951 |
| 2023 | 6,156 | 833 |
| 2024 | 5,737 | 701 |

The figures for 2020 to 2023 come from NCRB's reports for those years [[ncrb-cii-2020]] [[ncrb-cii-2021]] [[ncrb-cii-2022]] [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

Four years of decline is a real change in the records. Whether it is the same change in women's lives is harder to say. Fewer registered cases is what you would see if fewer women were dying. It is also what you would see if more deaths were written off as accidents or suicides, or if fewer families went to the police. Police tables cannot tell these apart.

One check is possible. If dowry deaths were simply being re-filed as abetment of suicide, that category would rise. It fell too, from 4,963 cases with women as victims in 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2022]] to 4,220 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But a death recorded as an accident, with no complaint, enters no crime table at all.

The longer record shows the scale. From 1999 to 2016, dowry deaths made up 40% to 50% of all killings of women recorded in India each year, according to UNODC's analysis of NCRB data [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]].

## Uttar Pradesh's 35.5%

Uttar Pradesh registered 2,038 dowry deaths in 2024, or 35.5% of India's total. Bihar came next with 1,078, followed by Madhya Pradesh (450), Rajasthan (386) and West Bengal (337) [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Part of that share is size: a large state registers more cases. But not all of it: Uttar Pradesh recorded 1.8 dowry deaths per lakh women, more than twice the national rate of 0.8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

NCRB warns against ranking states on crime figures alone, because a higher count can also mean that police there register more cases. Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, the top two for dowry deaths, also register most of India's cases under the 1961 Dowry Prohibition Act: 4,482 and 3,780 of the 12,343 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Both readings can be true at once: dowry pressure is heavy there, and police there are more used to naming it. A low count elsewhere is not proof that dowry is rare.

## Dowry deaths, dowry murders and what the categories hide

The 701 dowry murders of 2024 are not part of the 5,737. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence. An FIR that includes both dowry death and cruelty counts only as a dowry death, and a killing booked as murder goes into the murder table, where dowry appears only as the motive [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]].

The rule stops double counting, but it makes every column partial. And some deaths never reach the dowry-death column at all:

- a woman who dies more than seven years after her wedding cannot be a "dowry death" in law, however long the harassment lasted;
- a death recorded as an accident or a suicide, with no complaint of harassment, never becomes a crime record;
- a woman whose family never goes to the police leaves no trace in these tables.

So 5,737 is a floor, not a ceiling. It counts only the deaths that someone reported and police recorded as dowry deaths.

## What families can do before and after the wedding

When women in India seek help after violence, most turn to their own family: 60.9% of them, against 6.3% who went to the police, in the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That makes a woman's own family the people most likely to hear the first warning.

Imagine a 24-year-old software tester in Bengaluru, eight months married. She phones her mother to say that her in-laws want a car before Diwali, and that her husband has stopped speaking to her until it arrives. This is the moment the law is built for. Demanding dowry is a crime under the 1961 Act, with six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Harassing a woman to make her or her family meet an unlawful demand for property is cruelty under Sections 85 and 86 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

A common family answer is "adjust, it will settle down". A better one starts before the wedding: refuse dowry out loud, as a family. After it, treat the first demand as the warning it is. Believe her, keep a record, and make sure she knows she can come home. Every death in this count followed harassment over dowry. The question is whether families act at the first demand, or only after a death.
dowry-deaths-sixteen-women-a-day.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne 5,737 dowry deaths register kin, aur 5,811 auraton ko victim gina [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani roz qareeb 16. Law ki nazar mein har case ek aisi aurat hai jiski maut shaadi ke saat saal ke andar hui, aur usse pehle uske pati ya sasural walon ne dowry ke liye use pareshan kiya ya uske saath cruelty ki [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. India ne 1961 mein hi dowry lena aur dena crime bana diya tha [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. 63 saal baad yeh count gir raha hai, par bahut dheere. Aur yeh poora count bhi nahi hai.

## Roz 16: yeh number asal mein kya ginta hai

"Dowry death" ek legal category hai, koi aam description nahi. Ab yeh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 80 hai; 1 July 2024 se pehle yahi IPC ka Section 304B tha. Yeh tab lagta hai jab shaadi ke saat saal ke andar kisi aurat ki maut jalne se, chot se, ya "normal circumstances se hatkar" ho, aur yeh dikhaya jaye ki maut se kuch hi pehle dowry demand ko lekar use pareshan kiya gaya ya uske saath cruelty hui. Saza kam se kam saat saal hai, aur life imprisonment tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Toh 5,737 ka matlab "dowry ke liye maari gayi har aurat" nahi hai. Yeh un maut ka count hai jinhe police ne is ek heading mein register kiya. UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) ke shabdon mein yeh provision "may apply in any unnatural death of a woman within seven years of marriage", yaani shaadi ke pehle saat saal mein kisi bhi unnatural death par lag sakta hai. Isliye is category mein kuch aisi maut bhi aa sakti hain jo strict sense mein murder nahi hain [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]]. Par har case mein ek cheez common hai: maut se pehle ki harassment. Law ki apni definition se hi, har maut dowry harassment ke baad hui, yaani har case mein maut se pehle ek warning thi.

## 6,966 se 5,737 tak: dheemi giraavat

2020 ke baad se registered dowry deaths har saal kam hui hain. Woh murders bhi kam hue hain jinme police ne motive dowry likha, jinhe NCRB ek alag table mein ginta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| Saal | Registered dowry deaths | Murders jinka motive dowry darj hua |
|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 6,966 | 1,171 |
| 2021 | 6,753 | 952 |
| 2022 | 6,450 | 951 |
| 2023 | 6,156 | 833 |
| 2024 | 5,737 | 701 |

2020 se 2023 tak ke figures NCRB ki un saalon ki reports se liye gaye hain [[ncrb-cii-2020]] [[ncrb-cii-2021]] [[ncrb-cii-2022]] [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

Chaar saal ki giraavat records mein asli badlaav hai. Par kya auraton ki zindagi mein bhi utna hi badlaav aaya? Yeh kehna mushkil hai. Agar kam auratein mar rahi hon, toh registered cases kam honge. Lekin agar zyada maut ko accident ya suicide bolkar chhod diya jaye, ya kam families police tak jayein, tab bhi cases kam honge. Police ki tables in dono mein farq nahi bata sakti.

Ek check zaroor ho sakta hai. Agar dowry deaths bas "abetment of suicide" waale column mein shift ho rahi hoti, toh woh count badhta. Par woh bhi gira: auraton ke abetment of suicide ke cases 2022 mein 4,963 the [[ncrb-cii-2022]], aur 2024 mein 4,220 reh gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin jo maut accident maankar darj ho aur koi complaint na ho, woh kisi crime table tak pahunchti hi nahi.

Lamba record is crime ka scale dikhata hai. UNODC ne NCRB data dekhkar bataya ki 1999 se 2016 tak India mein har saal recorded auraton ke kul murders mein 40% se 50% dowry deaths thi [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]].

## Uttar Pradesh ka 35.5%

2024 mein Uttar Pradesh mein 2,038 dowry deaths register hui, yaani poore India ka 35.5%. Uske baad Bihar (1,078), Madhya Pradesh (450), Rajasthan (386) aur West Bengal (337) aate hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Is bade hisse ki ek wajah size hai: bade state mein cases bhi zyada register hote hain. Par poori wajah yahi nahi hai: Uttar Pradesh mein har ek lakh auraton par 1.8 dowry deaths darj hui, jabki national rate 0.8 hai. Yaani do guna se bhi zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

NCRB khud kehta hai ki sirf crime figures dekhkar states ki ranking mat karo, kyunki zyada count ka matlab yeh bhi ho sakta hai ki wahan police zyada cases register karti hai. Dowry deaths mein sabse aage rehne wale yahi do states, Uttar Pradesh aur Bihar, 1961 ke Dowry Prohibition Act ke zyada tar cases bhi register karte hain: 2024 ke 12,343 cases mein se 4,482 Uttar Pradesh mein aur 3,780 Bihar mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Dono baatein ek saath sach ho sakti hain: wahan dowry ka pressure bhaari hai, aur wahan ki police use dowry case bolne ki aadi bhi hai. Kisi aur state mein kam count ka matlab yeh nahi ki wahan dowry kam hai.

## Dowry deaths, dowry murders aur categories mein kya chhup jaata hai

2024 ke 701 dowry murders in 5,737 mein shaamil nahi hain. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam se. Jis FIR mein dowry death aur cruelty dono hain, woh sirf dowry death gini jaati hai. Aur jis maut ko murder ka case banaya gaya, woh murder table mein jaati hai, jahan dowry sirf motive ke roop mein dikhta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]].

Is rule se double counting nahi hoti, par har column adhoora reh jaata hai. Aur kuch maut dowry death waale column tak kabhi pahunchti hi nahi:

- jis aurat ki maut shaadi ke saat saal baad hui, woh law mein "dowry death" nahi ho sakti, chahe harassment kitne bhi saal chali ho;
- jo maut accident ya suicide maankar darj hui aur harassment ki koi complaint nahi hui, woh kabhi crime record nahi banti;
- jis aurat ki family kabhi police ke paas nahi gayi, uska in tables mein koi nishaan nahi milta.

Isliye 5,737 sabse neeche ka count hai, upar ki limit nahi. Ismein sirf woh maut hain jinki kisi ne report ki aur police ne unhe dowry death ke roop mein darj kiya.

## Shaadi se pehle aur baad mein family kya kar sakti hai

India mein jo auratein violence ke baad madad maangti hain, unme se zyada tar apni hi family ke paas jaati hain: National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) ke hisaab se 60.9% family ke paas gayi, aur sirf 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Isliye pehli warning sunne ka sabse zyada chance aurat ki apni family ka hi hota hai.

Sochiye, Bengaluru mein 24 saal ki ek software tester hai, shaadi ko aath mahine hue hain. Woh apni maa ko phone karke batati hai ki sasural wale Diwali se pehle car chahte hain, aur jab tak car nahi aati, pati ne usse baat karna band kar diya hai. Law isi moment ke liye bana hai. 1961 ke Act mein dowry maangna apne aap mein crime hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal tak hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Aur kisi aurat ko isliye pareshan karna ki woh ya uski family property ki koi illegal demand poori kare, BNS ke Section 85 aur 86 ke under cruelty hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Family ka ek aam jawab hota hai, "adjust kar lo, sab theek ho jayega." Behtar jawab shaadi se pehle shuru hota hai: poori family milkar, khulkar dowry ko na kahe. Shaadi ke baad pehli demand ko warning samjhiye. Uski baat par bharosa kijiye, record rakhiye, aur use pakka bataiye ki woh ghar aa sakti hai. Is count ki har maut se pehle dowry ke liye harassment hui thi. Sawaal yeh hai ki families pehli demand par kadam uthati hain, ya sirf kisi ki maut ke baad.

dowry-prohibition-act-enforcement-failur.en:
Read the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and it sounds severe. Giving, taking or abetting dowry carries at least five years in prison and a fine of at least Rs 15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more. Demanding it carries six months to two years and a fine of up to Rs 10,000. Every offence is non-bailable [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Now look at the courts. In 2024, trials under the Act ended in 719 convictions and 3,062 acquittals across the whole country [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The distance between those two pictures is the story of India's dowry law.

## What the 1961 law says

The Act goes after the deal itself. It does not wait for violence or a death: a demand is a crime even if nothing is ever paid [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

Its offences are also non-compoundable, which means the two families cannot settle the case between themselves and make it disappear. Courts may give less than the five-year minimum, but only for "adequate and special reasons" written into the judgment [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

The Act does not stand alone. Harassing a woman to make her or her family meet an unlawful demand for property is cruelty under Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), with up to three years in prison. If she dies in abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage after dowry-linked cruelty or harassment, it is a dowry death under Section 80, with seven years to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In 2024, police registered 5,737 such deaths [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This article is general information, not legal advice.

## 12,343 cases: who files and where

Police registered 12,343 cases under the Act in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The count had risen from 10,366 in 2020 [[ncrb-cii-2022]] to 15,489 in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] before it fell.

Three states produced more than four in five of the 2024 cases: Uttar Pradesh (4,482), Bihar (3,780) and Karnataka (1,991). West Bengal registered none at all. Maharashtra registered 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

That map says more about police habits than about where dowry lives. West Bengal recorded zero Dowry Act cases in 2024, yet it recorded 337 dowry deaths, the fifth-highest count in India, and 19,330 cases of cruelty by husbands or relatives, the second-highest [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Dowry is clearly present there. Complaints about it are most likely being filed under other headings, such as cruelty, the largest single crime against women in India's data.

The counting rule hides more. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. If a woman dies, the case goes into the dowry-death or murder count. If a dowry demand is filed together with cruelty, which carries a longer maximum sentence than demanding dowry, the FIR is counted as cruelty. The Dowry Act column shows only the complaints in which the Act was the most serious charge.

And most women who face violence never complain at all. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone. Of those who did seek help, only 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 17.4% convicted, 83,298 pending

Of the Dowry Act trials that courts completed in 2024, 17.4% ended in conviction: 719 convictions against 3,062 acquittals. At the end of the year, 83,298 cases were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the same year police registered 12,343 new cases, about three times the number of trials the courts completed.

The same courts did better with related crimes that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Offence (2024) | Conviction rate |
|---|---|
| Dowry death (Section 80 BNS / 304B IPC) | 46.2% |
| All crimes against women | 25.7% |
| Cruelty by husband or relatives | 20.1% |
| Dowry Prohibition Act | 17.4% |

The Act, whose penalties start at six months for demanding dowry and five years for giving or taking it, convicts less often than the cruelty law, which has no minimum sentence at all [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Severity on paper has not turned into punishment in court. And a 17.4% rate tells a family something before they ever file: most cases that reach a verdict end in acquittal, and the wait is long.

## On paper, the giver is guilty too

The Act punishes "giving, taking or abetting" dowry alike [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. On paper, parents who pay are offenders too, facing the same five-year minimum as the family that takes.

In practice, the payment can be the part of the story that never reaches the police. Consider a schoolteacher in Bhopal who took a loan to pay what his daughter's in-laws asked for. A year later the demands return, and she is being harassed. To her family, that loan may feel like a wedding expense or a private shame, not evidence of a crime. Their complaint may describe the harassment and leave the payment out.

That is where the law runs into social habit. Dowry is rarely called dowry. It is a "gift", a "custom", "what everyone gives". Its pull starts long before the wedding: UNFPA notes that where a bride's family pays dowry, younger brides usually command smaller dowries, which gives poor parents a reason to marry daughters off early [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. A law that depends on families calling a payment dowry, when everyone around them calls it a gift, will not catch much.

## What real enforcement would need

Our reading of the numbers points to four changes:

- **Make reporting safe.** Prosecution should aim at the people who demand and take, and families who come forward should be treated as witnesses.
- **Count every dowry charge.** NCRB shows only the lead charge in each FIR. A count of every FIR that includes a Dowry Act section would show the real scale.
- **Clear the queue.** With 83,298 cases pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]], a complaint filed today joins a very long line.
- **Watch the wedding season.** For child marriage, the Supreme Court in October 2024 told states to appoint district officers with no other duties, publish their reports online every quarter, and have magistrates act early around "auspicious days" for mass weddings [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Dowry enforcement could borrow that model.

None of this replaces what happens inside families. The 1961 Act will start to bite when refusing dowry is normal, not brave: when a family says no before the match is fixed, keeps a record of every demand, and reports the first one.
dowry-prohibition-act-enforcement-failur.hg:
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 padhiye, toh yeh kaafi sakht law lagta hai. Dowry dene, lene ya usme madad karne par kam se kam paanch saal jail, aur kam se kam Rs 15,000 ya dowry ki value jitna fine, jo bhi zyada ho. Dowry maangne par chhe mahine se do saal jail aur Rs 10,000 tak fine. Har offence non-bailable hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Ab courts ki taraf dekhiye. 2024 mein poore desh mein is Act ke trials se sirf 719 convictions nikle, aur 3,062 cases mein accused bari ho gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In do tasveeron ke beech ki doori hi India ke dowry law ki kahani hai.

## 1961 ka law kya kehta hai

Yeh Act seedha deal par vaar karta hai. Yeh kisi violence ya maut ka intezaar nahi karta: dowry maangna hi crime hai, chahe ek rupaya bhi na diya gaya ho [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

Iske offences non-compoundable bhi hain, yaani dono families aapas mein settle karke case khatam nahi kar sakti. Court paanch saal se kam saza de sakti hai, par sirf "adequate and special reasons" ke liye, jo judgment mein likhe jayein [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

Yeh Act akela nahi hai. Kisi aurat ko isliye pareshan karna ki woh ya uski family property ki koi illegal demand poori kare, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 85 aur 86 ke under cruelty hai, jisme teen saal tak jail hai. Aur agar dowry ke liye aisi cruelty ya harassment ke baad shaadi ke saat saal ke andar abnormal circumstances mein uski maut ho jaye, toh yeh Section 80 ke under dowry death hai, jisme saat saal se life imprisonment tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2024 mein police ne aisi 5,737 maut register kin [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh article general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 12,343 cases: kaun complaint karta hai, aur kahan

2024 mein police ne is Act ke under 12,343 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2020 mein yeh count 10,366 tha [[ncrb-cii-2022]], 2023 mein badhkar 15,489 hua [[ncrb-cii-2023]], aur phir gira.

2024 ke har paanch mein se chaar se zyada cases sirf teen states se aaye: Uttar Pradesh (4,482), Bihar (3,780) aur Karnataka (1,991). West Bengal mein ek bhi case register nahi hua. Maharashtra mein sirf 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh map dowry ke baare mein kam, aur police ki aadaton ke baare mein zyada batata hai. West Bengal mein 2024 mein Dowry Act ka ek bhi case nahi tha, phir bhi wahan 337 dowry deaths darj hui, jo India mein paanchvein number par hai, aur pati ya sasural walon ki cruelty ke 19,330 cases, jo doosre number par hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Matlab dowry wahan hai. Zyada sambhavna yahi hai ki uski complaints doosre columns mein darj ho rahi hain, jaise cruelty, jo India ke data mein auraton ke khilaf sabse bada crime hai.

Counting ka rule aur bhi bahut kuch chhupa deta hai. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke naam se [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Agar aurat ki maut ho gayi, toh case dowry death ya murder mein gina jaata hai. Agar dowry demand ke saath cruelty ka section bhi laga, toh FIR cruelty mein gini jaati hai, kyunki cruelty ki maximum saza dowry maangne se lambi hai. Dowry Act waale column mein sirf woh complaints aati hain jinme yahi Act sabse serious charge tha.

Aur violence jhelne wali zyada tar auratein complaint karti hi nahi. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% auraton ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya. Jinhone madad maangi, unme se sirf 6.3% police ke paas gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 17.4% convicted, 83,298 pending

2024 mein courts ne Dowry Act ke jin trials ko poora kiya, unme se sirf 17.4% mein conviction hua: 719 convictions aur 3,062 acquittals. Saal ke end mein 83,298 cases abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal police ne 12,343 naye cases register kiye, yaani courts ne jitne trials khatam kiye, uske qareeb teen guna naye cases jud gaye.

Usi saal, unhi courts mein, milte-julte crimes ka haal thoda behtar tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Offence (2024) | Conviction rate |
|---|---|
| Dowry death (BNS Section 80 / IPC 304B) | 46.2% |
| Auraton ke khilaf saare crimes | 25.7% |
| Pati ya sasural walon ki cruelty | 20.1% |
| Dowry Prohibition Act | 17.4% |

Is Act mein saza dowry maangne par chhe mahine se aur dowry dene ya lene par paanch saal se shuru hoti hai. Phir bhi yeh cruelty waale law se bhi kam cases mein conviction dila paata hai, jabki cruelty mein minimum saza ki koi shart hi nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Kaagaz ki sakhti court mein saza nahi ban paayi. Aur 17.4% ka number kisi family ko complaint se pehle hi ek baat bata deta hai: jin cases ka faisla aata hai, unme se zyada tar mein accused bari hote hain, aur intezaar lamba hai.

## Kaagaz par dene wala bhi guilty

Yeh Act dowry "dene, lene ya usme madad karne" ko ek jaisa crime maanta hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Yaani kaagaz par dowry dene wale maa-baap bhi offenders hain, aur un par bhi wahi kam se kam paanch saal ki saza lagu hoti hai jo lene wali family par.

Asal zindagi mein payment wali baat kai baar police tak pahunchti hi nahi. Sochiye, Bhopal mein ek school teacher hain jinhone loan lekar beti ke sasural walon ki demand poori ki. Ek saal baad demands phir shuru ho jaati hain, aur beti ko pareshan kiya ja raha hai. Family ko woh loan shaadi ka ek kharcha ya sharm ki baat lag sakta hai, kisi crime ka saboot nahi. Unki complaint mein harassment ki baat ho sakti hai, aur payment ki baat chhoot sakti hai.

Yahin law samaaj ki aadaton se takraata hai. Dowry ko shayad hi kabhi dowry bola jaata hai. Woh "gift" hai, "rivaaj" hai, "sab dete hain". Iska asar shaadi se bahut pehle shuru ho jaata hai: UNFPA batata hai ki jahan dulhan ki family dowry deti hai, wahan kam umar ki dulhan ke liye aam taur par kam dowry maanga jaata hai, jisse gareeb maa-baap ko betiyon ki jaldi shaadi karne ki wajah mil jaati hai [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. Jo law is baat par tika ho ki family payment ko dowry kahe, jabki aas-paas sab use gift kehte hain, woh zyada kuch nahi pakad paayega.

## Asli enforcement ke liye kya chahiye

Numbers padhkar humein chaar badlaav zaroori lagte hain:

- **Report karna safe banaiye.** Action unpar ho jo maangte aur lete hain, aur aage aane wali families ko witness maana jaye.
- **Har dowry charge giniye.** NCRB har FIR mein sirf sabse bada charge dikhata hai. Agar har us FIR ka count ho jisme Dowry Act ka koi section laga, toh asli scale dikhega.
- **Atke cases nipataiye.** 83,298 cases pending hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]], toh aaj ki complaint bahut lambi line mein lagti hai.
- **Shaadi ke season par nazar rakhiye.** Child marriage ke liye Supreme Court ne October 2024 mein states se kaha tha ki har district mein aise officers rakhe jaayein jinke paas koi aur kaam na ho, unki reports har teen mahine online daali jaayein, aur magistrates mass weddings waale "auspicious days" ke aaspaas pehle se action lein [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Dowry rokne ke liye bhi yahi model apnaya ja sakta hai.

Inme se koi bhi badlaav families ke andar ki soch ki jagah nahi le sakta. 1961 ka Act tab asar dikhayega jab dowry ko na kehna normal hoga, bahaduri nahi: jab family rishta pakka hone se pehle na kahe, har demand ka record rakhe, aur pehli demand par hi report kare.

dowry-questions-before-after-wedding.en:
In 2024 police recorded 5,737 dowry deaths in India, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]], in a country that made dowry a crime in 1961. Part of the problem is that dowry is rarely called dowry. It arrives as a list of "expectations", a car that is "not a demand", a father's loan. Here are ten questions families actually ask, answered under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). This is general information, not legal advice.

## What does the 1961 Act call dowry?

**1. What counts as dowry?**

The Dowry Prohibition Act is about property or valuables passed between the two sides in connection with a marriage, and it punishes three acts: giving dowry, taking it and demanding it [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Cash, gold, a car or a flat can all be dowry. What the families call it does not change that.

**2. What is the punishment?**

Giving, taking or abetting dowry carries at least 5 years in prison and a fine of at least Rs 15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more. Demanding it carries 6 months to 2 years and a fine of up to Rs 10,000 [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. A demand is a crime even if nothing is ever paid.

## Are 'gifts' and the bride's parents covered?

**3. Is it dowry if they call it a gift?**

The label does not decide it; the demand does. Because the Act makes demanding dowry a crime in its own right [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]], the question is whether something was asked for, hinted at as "expected" or made a condition of the match. Calling it a gift does not turn a demand into a present. "We are not asking, but everyone in our family gives a car" can still be a demand, if it can be proved.

**4. Can the bride's parents be prosecuted for paying?**

On paper, yes: the Act punishes giving dowry with the same minimum of five years as taking it [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. That can make a family afraid to speak. Before filing, get free legal advice from a Legal Services Authority on how to word the complaint [[nalsa]]. Do not let the fear keep a family silent while she is being harassed: harassment over a demand is a crime against her, whoever paid.

## Is a demand after the wedding still dowry?

**5. The wedding is over and now they want a car. Is that still dowry?**

Yes, and it is a crime whenever it comes. Demanding dowry is an offence under the 1961 Act [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Harassment to force her or her family to pay, or to punish them for not paying, is also cruelty under Section 86 of the BNS, punishable under Section 85 with up to three years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

**6. What if the harassment ends in her death?**

If a woman dies of burns, bodily injury or in abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, and she was subjected to cruelty or harassment over dowry soon before her death, the case can become a "dowry death" under Section 80 of the BNS, with seven years to life in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Few such cases are decided quickly: in 2024 courts completed 4,043 dowry-death trials, 46.2% ended in conviction, and 59,446 cases (93.6%) were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## How are dowry and child marriage linked?

**7. Why does dowry push families to marry daughters early?**

UNFPA notes that where the bride's family pays dowry, younger brides typically command smaller dowries, which gives poor parents an incentive to marry daughters off early [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. That is how a "custom" about gifts can end a girl's schooling. UNICEF says girls who marry before 18 are more likely to face domestic violence and less likely to stay in school [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Of an estimated 640 million girls and women alive today who were married as children, one third are in India [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]].

**8. What does the law say about child marriage?**

Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a marriage is a child marriage if the bride is under 18 or the groom under 21. An adult man who marries a child, and anyone who performs or abets the marriage, faces up to 2 years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh; the offences are cognizable and non-bailable. The child can have the marriage annulled until two years after reaching adulthood [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. And sex with a wife under 18 is rape: the BNS marital exception does not cover her [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. To stop a child marriage, call the Child Helpline on 1098 [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

## Why do so few dowry cases end in conviction?

**9. How often do dowry cases end in conviction?**

Rarely. Police registered 12,343 cases under the Dowry Act in 2024. Of the trials courts completed that year, 17.4% ended in conviction, and 83,298 cases were still pending at its end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB does not record why trials fail, but a demand made across a living-room table leaves no trace unless someone writes it down.

**10. What should a family do when the first demand comes?**

Treat it as evidence, not a negotiation. Write down that day who asked, for what, and who heard it; save messages and voice notes. Keep a written list of wedding presents, signed by the bride and the groom, so it is clear later what was given freely. Remember that dowry offences are non-bailable and non-compoundable, so the families cannot simply settle them [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. If harassment follows the wedding, one complaint can invoke the Dowry Act and Sections 85 and 86 of the BNS together. You can report at any police station, wherever the demand was made, or file an e-FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
dowry-questions-before-after-wedding.hg:
2024 mein police ne India mein 5,737 dowry deaths darj kin, yaani roz lagbhag 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], us desh mein jahan 1961 se dowry crime hai. Problem ka ek hissa yeh hai ki dowry ko shayad hi kabhi dowry kaha jaata hai. Woh "expectations" ki list ban kar aati hai, ek car jo "demand nahi hai", ek pita ka loan. Yahan hain dus sawaal jo families sach mein poochti hain, Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 aur Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke hisaab se jawab ke saath. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1961 ka Act dowry kise kehta hai?

**1. Dowry mein kya-kya aata hai?**

Dowry Prohibition Act shaadi ke silsile mein dono pakshon ke beech di jaane wali property ya keemti cheezon ke baare mein hai, aur yeh teen kaamon ki saza deta hai: dowry dena, lena aur maangna [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Cash, sona, car ya flat, sab dowry ho sakte hain. Families use kya naam deti hain, isse yeh baat nahi badalti.

**2. Saza kya hai?**

Dowry dena, lena ya usme madad karna: kam se kam 5 saal ki jail, aur kam se kam Rs 15,000 ya dowry ki keemat, jo bhi zyada ho, utna fine. Dowry maangna: 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10,000 tak fine [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Kuch bhi na diya gaya ho, tab bhi sirf demand karna crime hai.

## Kya 'gifts' aur dulhan ke maa-baap bhi isme aate hain?

**3. Agar woh ise gift kahein, toh kya yeh dowry hai?**

Naam se faisla nahi hota; demand se hota hai. Kyunki Act dowry maangne ko apne aap mein crime banata hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]], sawaal yeh hai ki kya kuch maanga gaya, "expected" bolkar ishaara kiya gaya, ya rishte ki shart banaya gaya. Gift kehne se demand present nahi ban jaati. "Hum maang nahi rahe, par hamari family mein sab car dete hain" bhi demand ho sakti hai, agar prove ho jaaye.

**4. Kya dulhan ke maa-baap par dowry dene ke liye case chal sakta hai?**

Kagaz par, haan: Act dowry dene par bhi wahi kam se kam paanch saal ki saza rakhta hai jo lene par [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Is wajah se family bolne se darr sakti hai. Complaint karne se pehle kisi Legal Services Authority se free legal advice lijiye ki complaint kaise likhein [[nalsa]]. Jab beti ke saath harassment ho rahi ho, tab is darr se family chup na baithe: demand ke liye harassment uske khilaf crime hai, paise kisi ne bhi diye hon.

## Kya shaadi ke baad ki demand bhi dowry hai?

**5. Shaadi ho gayi, ab unhe car chahiye. Kya yeh bhi dowry hai?**

Haan, aur demand jab bhi aaye, crime hai. Dowry maangna 1961 ke Act ke under offence hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Use ya uski family ko paise dene par majboor karne ke liye, ya na dene ki saza dene ke liye ki gayi harassment BNS ke Section 86 mein cruelty bhi hai, jiski saza Section 85 mein teen saal tak ki jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

**6. Agar harassment ka ant uski maut par ho toh?**

Agar shaadi ke saat saal ke andar kisi aurat ki maut jalne, shareerik chot ya asaamaanya halaat mein hoti hai, aur maut se kuch hi pehle uske saath dowry ke liye cruelty ya harassment hui thi, toh case BNS ke Section 80 mein "dowry death" ban sakta hai, jisme saat saal se life imprisonment tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aise cases ka faisla jaldi nahi hota: 2024 mein courts ne 4,043 dowry-death trials poore kiye, 46.2% mein conviction hua, aur saal ke end tak 59,446 cases (93.6%) pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Dowry aur child marriage ka kya connection hai?

**7. Dowry families ko betiyon ki jaldi shaadi ki taraf kyun dhakelti hai?**

UNFPA batata hai ki jahan dulhan ki family dowry deti hai, wahan kam umar ki dulhan ke liye aam taur par kam dowry deni padti hai, jisse gareeb maa-baap ko betiyon ki shaadi jaldi karne ka lalach milta hai [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. Isi tarah gifts ka ek "rivaaz" kisi ladki ki padhai khatam kar sakta hai. UNICEF kehta hai ki 18 se pehle byaahi gayi ladkiyon ke saath domestic violence hone ki sambhavna zyada hoti hai, aur unke school mein tike rehne ki sambhavna kam [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Aaj zinda jin lagbhag 640 million ladkiyon aur auraton ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi, unme se ek-tihaai India mein hain [[un-sdg-report-2024-goal5]].

**8. Child marriage par law kya kehta hai?**

Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke hisaab se agar dulhan 18 se kam ya dulha 21 se kam umar ka hai, toh woh child marriage hai. Jo adult aadmi kisi bachchi se shaadi karta hai, aur jo bhi shaadi karwata hai ya usme madad karta hai, use 2 saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment aur Rs 1 lakh tak ka fine ho sakta hai; yeh offences cognizable aur non-bailable hain. Bachcha adult hone ke do saal baad tak shaadi ko annul karwa sakta hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Aur 18 se kam umar ki patni ke saath sex rape hai: BNS ka marital exception us par laagu nahi hota [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Child marriage rokne ke liye Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].

## Dowry ke itne kam cases mein conviction kyun hota hai?

**9. Dowry cases mein kitni baar conviction hota hai?**

Bahut kam. 2024 mein police ne Dowry Act ke under 12,343 cases register kiye. Us saal courts ne jo trials poore kiye, unme se 17.4% mein conviction hua, aur saal ke end tak 83,298 cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB yeh record nahi karta ki trials kyun fail hote hain, par drawing room mein baithkar ki gayi demand ka koi nishaan nahi bachta, jab tak koi use likh na le.

**10. Jab pehli demand aaye, tab family kya kare?**

Use saboot ki tarah dekhiye, mol-bhaav ki tarah nahi. Usi din likhiye ki kisne maanga, kya maanga, aur kisne suna; messages aur voice notes save rakhiye. Shaadi ke presents ki likhit list rakhiye, jis par dulhan aur dulhe dono ke sign hon, taaki baad mein saaf rahe ki kya apni marzi se diya gaya. Yaad rakhiye ki dowry ke offences non-bailable aur non-compoundable hain, yaani families aapas mein settle karke case khatam nahi kar sakti [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Agar shaadi ke baad harassment ho, toh ek hi complaint mein Dowry Act aur BNS ke Sections 85 aur 86 dono lagaye ja sakte hain. Aap kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte hain, demand chahe kahin bhi hui ho, ya e-FIR file kar sakte hain [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

fast-track-courts-skip-domestic-crimes.en:
On 4 November 2026 the Union Cabinet gave India's fast-track courts five more years. The Fast Track Special Courts scheme will run until 31 March 2031, with an outlay of Rs 3,788.04 crore and room for up to 850 courts [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. It has one job: rape and POCSO trials. Cruelty by a husband or in-laws, dowry deaths, acid attacks and honour killings were never part of it. This investigation follows those cases into the queue they join instead.

## 779 courts for two kinds of crime

The scheme began on 2 October 2019. By November 2026 it ran 779 courts in 29 states and union territories, 399 of them only for POCSO cases, and they had disposed of 4,02,457 rape and POCSO cases since launch [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. The Centre's share of the new outlay, Rs 2,353.15 crore, comes from the Nirbhaya Fund [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

These courts are no miracle: about 2,45,579 cases were pending before them at the end of 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. But they have what other crimes against women lack: dedicated courtrooms, a dedicated budget, and a count of cases decided that the government reports to Parliament. Under the central scheme, cruelty, dowry deaths and acid attacks have no lane at all.

## 8,54,798 cruelty cases waiting

Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is the largest category of crime against women, with 1,20,227 cases registered in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most reach a court: police charge-sheeted 90.2% of the cruelty cases they disposed of that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The queue is in the courts. In 2024 they had 9,27,199 cruelty cases before them, completed trials in 53,137, convicted in 10,689 (a conviction rate of 20.1%) and ended the year with 8,54,798 still pending, 92.2% of the load [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. By our arithmetic, fewer than 8 in 100 of those cases left the list that year by any route, verdict or compromise. At that pace the backlog alone would take nearly 12 years to clear, even if no new case arrived.

Consider a 26-year-old teacher in Lucknow who files a cruelty complaint against her husband and in-laws under Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced Section 498A of the IPC and carries up to three years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The police file a chargesheet. Then her case joins the line. Every hearing costs her a day's leave and a corridor where she may meet his family.

Rape trials are slow too, with 89.8% pending at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But rape has a lane built to clear it; cruelty does not.

## When compromise outnumbers conviction

In 2024, 16,396 cruelty cases ended in compromise or compounding, more than the 10,689 that ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The data do not say why each was settled. A compromise can be a real reconciliation, a separation with maintenance agreed, or a woman worn down by pressure.

Delay feeds the third kind. A case that waits for years gives the accused's family years to offer money, threaten a custody fight or lean on her parents, and costs her years of leave, fees and fear. A slow court does not have to acquit anyone for the accused to win. It only has to outlast her. If the Lucknow teacher accepts an offer, the file closes and the system counts one more case disposed of.

## Dowry deaths, acid attacks and honour killings in the slow lane

India recorded 5,737 dowry deaths in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], a crime punishable with at least seven years and up to life under Section 80 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Courts had 63,516 dowry-death cases before them that year, completed 4,043 trials and convicted in 1,869, a conviction rate of 46.2%; 59,446 cases, or 93.6%, were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When these trials finish, nearly half end in conviction. The problem is how few finish: at the 2024 pace, the backlog would take nearly 15 years to clear.

Acid attacks are rarer and slower still. Of 804 acid-attack cases on women before the courts in 2024, trials were completed in 24 and 13 ended in conviction; 778, or 96.8%, were pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That backlog would last about 30 years at the same pace, for a crime that carries at least 10 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Honour killings were promised a fast track by the Supreme Court. In Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018), it directed special cells, fast-track and special courts and district monitoring committees; in December 2025 the Delhi High Court was told that no fast-track courts for honour-killing cases had been set up in Delhi [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]].

## What a fast track for the home would need

The data point to four changes.

- **A lane of its own.** Bring dowry deaths, acid attacks and cruelty into the fast-track scheme or a parallel one. The Nirbhaya Fund, which had put Rs 1,234.55 crore into fast-track courts for rape and POCSO cases by July 2026 [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]], exists for women's safety; these are women's-safety crimes.
- **A public count.** Report pending cruelty, dowry-death and acid-attack cases court by court, the way fast-track figures reach Parliament.
- **Protection while she waits.** The 2005 Domestic Violence Act is mainly a civil law, under which a woman can seek protection, residence and maintenance orders from a magistrate, separately from the criminal case [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yet criminal cases under that Act crawl too: of 4,017 before the courts in 2024, trials were completed in 84 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Support that does not wait.** Free legal aid is available through the District Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]], and under NALSA's 2018 scheme an acid-attack survivor must receive Rs 1 lakh within 15 days of her case reaching that authority [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

Speed is not the whole answer. Only 20.1% of completed cruelty trials ended in conviction, so a faster lane also needs stronger investigation and support for women who testify. This is general information, not legal advice.

A fast-track court is a decision about whose cases cannot wait. For now, that decision leaves out the crimes that happen at home.
fast-track-courts-skip-domestic-crimes.hg:
4 November 2026 ko Union Cabinet ne India ke fast-track courts ko paanch saal aur de diye. Fast Track Special Courts scheme ab 31 March 2031 tak chalegi, Rs 3,788.04 crore ke outlay aur 850 courts tak ki gunjaish ke saath [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Iska kaam ek hi hai: rape aur POCSO ke trials. Husband ya sasural walon ki cruelty, dowry deaths, acid attacks aur honour killings is scheme ka hissa kabhi the hi nahi. Yeh investigation un cases ke peechhe us queue tak jaati hai jisme woh iske bajaye khade hote hain.

## 779 courts, sirf do tarah ke crimes ke liye

Scheme 2 October 2019 ko shuru hui thi. November 2026 tak iske under 29 states aur union territories mein 779 courts chal rahe the, jinme se 399 sirf POCSO cases ke liye hain, aur launch se ab tak inhone rape aur POCSO ke 4,02,457 cases dispose kiye hain [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Naye outlay mein Centre ka hissa, Rs 2,353.15 crore, Nirbhaya Fund se aata hai [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

Yeh courts koi chamatkaar nahi hain: 2025 ke end mein inke saamne lagbhag 2,45,579 cases pending the [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Lekin inke paas woh hai jo women ke khilaaf baaki crimes ke paas nahi: apne alag courtrooms, apna alag budget, aur decide hue cases ki aisi ginti jo sarkar Parliament ko batati hai. Central scheme mein cruelty, dowry deaths aur acid attacks ke liye koi lane hai hi nahi.

## 8,54,798 cruelty cases intezaar mein

Husband ya uske rishtedaaron ki cruelty women ke khilaaf crime ki sabse badi category hai: 2024 mein iske 1,20,227 cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Zyada tar court tak pahunchte hain: us saal police ne jitne cruelty cases dispose kiye, unme se 90.2% mein chargesheet file hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Queue courts mein hai. 2024 mein unke saamne 9,27,199 cruelty cases the. Trial 53,137 mein poora hua, conviction 10,689 mein hui (conviction rate 20.1%), aur saal ke end mein 8,54,798 cases ab bhi pending the, yaani poore load ka 92.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Hamare hisaab se, us saal har 100 mein se 8 se bhi kam cases list se bahar nikle, chahe verdict se ya compromise se. Is raftaar se sirf backlog khaali hone mein lagbhag 12 saal lagenge, tab bhi jab ek bhi naya case na aaye.

Sochiye, Lucknow ki ek 26 saal ki teacher apne husband aur sasural walon ke khilaaf Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 85 ke under cruelty ki complaint karti hai. Yeh section IPC ke Section 498A ki jagah aaya hai aur isme teen saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police chargesheet file kar deti hai. Phir uska case line mein lag jaata hai. Har hearing ka matlab hai ek din ki chhutti, aur ek aisa corridor jahan uska saamna husband ke parivaar se ho sakta hai.

Rape trials bhi slow hain: 2024 ke end mein 89.8% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lekin rape ke paas ek aisi lane hai jo backlog nikaalne ke liye hi bani hai; cruelty ke paas nahi.

## Jab compromise conviction se aage nikal jaaye

2024 mein 16,396 cruelty cases compromise ya compounding pe khatam hue, jo conviction pe khatam hue 10,689 cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data yeh nahi batata ki har case kyun settle hua. Compromise ek sachchi sulah ho sakti hai, maintenance tay karke hui separation ho sakti hai, ya pressure se thak chuki ek woman ka haar maan lena ho sakta hai.

Deri is teesri kism ko badhaati hai. Jo case saalon wait karta hai, woh accused ke parivaar ko saalon ka waqt deta hai: paisa offer karne ka, custody ki ladaai ki dhamki dene ka, uske maa-baap pe dabaav daalne ka. Aur us woman se saalon ki chhutti, fees aur darr vasool karta hai. Accused ke jeetne ke liye slow court ko kisi ko acquit karna zaroori nahi. Court ko bas us woman se zyada der tak tike rehna hota hai. Agar Lucknow ki teacher koi offer maan le, toh file band ho jaati hai aur system ek aur case ko "disposed" gin leta hai.

## Dowry deaths, acid attacks aur honour killings slow lane mein

India mein 2024 mein 5,737 dowry deaths record hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Section 80 ke under is crime ki saza kam se kam saat saal aur umr qaid tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Us saal courts ke saamne dowry death ke 63,516 cases the; trial 4,043 mein poora hua aur conviction 1,869 mein hui, yaani conviction rate 46.2%; 59,446 cases, ya 93.6%, ab bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab yeh trials poore hote hain, toh lagbhag aadhe conviction pe khatam hote hain. Problem yeh hai ki poore bahut kam hote hain: 2024 ki raftaar se backlog khaali hone mein lagbhag 15 saal lagenge.

Acid attacks kam hote hain, aur unke trials aur bhi slow hain. 2024 mein courts ke saamne women pe acid attack ke 804 cases the; trial 24 mein poora hua aur 13 mein conviction hui; saal ke end mein 778, yaani 96.8%, pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isi raftaar se yeh backlog lagbhag 30 saal chalega, woh bhi ek aise crime ke liye jisme kam se kam 10 saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Honour killings ke liye fast track ka promise khud Supreme Court ne kiya tha. Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018) mein usne special cells, fast-track aur special courts aur district monitoring committees ka direction diya tha; December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ko bataya gaya ki Delhi mein honour-killing cases ke liye koi fast-track court bana hi nahi tha [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]].

## Ghar ke crimes ke fast track ko kya chahiye

Data chaar badlaavon ki taraf ishaara karta hai.

- **Apni alag lane.** Dowry deaths, acid attacks aur cruelty ko fast-track scheme mein ya uske jaisi kisi parallel scheme mein laaya jaaye. Nirbhaya Fund, jisse July 2026 tak rape aur POCSO ke fast-track courts mein Rs 1,234.55 crore lag chuke the [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]], women ki safety ke liye hi bana hai; yeh bhi women ki safety ke hi crimes hain.
- **Public ginti.** Pending cruelty, dowry-death aur acid-attack cases ka hisaab court-wise diya jaaye, jaise fast-track ke figures Parliament tak pahunchte hain.
- **Intezaar ke dauraan protection.** 2005 ka Domestic Violence Act zyada tar ek civil law hai, jiske under woman criminal case se alag, magistrate se protection, residence aur maintenance orders maang sakti hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Phir bhi is Act ke criminal cases bhi rengte hain: 2024 mein courts ke saamne aise 4,017 cases the, aur trial sirf 84 mein poora hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Support jo wait na kare.** District Legal Services Authority ke through free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]], aur NALSA ki 2018 ki scheme ke under acid-attack survivor ko, case us authority tak pahunchne ke 15 din ke andar, Rs 1 lakh milna zaroori hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

Speed poora jawaab nahi hai. Poore hue cruelty trials mein se sirf 20.1% conviction pe khatam hue, isliye tez lane ke saath behtar investigation aur gawahi dene wali women ke liye support bhi chahiye. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Fast-track court asal mein ek faisla hai ki kiske cases wait nahi kar sakte. Filhaal yeh faisla un crimes ko bahar rakhta hai jo ghar ke andar hote hain.

financial-abuse-dowry-demands-marriage.en:
Consider this situation. A 27-year-old schoolteacher in Indore hands her debit card to her husband in the first month of marriage, because "that is how it is done in this house". She has to ask for money to buy sanitary pads. Two years on, her father is still paying for the car her in-laws asked for at the wedding, and now they want a flat. Nobody has hit her. She is still being abused. Economic abuse is rarely named as abuse in Indian families, yet the law already reaches more of it than most families know. This explainer is general information, not legal advice.

## What economic abuse looks like

The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts economic abuse as domestic violence, alongside physical, sexual, verbal and emotional abuse. It covers depriving a woman of money or resources she is entitled to, including her stridhan; disposing of her valuables or property; and cutting off her access to things she is entitled to use, including the shared home [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

In daily life it looks like this:

- her salary goes into an account she cannot see, or her card and PIN stay with her husband or a parent-in-law;
- her wedding jewellery is "kept safe" in a locker she has no key to;
- she is made to quit her job, or not allowed to take one;
- she has no money of her own for a bus ticket, a phone recharge or a doctor;
- loans are taken in her name, or she signs papers she has not read;
- her parents are asked for money again and again, long after the wedding.

Each item can pass as family management. The test is choice: can she spend, save and leave without anyone's permission?

## 41.7% and 10.8%: why so many wives have no money of their own

Control is easy when a woman has no income. In 2023-24, 41.7% of Indian women aged 15 and above were in the labour force, against 78.8% of men; in cities, only 28.0% of women were [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].

Being counted as working is not the same as being paid. In July-September 2025, only 10.8% of employed rural women had a regular wage or salaried job. Another 37.5% worked on their own account or as employers, and 34.2% were helpers in household enterprises [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]], the survey's term for unpaid family workers on a family farm or in a family business.

So a woman can work in the fields all day and still not have a rupee she can call her own. When leaving a marriage means having nowhere to live and nothing to live on, whoever holds the money holds the exit.

## Demands after the wedding: still dowry, still a crime

The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 defines dowry as property or valuable security given or agreed to be given in connection with the marriage, before the wedding, at it, or any time after it [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. A car demanded on the first Diwali, a flat "for the couple" or money to rescue the husband's business can all be dowry if they are tied to the marriage.

Demanding dowry, directly or indirectly, is punishable with six months to two years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 10,000. Giving or taking it carries at least five years and a fine of at least Rs 15,000 or the dowry's value, whichever is more. These offences are non-bailable [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

Police registered 12,343 cases under the Act in 2024, most in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Karnataka; West Bengal registered none and Maharashtra 12 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That reflects police practice, not an absence of dowry.

## Section 86, the Domestic Violence Act and which law fits

When demands come with harassment, criminal law steps in. Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty with up to three years in prison and a fine, and Section 86 defines cruelty to include harassment meant to force her or her family to meet an unlawful demand for property [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 1,20,227 cases of this cruelty, formerly Section 498A of the IPC, in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The Domestic Violence Act works differently. It is mainly civil: a magistrate can order the abuse to stop, keep her in the shared home and make the abuser pay, and a protection order can stop him operating joint bank accounts or touching her stridhan [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. A police case under it is possible only for breaking an order or for a Protection Officer failing in duty, so police registered just 616 criminal cases under it in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

| Situation | Law that fits |
|---|---|
| Money, a car or a flat demanded from her parents, even after the wedding | Dowry Prohibition Act: demanding dowry |
| She is harassed or hurt because a demand was not met | Sections 85 and 86 BNS: cruelty |
| Her salary, card, jewellery or stridhan is taken, or she is kept without money | Domestic Violence Act: protection order and monetary relief |
| She is told to leave the marital home | Domestic Violence Act: residence order |
| She dies in abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, after dowry-linked cruelty soon before her death | Section 80 BNS: dowry death |

These routes can run together, and a Domestic Violence Act application does not need a police case first.

## Protecting your own money: first steps

Economic control tightens slowly, so the first steps are small and private:

- Keep one bank account in your name only, with your own phone number and email for alerts.
- Keep copies of your Aadhaar, PAN, bank passbook, degree certificates and marriage papers outside the house, with someone you trust or in a secure online folder.
- Photograph your jewellery and stridhan, and save proof of every demand, with dates.
- Tell one person outside the marital home what is happening.

The Women Helpline and the district One Stop Centre can connect you to counselling, legal aid and shelter [[wcd-mission-shakti]], and the District Legal Services Authority gives free legal aid [[nalsa]]. Parents can help most by recording every demand and payment, and by telling their daughter plainly that she can come home.
financial-abuse-dowry-demands-marriage.hg:
Sochiye. Indore ki 27 saal ki ek school teacher shaadi ke pehle hi mahine apna debit card pati ko de deti hai, kyunki "is ghar mein aise hi hota hai". Sanitary pads khareedne ke liye bhi use paise maangne padte hain. Do saal baad bhi uske papa us car ke paise bhar rahe hain jo sasural walon ne shaadi mein maangi thi, aur ab unhe flat chahiye. Kisi ne use haath nahi lagaya. Phir bhi uske saath abuse ho raha hai. Indian families mein economic abuse ko shaayad hi kabhi abuse kaha jaata hai, jabki law isme se jitna cover karta hai, utna zyada tar families jaanti bhi nahi. Yeh explainer general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Economic abuse kaisa dikhta hai

Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 economic abuse ko domestic violence maanta hai, physical, sexual, verbal aur emotional abuse ke saath. Isme aata hai: aurat ko us paise ya resources se mehroom rakhna jiski woh haqdaar hai, uska stridhan bhi; uske qeemti saamaan ya property ko bech dena ya hata dena; aur un cheezon tak uski pahunch kaat dena jinhe istemaal karne ka use haq hai, shared ghar bhi [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Roz ki zindagi mein yeh aisa dikhta hai:

- uski salary aise account mein jaati hai jo woh dekh nahi sakti, ya uska card aur PIN pati ya saas-sasur ke paas rehta hai;
- shaadi ke gehne ek locker mein "safe rakhe" hain jiski chaabi uske paas nahi;
- use naukri chhodne par majboor kiya jaata hai, ya naukri karne hi nahi di jaati;
- bus ticket, phone recharge ya doctor ke liye bhi uske paas apna paisa nahi hota;
- uske naam par loan liye jaate hain, ya use bina padhe kaagaz sign karne padte hain;
- shaadi ke kaafi baad bhi uske maa-baap se baar-baar paise maange jaate hain.

Har baat ko "ghar ka hisaab-kitaab" bolkar chalaya ja sakta hai. Asli test choice ka hai: kya woh kisi ki permission ke bina kharch kar sakti hai, bacha sakti hai, aur ghar chhod sakti hai?

## 41.7% aur 10.8%: itni biwiyon ke paas apna paisa kyun nahi hota

Jab aurat ki apni kamai na ho, toh control aasaan ho jaata hai. 2023-24 mein 15 saal se upar ki 41.7% Indian auratein labour force mein thi, jabki mard 78.8%; shehron mein toh sirf 28.0% auratein [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].
