Koi bhi police station cognizable offence record karega, chahe woh kahin bhi hua ho; electronic complaint ko teen din ke andar sign karna hota hai; aur FIR ki copy free milti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Kyunki cruelty mein teen saal tak ki saza hai, police Deputy Superintendent ki permission se FIR se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar station mana kare, toh Superintendent of Police ko likhiye, phir magistrate ke paas jaiye.

Civil raasta bhi istemaal kijiye. Magistrate ko Domestic Violence Act ki application, Protection Officer, lawyer ya One Stop Centre ke zariye, abuse rukwa sakti hai aur use apne ghar mein rehne de sakti hai, criminal trial ka intezaar kiye bina [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Maa-baap, compromise ki jaldi mat kijiye. 2024 mein court mein cruelty ke 16,396 cases compromise par khatam hue, jo conviction wale 10,689 cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme se kuch sachche suleh the; data yeh nahi bata sakta ki kitne aurat par dabaav ka nateeja the. Apni beti se poochiye ki woh kya chahti hai, aur use bataiye ki woh ghar laut sakti hai.

india-has-no-femicide-count.en:
Every year the United Nations tries to count the women and girls killed by the people closest to them. For 2024, UNODC and UN Women put the number at about 50,000 worldwide: 60% of the roughly 83,000 women and girls killed intentionally that year, or 137 a day [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. India's crime records cannot answer that question. They count legal categories, not women killed by a husband, father, brother or in-laws. So any estimate for India has to lean on a stand-in, and the obvious one is dowry deaths.

## What a femicide count is, and why India has none

The UN briefs estimate "intimate partner/family member femicides": intentional killings of women and girls by a partner or relative [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Counting them needs three facts recorded together for every death. It was a killing. The person killed was female. The killer was her partner or family.

India's National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) records crimes by legal section, and counts each FIR only once, under the offence with the heaviest punishment: the "principal offence rule" [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Its tables show murders, dowry deaths and a list of murder motives. The motive table does not even give the victim's sex [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and no single column answers the plain question: how many women were killed by a partner or relative? India is not alone in looking away: the number of countries reporting such data peaked at 75 in 2020 and had halved by 2023 [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

## 59% by relatives: killing at home is a family matter

In Europe, 64% of women killed in the private sphere in 2023 were killed by a partner. Outside Europe and the Americas, in the countries with data, 59% were killed by other family members and 41% by partners [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. The gap between the sexes is starker still. Men and boys were 80% of the world's homicide victims in 2024, yet only 11% of male victims were killed by a partner or relative, against almost 60% of female victims. In Asia the share for women was 55% [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]].

In an Indian home, "family" can mean a husband, but also a mother-in-law, a father or a brother. Consider a hypothetical: a 22-year-old is killed by her own family for choosing whom to marry. To the UN, hers is a femicide. In India's tables it can be an "honour killing", a murder over "love affairs" or a murder with some other motive, depending on what the investigating officer writes down.

## Dowry deaths as the UN's stand-in

Where a country does not report these killings, UNODC and UN Women build estimates from related offences, such as dowry death and honour killing, wherever national law defines them [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Indian law defines one of them. Under Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), earlier Section 304B IPC, a woman's death by burns, injury or in abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, after dowry-linked cruelty, is a "dowry death" [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The stand-in is big. UNODC found that dowry deaths made up 40% to 50% of all female homicides recorded in India every year from 1999 to 2016 [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]]. In 2024 police registered 5,737 dowry-death cases with 5,811 victims, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. But a stand-in is not a count. It catches married women, in their first seven years of marriage, where dowry cruelty can be shown, and only when police register the death that way. It also takes in some deaths that are not murders in the narrow sense, UNODC notes [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]].

## Why the columns cannot be added up

| Column in Crime in India 2024 | Count | What it really counts |
|---|---|---|
| Dowry deaths (Section 80 BNS / 304B IPC) | 5,737 cases | Deaths within seven years of marriage after dowry cruelty |
| Murders, motive "dowry" | 701 | Murder cases, counted apart from dowry deaths |
| Murders, motive "honour killing" | 36 | Murder cases; the victim's sex is not given |
| Murders, motive "witchcraft" | 54 | Murder cases; the victim's sex is not given |

All four figures are NCRB's [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Adding them would be wrong, for three reasons.

They are different units. A dowry death is an offence; "dowry", "honour killing" and "witchcraft" are motives police record on murder cases, and the motive table does not give the victim's sex [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Witch-hunting is widely reported to target women, often widows, yet nobody can say how many of the 54 witchcraft murders were femicides.

Each FIR sits in one column only. A dowry killing charged as murder moves to the murder table [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Murders with a dowry motive fell from 1,171 in 2020 to 701 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], but nobody knows how many dowry killings went into other columns instead.

And the labels leak. Police recorded 36 honour killings in all of India in 2024, against 1,391 murders over "love affairs" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB shows no honour killing in Tamil Nadu from 2020 to 2023 and one in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], yet the Madras High Court observed in June 2026 that the state had seen 59 in 10 years [[livelaw-madras-hc-honour-killings-2026]]. In April 2025 the Supreme Court overturned orders that let an alleged honour killing be tried as culpable homicide instead of murder, calling it "a clear case of honour killing" [[barandbench-honour-killing-lesser-charge-2025]]. A lighter charge means a different column. And deaths that police log as suicide or accident may never become dowry deaths at all.

Across thousands of cases, nobody can say how many women in India were killed by their own families in a year.

## What a national femicide measure would need

India does not need a new law to count. It needs columns:

- **the victim's sex and her relationship to the killer** on every murder and culpable-homicide record, published together;
- **a femicide flag that stays with the case**, whether it is booked as murder, dowry death or a lesser charge;
- **victims, not only FIRs**, in the motive tables, by sex and age;
- **a link to earlier complaints.** In France, South Africa and Colombia, between 22% and 37% of women killed by partners had already reported violence by them, which UNODC and UN Women read as a sign that many such killings are preventable [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. India registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by husbands or their relatives in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], but it cannot say how many women who were later killed had filed one.

Until then, any estimate for India will lean on its dowry deaths. And a woman killed by her own family for any other reason will be missing twice: from her home, and from the record.
india-has-no-femicide-count.hg:
Har saal United Nations (UN) un auraton aur ladkiyon ko ginne ki koshish karta hai jinhe unke sabse kareebi logon ne maar diya. 2024 ke liye UNODC aur UN Women ka estimate hai ki duniya bhar mein lagbhag 50,000 aisi hatyaein hui: us saal jaan-boojhkar maari gayi qareeb 83,000 auraton aur ladkiyon ka 60%, yaani roz 137 [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. India ke crime records is sawaal ka jawab nahi de sakte. Woh legal categories ginte hain, yeh nahi ki kitni auraton ko pati, pita, bhai ya sasural walon ne maara. Isliye India ka koi bhi estimate kisi proxy par tikta hai, aur sabse seedha proxy hai dowry deaths.

## Femicide count kya hota hai, aur India ke paas kyun nahi hai

UN ke briefs "intimate partner/family member femicides" ka estimate dete hain: auraton aur ladkiyon ki woh jaan-boojhkar ki gayi hatyaein jo partner ya kisi rishtedaar ne ki [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Inhe ginne ke liye har maut ke baare mein teen baatein ek saath record honi chahiye. Yeh hatya thi. Jo maari gayi, woh female thi. Maarne wala uska partner ya family member tha.

India ka National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) crimes ko legal section ke hisaab se record karta hai, aur har FIR ko sirf ek baar ginta hai, us offence ke under jiski saza sabse bhaari ho: yahi hai "principal offence rule" [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Uski tables mein murders hain, dowry deaths hain, aur murder ke motives ki ek list hai. Motive wali table toh victim ka sex tak nahi batati [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur koi ek column is seedhe sawaal ka jawab nahi deta: kitni auraton ko partner ya rishtedaar ne maara? Aur nazar pherne wala akela India nahi hai: aisa data report karne wale deshon ki ginti 2020 mein 75 tak pahunchi, aur 2023 tak aadhi reh gayi [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

## 59% rishtedaron ke haathon: ghar mein hatya family ka maamla hai

Europe mein 2023 mein ghar ke daayre mein (private sphere mein) maari gayi auraton mein se 64% ko partner ne maara. Europe aur Americas ke bahar, jin deshon ka data maujood hai, wahan 59% ko doosre family members ne maara aur 41% ko partners ne [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. Mardon aur auraton ke beech ka fark aur bhi tez hai. 2024 mein duniya ke homicide victims mein 80% mard aur ladke the, phir bhi male victims mein se sirf 11% partner ya rishtedaar ke haathon maare gaye, jabki female victims mein yeh hissa lagbhag 60% tha. Asia mein auraton ke liye yeh hissa 55% tha [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]].

Ek Indian ghar mein "family" ka matlab pati ho sakta hai, par saas, pita ya bhai bhi. Ek hypothetical sochiye: ek 22 saal ki ladki ko uski apni family maar deti hai, kyunki usne khud chuna ki woh kisse shaadi karegi. UN ke liye yeh femicide hai. India ki tables mein yeh "honour killing" ho sakti hai, "love affairs" wala murder ho sakta hai, ya kisi aur motive wala murder. Sab is par depend karta hai ki investigating officer kya likhta hai.

## Dowry deaths: UN ka proxy

Jahan koi desh aisi hatyaein report nahi karta, wahan UNODC aur UN Women milte-julte offences se estimate banate hain, jaise dowry death aur honour killing, jahan bhi us desh ka kanoon unhe define karta ho [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2024]]. Indian kanoon inmein se ek ko define karta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 80 ke under, jo pehle IPC ki Section 304B thi, agar kisi aurat ki maut shaadi ke saat saal ke andar jalne se, chot se ya kisi abnormal halaat mein ho, aur usse pehle dahej ko lekar cruelty hui ho, toh woh "dowry death" hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh proxy chhota nahi hai. UNODC ne paaya ki 1999 se 2016 tak har saal India mein darj auraton ki hatyaon mein 40% se 50% dowry deaths thi [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]]. 2024 mein police ne 5,737 dowry-death cases register kiye, jinmein 5,811 victims the, yaani roz qareeb 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Par proxy count nahi hota. Yeh shaadishuda auraton ko pakadta hai, woh bhi shaadi ke pehle saat saal mein, jahan dahej wali cruelty dikhayi ja sake, aur tabhi jab police us maut ko isi tarah register kare. UNODC yeh bhi note karta hai ki ismein kuch aisi mautein bhi aa jaati hain jo strict matlab mein murder nahi hain [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]].

## Yeh columns jode kyun nahi ja sakte

| Crime in India 2024 ka column | Count | Asal mein yeh kya ginta hai |
|---|---|---|
| Dowry deaths (Section 80 BNS / 304B IPC) | 5,737 cases | Shaadi ke saat saal ke andar, dahej cruelty ke baad hui mautein |
| Murders, motive "dowry" | 701 | Murder cases, dowry deaths se alag gine gaye |
| Murders, motive "honour killing" | 36 | Murder cases; victim ka sex nahi diya gaya |
| Murders, motive "witchcraft" | 54 | Murder cases; victim ka sex nahi diya gaya |

Chaaron figures NCRB ke hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inhe jodna galat hoga, teen wajahon se.

Pehli wajah: yeh alag-alag units hain. Dowry death ek offence hai; "dowry", "honour killing" aur "witchcraft" woh motives hain jo police murder cases par likhti hai, aur motive wali table victim ka sex nahi batati [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Witch-hunting ke baare mein bahut report hota hai ki iska nishana auratein banti hain, aksar widows, phir bhi koi nahi bata sakta ki 54 witchcraft murders mein se kitne femicide the.

Doosri wajah: har FIR sirf ek column mein baithti hai. Dahej ke liye hui hatya agar murder ke roop mein charge hui, toh woh murder table mein chali jaati hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Dahej motive wale murders 2020 mein 1,171 the aur 2024 mein ghatkar 701 reh gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], par kisi ko nahi pata ki kitni dahej hatyaein iske bajaye doosre columns mein chali gayi.

Teesri wajah: labels leak hote hain. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne sirf 36 honour killings darj ki, jabki "love affairs" ki wajah se 1,391 murders darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB ke hisaab se Tamil Nadu mein 2020 se 2023 tak ek bhi honour killing nahi hui aur 2024 mein sirf ek [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jabki Madras High Court ne June 2026 mein kaha ki state mein 10 saal mein 59 honour killings hui hain [[livelaw-madras-hc-honour-killings-2026]]. April 2025 mein Supreme Court ne un orders ko palat diya jinmein ek kathit honour killing ka trial murder ke bajaye culpable homicide ke taur par chalne diya gaya tha, aur kaha ki yeh "a clear case of honour killing" hai [[barandbench-honour-killing-lesser-charge-2025]]. Halka charge, matlab alag column. Aur jin mauton ko police suicide ya accident likh deti hai, woh shayad kabhi dowry death bante hi nahi.

Hazaaron cases mein yahi hota hai, aur nateeja yeh ki koi nahi bata sakta ki ek saal mein India mein kitni auraton ko unki apni family ne maara.

## National femicide count ke liye kya chahiye

India ko ginne ke liye naya kanoon nahi chahiye. Columns chahiye:

- **victim ka sex aur maarne wale se uska rishta**, har murder aur culpable-homicide record par, dono ek saath publish hon;
- **ek femicide flag jo case ke saath chale**, chahe case murder mein book ho, dowry death mein ya kisi halke charge mein;
- **sirf FIRs nahi, victims bhi**, motive tables mein, sex aur umar ke hisaab se;
- **pichhli complaints se link.** France, South Africa aur Colombia mein partner ke haathon maari gayi auraton mein se 22% se 37% pehle hi us partner ki violence report kar chuki thi, aur UNODC aur UN Women ise is baat ka sanket maante hain ki aisi kai hatyaein roki ja sakti hain [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]]. India ne 2024 mein pati ya uske rishtedaron ki cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], par woh yeh nahi bata sakta ki baad mein maari gayi auraton mein se kitno ne pehle aisi complaint ki thi.

Tab tak India ka har estimate uske dowry deaths par hi tika rahega. Aur jis aurat ko uski apni family kisi aur wajah se maar de, woh do jagah se gaayab rahegi: apne ghar se, aur record se.

india-partner-violence-south-asia-neighb.en:
Ask why so many Indian husbands hit their wives and someone will say it is culture: the joint family, dowry, the idea that a bride now belongs to her in-laws. Then look next door. The World Health Organization's newest estimates let us set India beside six of its neighbours, and countries whose languages, religions and wedding customs overlap differ nearly threefold [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. If violence at home were simply "our culture", neighbours who share so much of it would land close together. They do not.

## Afghanistan 50.9% to Sri Lanka 17.2%

The figures below are WHO's 2023 estimates for women aged 15-49 who have ever been married or had a partner. "Lifetime" means physical or sexual violence by a husband or partner at any point. "Past 12 months" means in the year before the survey [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

| Country | Lifetime | Past 12 months |
|---|---|---|
| Afghanistan | 50.9% | 39.7% |
| Bangladesh | 48.9% | 15.7% |
| India | 29.9% | 22.4% |
| Nepal | 26.1% | 12.3% |
| Pakistan | 24.8% | 13.1% |
| Sri Lanka | 17.2% | 8.0% |

Bhutan sits beside Sri Lanka, at 17.6% lifetime and 5.9% in the past year [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Imagine two women married in the same month, one in Kolkata and one in Dhaka. They speak the same language, sing the same wedding songs and may have grown up on the same films. Their countries' lifetime figures are 29.9% and 48.9%. Whatever drives that difference, it is not language or song.

India's middle place on the lifetime column hides something worse. For violence in the past 12 months, India's 22.4% is second only to Afghanistan in South Asia [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India's past-year figure is not far below its lifetime one, which suggests that for many Indian women who have faced this violence, it is not a memory. It is still going on. And it stays hidden: in India's own health survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Southern Asia's recent-violence rank

Taken together, the region stands above the world. In Southern Asia, 31.2% of women aged 15-49 who have had a partner have faced violence from one in their lifetime, and 20.5% in the past year, against global averages of 25.8% and 13.7% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India, by far the most populous country in the group, weighs heavily in that regional figure.

WHO's release of 19 November 2025 put Southern Asia second in its list of regions for recent partner violence, behind only Oceania excluding Australia and New Zealand: 19% of women aged 15 and older who have had a partner faced it in the past 12 months, against 38% there and 11% worldwide [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]]. That list covers only broad regions and a few subregions; in WHO's full report and the UN's SDG database, some small Pacific subregions also sit above Southern Asia.

WHO also names India in the group of countries with the highest past-year rates anywhere, and Afghanistan is the only other South Asian country in that group [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## Why the comparison needs care

These are modelled estimates, and WHO publishes an uncertainty range around each one. For India's lifetime figure, that range runs from 24.4% to 36.4% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Nepal (26.1%) and Pakistan (24.8%) fall inside it, so ranking India against them is guesswork. The ranges for Bangladesh and Sri Lanka do not overlap India's, which is why the gaps at the two ends of the table are more than noise.

Surveys also ask differently. Discussing sexual violence data, WHO notes that dedicated surveys on violence against women draw more disclosure than short modules inside broader surveys, and that this, with stigma and the range of acts asked about, limits comparisons between countries [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India's National Family Health Survey (NFHS) uses exactly such a module.

A low number can mean less violence, or less telling. WHO says women in more gender-equal societies are more likely to disclose sexual violence, which raises the measured level, while where stigma is high and services are few, the real level of sexual violence by non-partners is likely much higher than the estimate [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Finally, do not compare rounds. WHO's previous estimates, for 2018, put India at 35% lifetime and 18% in the past year [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. The fall to 29.9% does not show progress, and the rise to 22.4% does not show that things got worse: WHO says the 2023 estimates are not comparable with earlier rounds, because methods and data changed [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## If neighbours differ, change is possible

Careful reading does not erase the main finding. Inside India the spread is even wider. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 44.4% of ever-married women in Karnataka reported physical or sexual violence by a husband, against 6.5% in Nagaland and 1.3% in Lakshadweep [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Same Constitution, same criminal law, very different homes. Our state-by-state reading of the survey and police data looks at these gaps more closely.

The risk factors the survey finds are things that can move. Of women whose husbands often get drunk, 71% reported physical or sexual violence by their husband, against 23% of women whose husbands do not drink. Husbands with 12 or more years of schooling were half as likely as those with none to commit physical, sexual or emotional violence, 22% against 43% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. These are associations, not proof of cause, but neither factor is fixed by birth or faith.

"Custom" has moved before. Child marriage was defended as tradition too. The share of Indian women aged 20-24 married before 18 fell from 47.4% in 2005-06 [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]] to 20.1% in 2023-24 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], and the UN says the worldwide fall in child marriage came largely from progress in Southern Asia [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]].

Violence by partners is falling far more slowly. Worldwide it has declined by only about 0.2% a year over two decades [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. In 2022, programmes to prevent violence against women received just 0.2% of global development aid, and WHO says that funding fell further in 2025 [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]].

Sri Lanka's figure is not a miracle, and Bangladesh's is not fate. WHO's tables cannot say what drives each country's number. But the gap answers one question: a husband's violence is not a fixed part of South Asian life. On the lifetime measure, India sits in the middle of its neighbours. Which way it moves depends on what its families, schools, police and governments choose to do.
india-partner-violence-south-asia-neighb.hg:
Kisi se poochiye ki India mein itne husbands apni wife par haath kyun uthate hain, toh aksar jawab milega: "Yeh toh hamara culture hai." Joint family, dowry, aur yeh soch ki shaadi ke baad bahu sasural ki ho gayi. Ab zara padosi deshon ko dekhiye. World Health Organization (WHO) ke naye estimates se India ko uske chhe padosiyon ke saath ek hi table par rakh kar dekh sakte hain. In deshon ki bhashayein, dharm aur shaadi ke rivaaz kaafi had tak milte-julte hain. Phir bhi inke numbers mein qareeb teen guna ka farq hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Agar ghar ki violence bas "hamara culture" hoti, toh ek jaise culture wale padosi aas-paas hi hote. Aisa nahi hai.

## Afghanistan 50.9% se Sri Lanka 17.2% tak

Neeche WHO ke 2023 ke estimates hain, 15 se 49 saal ki un auraton ke liye jinki kabhi shaadi hui ya koi partner raha. "Lifetime" ka matlab hai ki husband ya partner ne kabhi bhi physical ya sexual violence ki. "Pichhle 12 mahine" ka matlab hai survey se theek pehle ka ek saal [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

| Desh | Lifetime | Pichhle 12 mahine |
|---|---|---|
| Afghanistan | 50.9% | 39.7% |
| Bangladesh | 48.9% | 15.7% |
| India | 29.9% | 22.4% |
| Nepal | 26.1% | 12.3% |
| Pakistan | 24.8% | 13.1% |
| Sri Lanka | 17.2% | 8.0% |

Bhutan Sri Lanka ke paas hai: lifetime 17.6% aur pichhle saal 5.9% [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Sochiye, do auraton ki shaadi ek hi mahine mein hui. Ek ki Kolkata mein, doosri ki Dhaka mein. Dono ek hi bhasha bolti hain. Dono ki shaadi mein ek jaise geet gaaye gaye. Shayad dono ek jaisi films dekhkar badi huin. Phir bhi unke deshon ka lifetime number 29.9% aur 48.9% hai. Yeh farq bhasha ya geeton se nahi aaya.

Table mein India beech mein dikhta hai, par iske peeche ek buri baat chhupi hai. Pichhle 12 mahine ki violence mein India ka 22.4% South Asia mein sirf Afghanistan se peeche hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India mein pichhle saal wala number lifetime wale se bahut kam nahi hai. Isse lagta hai ki jin auraton ne yeh violence jheli, unmein se kai ke liye yeh purani yaad nahi hai. Yeh ab bhi chal rahi hai. Aur yeh chhupi bhi rehti hai. India ke apne health survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein, physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% auraton ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Recent violence mein Southern Asia ki ranking

Poore region ko saath dekhein, toh yeh duniya se upar hai. Southern Asia mein 15-49 saal ki jin auraton ka kabhi partner raha, unmein se 31.2% ne zindagi mein kabhi uski violence jheli, aur 20.5% ne pichhle ek saal mein. Duniya ka average 25.8% aur 13.7% hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Is group mein sabse zyada aabaadi India ki hai, isliye is regional number par sabse bhaari asar bhi India ka hai.

WHO ne yeh estimates 19 November 2025 ko release kiye, aur saath mein regions ki ek ranking di ki recent partner violence kahan sabse zyada hai. Usmein Southern Asia doosre number par tha. Aage sirf Oceania tha, Australia aur New Zealand ko chhodkar. Southern Asia mein 15 saal aur usse upar ki jin auraton ka kabhi partner raha, unmein se 19% ne pichhle 12 mahine mein aisi violence jheli. Pacific ke us hisse mein yeh 38% tha, aur poori duniya mein 11% [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]]. Par yeh list sirf bade regions aur kuch subregions ko compare karti hai; WHO ki poori report aur UN ke SDG database mein Pacific ke kuch chhote subregions bhi Southern Asia se upar hain.

WHO India ka naam un deshon mein bhi leta hai jahan pichhle saal ki violence duniya mein sabse zyada hai. South Asia se us group mein India ke alawa sirf Afghanistan hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## Comparison mein savdhaani kyun zaroori hai

Yeh numbers ek model se nikale gaye estimates hain, aur WHO har number ke saath ek uncertainty range bhi deta hai. India ke lifetime number ki range 24.4% se 36.4% tak hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Nepal (26.1%) aur Pakistan (24.8%) isi range ke andar aate hain. Isliye India ko inse upar ya neeche rakhna bas andaaza hai. Par Bangladesh aur Sri Lanka ki range India ki range se nahi milti. Isliye table ke dono siron par jo farq hai, woh sirf ittefaaq nahi hai.

Surveys ka sawaal poochne ka tareeka bhi alag hota hai. Sexual violence ke data ke baare mein likhte hue WHO kehta hai ki jo surveys sirf auraton par violence ke liye bante hain, unmein auratein zyada khulkar batati hain. Bade surveys ke andar ke chhote module mein kam batati hain. Iske saath stigma, aur kis-kis tarah ki violence ke baare mein poocha gaya, in sab se deshon ka comparison mushkil hota hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. India ka National Family Health Survey (NFHS) theek aisa hi module use karta hai.

Kam number ka matlab kam violence bhi ho sakta hai, aur kam batana bhi. WHO kehta hai ki jin samaajon mein aurat aur mard mein barabari zyada hai, wahan auratein sexual violence ke baare mein zyada batati hain, isliye wahan measured number badh jaata hai. Jahan stigma zyada hai aur madad kam milti hai, wahan partner ke alawa doosron ki sexual violence ka asli level estimate se kahin zyada hone ki sambhavna hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Aakhri baat: purane aur naye rounds ko aapas mein compare mat kijiye. WHO ke pichhle estimate (2018 ke liye) mein India ka lifetime number 35% aur pichhle saal ka 18% tha [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2021]]. 29.9% tak girna progress nahi dikhata, aur 22.4% tak badhna yeh nahi dikhata ki haalat bigad gaye. WHO khud kehta hai ki 2023 ke estimates purane rounds se compare nahi ho sakte, kyunki method aur data dono badal gaye [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## Padosi alag hain, toh badlaav mumkin hai

Savdhaani se padhne par bhi asli baat nahi badalti. India ke andar toh farq aur bhi bada hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein Karnataka ki 44.4% shaadishuda auraton ne husband ki physical ya sexual violence batayi. Nagaland mein yeh 6.5% tha, aur Lakshadweep mein 1.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Wahi Constitution, wahi criminal law, par gharon ke haalat bilkul alag. States ke survey aur police data par hamari alag story in farqon ko aur kareeb se dekhti hai.

Survey jin risk factors ki taraf ishaara karta hai, woh badal sakte hain. Jin auraton ke husband aksar nashe mein rehte hain, unmein se 71% ne husband ki physical ya sexual violence batayi. Jinke husband sharaab nahi peete, unmein 23% ne. Jin husbands ne 12 saal ya usse zyada padhai ki, unke physical, sexual ya emotional violence karne ke chances bina padhe husbands se aadhe the: 22% vs 43% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh jude hue patterns hain, inhe wajah ka saboot mat maaniye. Par inmein se koi bhi janam ya dharm se tay nahi hota.

"Rivaaz" pehle bhi badle hain. Child marriage ko bhi parampara bolkar bachaya jaata tha. 20-24 saal ki jin auraton ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui, unka hissa 2005-06 mein 47.4% tha [[ceda-genderstats-underage-marriage-2021]]. 2023-24 mein yeh ghatkar 20.1% reh gaya [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. United Nations (UN) kehta hai ki duniya mein child marriage jo ghati, woh zyada tar Southern Asia ki progress ki wajah se ghati [[un-sdg-report-2025-goal5]].

Partner violence isse kahin dheere ghat rahi hai. Poori duniya mein pichhle bees saal mein yeh har saal average sirf 0.2% ghati hai [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. 2022 mein duniya bhar ki development aid ka sirf 0.2% hissa auraton par violence rokne wale programmes ko mila, aur WHO ke mutabik 2025 mein yeh funding aur ghat gayi [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]].

Sri Lanka ka number koi chamatkaar nahi hai, aur Bangladesh ka koi kismat nahi. WHO ki table yeh nahi bata sakti ki har desh ka number kis wajah se aisa hai. Par yeh farq ek sawaal ka jawab zaroor de deta hai: husband ki violence South Asian zindagi ka tay hissa nahi hai. Lifetime number ke hisaab se India apne padosiyon ke beech mein khada hai. Woh kis taraf jaayega, yeh is par tika hai ki uske parivaar, schools, police aur sarkaarein kya karti hain.

laxmi-v-union-acid-sale-rules.en:
On 18 July 2013 the Supreme Court tried to take acid off the open counter. In Laxmi v. Union of India it directed that acid could be sold only by a seller who keeps a register, only to a buyer who shows government photo ID and states a purpose, and never to anyone under 18, with fines of up to Rs 50,000 for breaking the rules [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. Eleven years later, in 2024, India registered 207 acid attacks [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In October 2026 the Court told the Centre that its acid-sale guidelines had "miserably failed" [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

## The petition and the 2013 order

The best-known order in Laxmi v. Union of India, dated 18 July 2013, came from a bench of Justices R.M. Lodha and Fakkir Mohamed Ibrahim Kalifulla [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. It dealt with two things: how acid is sold, and what the state owes the people it is used against.

On sales, the directions were interim: they were to govern over-the-counter sales until each state framed its own rules under the Poisons Act, 1919 [[sc-laxmi-2013]].

On money, state compensation schemes varied widely, some paying a small fraction of what others did. The bench set a floor. Every acid-attack survivor was to get at least Rs 3 lakh from the state government for after-care and rehabilitation: Rs 1 lakh within 15 days of the attack, and the rest within two months [[sc-laxmi-2013]].

## What sellers and buyers were told to do

The sale directions were specific [[sc-laxmi-2013]]:

- **No sale without a register.** Over-the-counter sale of acid was banned unless the seller kept a register of who bought it.
- **ID and a reason.** The buyer had to show a government photo ID carrying their address, and say why they wanted the acid.
- **Stock on record.** Sellers had to declare all their acid stock to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) within 15 days.
- **No sale to minors.** Nobody under 18 could be sold acid.
- **Penalties.** A seller who broke the directions could be fined up to Rs 50,000.

Consider what this asks of a hardware shop in a small town. A customer asks for a bottle of acid. Under the order, the shopkeeper should check the buyer's ID, write down the name, address and stated purpose, and refuse if the buyer is under 18. Nobody stands at the counter to see that it happens. The only check the order builds in is a stock declaration filed with the SDM, and a fine once a breach is found.

## Acid attack becomes a named crime

The order came months after Parliament had changed the criminal law. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which received assent on 2 April 2013 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]], created two new offences, acid attack and attempted acid attack, as Sections 326A and 326B of the Indian Penal Code [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. The same Act required every hospital, public or private, to give acid-attack and rape victims first aid or treatment immediately and free of cost, and made refusing them an offence [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Since 1 July 2024 these rules live in the new codes. Acid attack is Section 124 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS): at least 10 years and up to life in prison, plus a fine paid to the victim; an attempt carries 5 to 7 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Free treatment is Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The punishment on paper has been severe for more than a decade. The 2013 order asked a different question: could acid be kept out of an attacker's hands in the first place?

## About 200 attacks a year, still

| Year | Acid attacks | Attempted acid attacks |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 202 | 71 |
| 2023 | 207 | 65 |
| 2024 | 207 | 68 |

These National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) counts cover victims of every sex [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Of the 207 attacks in 2024, 118 were on women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]; the national count also includes male victims.

The line misses attacks never reported to police, and attacks booked under other sections: NCRB counts only cases registered under the acid-attack sections [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And since NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, an attack that kills and is charged as murder is counted as a murder [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]].

Registered cases can rise simply because more survivors come forward, so a flat line is hard to read. But a rule that kept acid out of attackers' hands should, over time, pull the count down. In the three latest years of data, it has barely moved.

## October 2026: 'miserably failed'

On 27 October 2026 a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, hearing Shaheen Malik v. Union of India, turned to the Centre's acid-sale guidelines. "Despite your guidelines (to restrict retail sale of acid), unfortunate incidents are taking place," the Chief Justice said, adding that "if incidents are rising, that means the policy has miserably failed." The bench asked the Centre to revisit the policy and questioned whether acid needs to be sold in retail at all [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

Earlier, on 4 May 2026, in the same case, the Chief Justice had said the acid-attack provisions added in 2013 had had "no deterrent effect", asked whether punishment should be harsher, and said people who sell acid illegally should be made vicariously liable in acid-attack cases [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]]. Those were oral remarks during a hearing, not a judgment.

So the file is open again, with three options in view: tighter control of retail sale, no retail sale at all, or making sellers answer for what their acid is used to do. For now the Court has asked the Centre to revisit its policy. Whichever comes, the thirteen years since the order show what a rule on paper needs in order to work: someone checking at the counter, and public data on whether anyone did.

This is general information, not legal advice.
laxmi-v-union-acid-sale-rules.hg:
18 July 2013 ko Supreme Court ne acid ko dukaan ke khule counter se hataane ki koshish ki. Laxmi v. Union of India mein usne kaha ki acid sirf wahi seller bech sakta hai jo register rakhe, sirf us buyer ko jo government photo ID dikhaye aur wajah bataye, aur 18 se kam umar ke kisi ko kabhi nahi. Niyam todne par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta tha [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. Gyarah saal baad, 2024 mein, India mein 207 acid attacks register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. October 2026 mein Court ne Centre se kaha ki uski acid-sale guidelines "miserably failed" ho chuki hain [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

## Petition aur 2013 ka order

Laxmi v. Union of India ka sabse mashhoor order, 18 July 2013 ka, Justices R.M. Lodha aur Fakkir Mohamed Ibrahim Kalifulla ki bench se aaya [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. Is order ne do cheezon par baat ki: acid kaise becha jaata hai, aur jin logon par iska istemaal hota hai, unke prati state ki kya zimmedari hai.

Sale par, directions interim the: jab tak har state Poisons Act, 1919 ke under apne rules na bana le, tab tak dukaan ke counter par hone wali sale par Court ke directions hi chalne the [[sc-laxmi-2013]].

Paise par, alag-alag states ki compensation schemes mein bahut fark tha; kuch states doosron ke muqable bahut kam dete the. Bench ne ek minimum tay kar diya. Har acid-attack survivor ko state government se after-care aur rehabilitation ke liye kam se kam Rs 3 lakh milne the: Rs 1 lakh attack ke 15 din ke andar, aur baaki do mahine ke andar [[sc-laxmi-2013]].

## Sellers aur buyers ko kya karna tha

Sale ke directions bilkul saaf the [[sc-laxmi-2013]]:

- **Register ke bina sale nahi.** Dukaan ke counter par acid ki sale tab tak band thi jab tak seller yeh register na rakhe ki acid kisne kharida.
- **ID aur wajah.** Buyer ko address wali government photo ID dikhani thi, aur batana tha ki acid kis kaam ke liye chahiye.
- **Stock ka record.** Sellers ko apna poora acid stock 15 din ke andar Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) ke paas declare karna tha.
- **Minors ko nahi.** 18 se kam umar ke kisi ko acid nahi becha ja sakta tha.
- **Saza.** Directions todne wale seller par Rs 50,000 tak fine lag sakta tha.

Sochiye, chhote sheher ki ek hardware dukaan se yeh order kya maangta hai. Ek customer acid ki bottle maangta hai. Order ke hisaab se dukaandaar ko buyer ki ID check karni chahiye, naam, address aur bataayi gayi wajah register mein likhni chahiye, aur buyer 18 se kam ho toh mana kar dena chahiye. Counter par koi khada nahi hai jo dekhe ki aisa sach mein hota hai ya nahi. Order mein bas ek hi check hai: SDM ke paas stock ka declaration, aur violation pakde jaane par fine.

## Acid attack ek alag crime bana

Yeh order Parliament ke criminal law badalne ke kuch mahine baad aaya. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, jise 2 April 2013 ko assent mila [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]], ne do naye offences banaye, acid attack aur acid attack ki koshish, Indian Penal Code ki Sections 326A aur 326B ke roop mein [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Isi Act ne har hospital ke liye, sarkari ho ya private, zaroori kar diya ki woh acid attack aur rape victims ko turant aur free mein first aid ya ilaaj de, aur ilaaj se mana karna ek offence bana diya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

1 July 2024 se yeh niyam naye codes mein hain. Acid attack ab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 124 hai: kam se kam 10 saal aur zyada se zyada umr qaid, saath mein fine jo victim ko diya jaata hai; koshish par 5 se 7 saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Free ilaaj ab Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ki Section 397 mein hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Kaagaz par saza das saal se zyada samay se sakht rahi hai. 2013 ke order ka sawaal alag tha: kya acid ko attacker ke haath tak pahunchne se pehle hi roka ja sakta hai?

## Ab bhi har saal qareeb 200 attacks

| Saal | Acid attacks | Acid attack ki koshish |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 202 | 71 |
| 2023 | 207 | 65 |
| 2024 | 207 | 68 |

National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke yeh counts har sex ke victims ko shaamil karte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2024 ke 207 attacks mein se 118 auraton par hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]; national count mein male victims bhi shaamil hain.

Is line mein woh attacks nahi hain jo police tak kabhi report nahi hue, aur woh bhi nahi jo doosri sections mein book hue, kyunki NCRB sirf acid-attack sections mein register cases ginta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur kyunki NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar, uske sabse gambhir offence ke under ginta hai, jis attack mein jaan chali jaaye aur murder ka charge lage, woh murder mein gina jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]].

Registered cases sirf isliye bhi badh sakte hain ki zyada survivors saamne aa rahe hain, isliye ek flat line ko padhna mushkil hai. Par jo rule sach mein acid ko attackers ke haath se door rakhta, usse waqt ke saath count neeche aana chahiye tha. Data ke teen sabse naye saalon mein yeh count mushkil se hila hai.

## October 2026: 'miserably failed'

27 October 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur V. Mohana ki bench ne, Shaheen Malik v. Union of India ki sunwai karte hue, Centre ki acid-sale guidelines par sawaal uthaya. Chief Justice ne kaha, "Despite your guidelines (to restrict retail sale of acid), unfortunate incidents are taking place," aur yeh bhi ki "if incidents are rising, that means the policy has miserably failed." Yaani guidelines ke bawajood haadse ho rahe hain, aur agar ghatnayein badh rahi hain toh policy buri tarah fail hui hai. Bench ne Centre se policy par dobara sochne ko kaha, aur sawaal kiya ki retail mein acid bechne ki zaroorat hi kya hai [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

Isse pehle, 4 May 2026 ko isi case mein Chief Justice ne kaha tha ki 2013 mein jode gaye acid-attack provisions ka "no deterrent effect" raha, yaani koi darr nahi bana; unhone poochha ki kya saza aur sakht honi chahiye, aur kaha ki jo log gair-kanooni tareeke se acid bechte hain, unhe acid-attack cases mein vicariously liable banaya jaana chahiye, yaani attack ke liye unhe bhi zimmedar thehraya jaaye [[livelaw-acid-harsher-punishment-2026]]. Yeh sunwai ke dauraan kahi gayi baatein thi, judgment nahi.

Toh yeh file phir se khul gayi hai, aur teen raaste saamne hain: retail sale par aur sakht control, retail sale bilkul band, ya sellers ko us cheez ke liye jawabdeh banana jiske liye unka acid istemaal hota hai. Abhi ke liye Court ne Centre se apni policy par dobara sochne ko kaha hai. Jo bhi aaye, order ke baad ke terah saal yeh dikhate hain ki kaagaz ke rule ko kaam karne ke liye kya chahiye: counter par check karne wala koi insaan, aur public data jo bataye ki kisi ne check kiya bhi ya nahi.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

marital-rape-exception-section-63-explai.en:
One sentence in India's penal code decides whether forced sex inside a marriage can be called rape. Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says that sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. By 2018, 77 of 185 countries had laws that explicitly made marital rape a crime [[unwomen-progress-worlds-women-2019]]. Here is that sentence, India's place on the world map, and why the map matters before the Supreme Court's December 2026 hearing. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The sentence in Section 63

Section 63 builds rape law around consent, which it defines as an "unequivocal voluntary agreement" to a specific sexual act [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Exception 2 then switches that test off for one man: a husband whose wife is 18 or older.

For any other man, rape carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to life, under Section 64. A husband who forces sex on a wife living separately faces 2 to 7 years under Section 67 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under the text of the law, a husband who lives with his adult wife cannot be charged with rape.

Even the age of 18 was first set by a court, not Parliament. The 2013 rewrite of rape law kept the exception for wives aged 15 and above. On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read the exception down so that sex with a wife under 18 is rape, and expressly left adult wives undecided [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## What it lets through

The exception does not make forced sex in marriage rare. It takes it out of rape law. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 6.3% of ever-married women aged 18-49 reported sexual violence by their husband, and 4.6% said he had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to. Among ever-married women who had ever faced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Consider a 24-year-old in Patna, two years married, whose husband forces sex on her after she says no. Had she moved out, the law would call it a crime carrying up to seven years. Because she lives with him, criminal law says it is not rape. She can file a cruelty complaint, which carries up to three years under Section 85 [[indiacode-bns-2023]], or seek orders under the 2005 Domestic Violence Act, which counts sexual abuse as domestic violence but punishes a breached protection order with at most a year in prison [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. None of these uses the word rape.

## 77 of 185, 35 of 54: the world's marital rape laws

Explicitly criminalising marital rape is still a minority position, so India is not alone. The counts show where it sits:

| Measure | Countries | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Laws explicitly criminalising marital rape, by 2018 | 77 of 185 (42%) | UN Women [[unwomen-progress-worlds-women-2019]] |
| Neither a crime nor open to a wife's criminal complaint, by 2018 | 34 of 185 | UN Women [[unwomen-progress-worlds-women-2019]] |
| No legislation at all addressing marital rape | 43 | UNFPA, 2021 [[unfpa-swop-2021]] |
| Commonwealth countries keeping some marital exemption | 35 of 54 | 2020 study cited by UNFPA [[unfpa-swop-2021]] |
| Consent-based rape laws that explicitly criminalise marital rape | 38% of 131 | UN SDG Report 2026 [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]] |

The counts use different country lists, definitions and years, so they cannot be added up or read as a trend; UN Women's figures reflect laws in mid-2017.

Some countries' laws say nothing at all about marital rape. India's law is not silent: it speaks, and it says a husband is exempt, which places India among the 35 Commonwealth countries that keep some form of exemption. On the SDG test, which needs both a consent-based rape law and explicit coverage of marriage, India's law would fail the second half. Its code defines consent carefully, then excludes wives from it.

## The UN asked twice: 2007 and 2014

The UN's CEDAW Committee reviews India's record on women's rights. In July 2014 it urged India to amend its criminal law so that marital rape is defined as a criminal offence, repeating a request from its previous review in 2007, and to implement the recommendations of the Justice Verma Committee [[cedaw-india-concluding-observations-2014]].

The Verma Committee was India's own. Set up after the 2012 Delhi gang rape, it reported on 23 January 2013 and recommended deleting the marital rape exception [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament kept it.

The CEDAW Committee has not dropped the question. In a list of issues dated 5 February 2026, it asked India what steps it has taken to review the BNS to criminalise marital rape. India's next report is due on 3 February 2027 [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]]. A UN committee cannot change Indian law, but India will have to answer in writing, a few weeks after its own Supreme Court is due to hear the case.

## Where India stands before its Supreme Court hearing

In an affidavit verified on 3 October 2024, the Union government told the Supreme Court that a husband "certainly does not have any fundamental right to violate the consent of the wife", yet argued that calling it rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. In December 2024 it told the Rajya Sabha it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]].

As of 19 November 2026 the court had not ruled. A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026, to examine whether the exception is constitutionally valid and whether a prosecution can be sustained if it survives [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

The world map will not decide the case; judges test Indian law against India's Constitution. But it answers a claim common in Indian debates: that making marital rape a crime is a foreign idea that cannot work here. Dozens of countries made that choice explicitly, India's own expert committee recommended it in 2013, and the UN has asked for it since 2007. The question in December is whether India's Constitution allows a law that defines consent for every woman except a wife.
marital-rape-exception-section-63-explai.hg:
India ke penal code ka ek sentence tay karta hai ki shaadi ke andar zabardasti kiye gaye sex ko rape kaha ja sakta hai ya nahi. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki kisi aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sexual intercourse ya sexual acts, agar wife 18 se kam umr ki nahi hai, rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2018 tak 185 mein se 77 deshon mein aise law the jo marital rape ko saaf taur par crime banate the [[unwomen-progress-worlds-women-2019]]. Yeh explainer us sentence ko padhta hai, duniya ke naqshe par India ki jagah dikhata hai, aur batata hai ki Supreme Court ki December 2026 ki hearing se pehle yeh naqsha kyun maayne rakhta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Section 63 ka woh sentence

Section 63 rape law ko consent ke ird-gird banata hai, aur consent ko kisi specific sexual act ke liye "unequivocal voluntary agreement" kehta hai, yaani bina kisi shak ki, apni marzi se di gayi haan [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Phir Exception 2 yeh test ek aadmi ke liye band kar deta hai: woh pati jiski wife 18 saal ya usse badi hai.

Kisi bhi doosre aadmi ke liye rape par Section 64 ke tahat kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo life tak ja sakti hai. Jo pati alag reh rahi wife ke saath zabardasti sex karta hai, use Section 67 ke tahat 2 se 7 saal ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Law ke text ke hisaab se, jo pati apni adult wife ke saath rehta hai, us par rape ka charge lag hi nahi sakta.

18 ki umr bhi pehli baar Parliament ne nahi, court ne tay ki. 2013 mein rape law dobara likhte waqt 15 saal aur usse badi wives ke liye exception bana rehne diya gaya. 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne exception ko read down kiya, taaki 18 se kam umr ki wife ke saath sex rape maana jaaye, aur adult wives ka sawaal saaf taur par khula chhod diya [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

## Yeh exception kya chhoot deta hai

Exception shaadi mein zabardasti sex ko kam nahi karta. Bas use rape law se bahar kar deta hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 18-49 saal ki ever-married women mein se 6.3% ne pati dwara sexual violence report kiya, aur 4.6% ne kaha ki pati ne unki marzi ke bina unhe physically intercourse ke liye majboor kiya. Jin ever-married women ne kabhi sexual violence jhela tha, unmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Sochiye, Patna ki ek 24 saal ki aurat, jiski shaadi ko do saal hue hain, aur jiska pati uske mana karne ke baad bhi zabardasti sex karta hai. Agar woh alag reh rahi hoti, toh law ise saat saal tak ki saza wala crime kehta. Kyunki woh uske saath rehti hai, criminal law kehta hai ki yeh rape nahi hai. Woh cruelty ki complaint kar sakti hai, jis par Section 85 ke tahat teen saal tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], ya 2005 ke Domestic Violence Act ke tahat orders maang sakti hai. Yeh Act sexual abuse ko domestic violence maanta hai, lekin protection order todne par zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail deta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Inmein se koi bhi "rape" shabd ka istemaal nahi karta.

## 185 mein se 77, 54 mein se 35: duniya ke marital rape laws

Marital rape ko saaf taur par crime banana aaj bhi duniya mein minority position hai, isliye India akela nahi hai. Numbers dikhate hain ki woh kahan khada hai:

| Kya mapa gaya | Desh | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Marital rape ko saaf taur par crime banane wale law, 2018 tak | 185 mein se 77 (42%) | UN Women [[unwomen-progress-worlds-women-2019]] |
| Na crime, na wife ki criminal complaint ka raasta, 2018 tak | 185 mein se 34 | UN Women [[unwomen-progress-worlds-women-2019]] |
| Marital rape par koi bhi law nahi | 43 | UNFPA, 2021 [[unfpa-swop-2021]] |
| Kisi na kisi marital exemption wale Commonwealth desh | 54 mein se 35 | UNFPA ki quote ki gayi 2020 ki study [[unfpa-swop-2021]] |
| Consent par based aur marital rape ko saaf taur par crime maanne wale rape laws | 131 mein se 38% | UN SDG Report 2026 [[un-sdg-report-2026-goal5]] |

Yeh counts alag-alag country lists, definitions aur saalon par based hain, isliye inhe joda nahi ja sakta, na trend ki tarah padha ja sakta hai; UN Women ke figures mid-2017 ke laws dikhate hain.

Kuch deshon ke law marital rape par bilkul chup hain. India ka law chup nahi hai: woh bolta hai, aur kehta hai ki pati ko chhoot hai. Isi wajah se India un 35 Commonwealth deshon mein aata hai jo aaj bhi kisi na kisi roop mein exemption rakhte hain. SDG test mein do shartein hain: consent par based rape law, aur shaadi ka saaf taur par shaamil hona. India ka law doosri shart par fail hoga. Uska code consent ko dhyaan se define karta hai, aur phir wives ko usse bahar kar deta hai.

## UN ne do baar kaha: 2007 aur 2014

UN ki CEDAW Committee women's rights par India ke record ka review karti hai. July 2014 mein usne India se kaha ki apna criminal law badle taaki marital rape ko criminal offence define kiya jaaye. Yeh 2007 ke pichhle review mein ki gayi request ka dohraav tha. Committee ne Justice Verma Committee ki recommendations laagu karne ko bhi kaha [[cedaw-india-concluding-observations-2014]].

Verma Committee India ki apni thi. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ke baad bani is committee ne 23 January 2013 ko report di aur marital rape exception hataane ki sifarish ki [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne exception bana rehne diya.

CEDAW Committee ne yeh sawaal chhoda nahi hai. 5 February 2026 ki list of issues mein usne India se poocha ki marital rape ko crime banane ke liye BNS ke review ki disha mein kya kadam uthaaye gaye. India ki agli report 3 February 2027 tak deni hai [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]]. UN committee Indian law nahi badal sakti, lekin India ko likhit jawab dena hoga, aur woh bhi apne hi Supreme Court ki tay hearing ke kuch hafton baad.

## Supreme Court ki hearing se pehle India kahan khada hai

3 October 2024 ko verify kiye gaye affidavit mein Union government ne Supreme Court se kaha ki "a husband certainly does not have any fundamental right to violate the consent of the wife", yaani pati ke paas wife ki consent todne ka koi fundamental right nahi hai. Lekin saath hi daleel di ki ise rape kehna "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" ho sakta hai [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. December 2024 mein government ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki marital rape ko crime banane ka uska koi proposal nahi hai [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]].

19 November 2026 tak court ne faisla nahi diya tha. Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur V. Mohana ki bench ne kaha ki woh final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko rakhegi. Bench dekhegi ki exception constitutionally valid hai ya nahi, aur agar exception bacha rehta hai toh kya prosecution chal sakta hai [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Duniya ka naqsha yeh case tay nahi karega; judges Indian law ko India ke Constitution ki kasauti par parakhte hain. Lekin yeh naqsha Indian debates mein aam ek daave ka jawab deta hai: ki marital rape ko crime banana ek videshi idea hai jo yahan kaam nahi kar sakta. Darjanon deshon ne yeh faisla saaf taur par liya hai, India ki apni expert committee ne 2013 mein yahi sifarish ki thi, aur UN 2007 se yahi maang raha hai. December mein sawaal yeh hai ki kya India ka Constitution aise law ki ijaazat deta hai jo har aurat ke liye consent define karta hai, sivaay wife ke.

men-who-hit-their-wives-how-to-stop.en:
This guide is for one reader: a man who has hit his wife, or is afraid he will, and wants to stop. You are not rare. In a 2014 ICRW-UNFPA survey of 9,205 men and 3,158 women in seven Indian states, 60% of men said they had acted violently against a wife or partner at some point [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 44% of men said a husband is justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations, up from 42% in the previous round, while agreement among women fell from 52% to 45% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Common does not mean normal. It means many men make this choice, and each can make a different one.

## If you have hit her, start here

Start with her safety, not your guilt.

- **Do not touch her again, and do not block her way.** If she wants to leave the room, the house or go to her parents, let her. If she is hurt, make sure she can see a doctor.
- **Say what you did, without "but".** "I hit you. It was wrong." Not "I hit you, but you...".
- **Do not ask her to forgive, forget or keep quiet,** and do not send relatives to talk her round. Calling a helpline, the police or a lawyer is her choice.
- **Notice her fear.** In NFHS-5, 59% of women who were afraid of their husband most of the time had experienced violence from him, against 15% of women who were never afraid [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. If the house goes silent when you walk in, that is not peace.
- **Plan for next time.** Know your warning signs: a raised voice, a clenched jaw, another drink. When they come, leave until you are calm. Walking out of an argument is not losing it.

## The excuses, and why they fail

Every man who hits has a reason ready. Test yours.

**"She provoked me."** The reason most often accepted for wife-beating in NFHS-5 was a wife showing disrespect to her in-laws, accepted by 31% of men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yet most men do not hit a boss who insults them, or a stranger rude to their mother. They hit the person they think cannot hit back or leave. That is control, not provocation.

**"I was drunk."** Of women whose husbands often get drunk, 71% reported physical or sexual violence from them, against 23% of women whose husbands do not drink [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That is a link, not proof that alcohol causes violence; the 23% shows sober men hit too. If drinking is part of your pattern, stopping drinking is part of stopping, not all of it.

**"My family expects it. My father did it."** Then you were taught it, which means it can be unlearnt. Men who had often faced discrimination as children were four times more likely to be violent to a partner, the ICRW-UNFPA study found [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. What was done to you explains where the habit came from. It does not excuse what you do with it.

**"She refused me."** In NFHS-5, 12.2% of men said a husband has the right to use force to have sex if his wife refuses [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. No such right exists. Forcing her is violence, whatever the marriage certificate says.

## What the law says about violence at home

This is general information, not legal advice. Hitting someone and hurting them is voluntarily causing hurt, with up to a year in prison under Section 115(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Against a wife it can also be cruelty under Section 85, with up to three years and a fine; Section 86 counts wilful conduct likely to endanger her life, limb or health, mental or physical [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

She can also seek a protection order under the 2005 Domestic Violence Act; breaking it can bring up to a year in prison or a fine of up to Rs 20,000 [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. If she uses any of these, accept it. Pressuring her or her family to withdraw is the same control by other means.

## What your children are learning

Children do not need to see the blow to learn from it. Imagine a nine-year-old in Patna who hears shouting through the wall at night, then watches his mother pretend at breakfast that all is well. He is learning what a husband does. His sister is learning what a wife puts up with.

The data show both lessons. Women whose fathers beat their mothers were more than twice as likely to face violence from their own husbands: 58% against 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The lesson can run the other way too: men raised in homes where fathers did household chores were twice as likely to hold gender-equitable views [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

So let your children see the change: the apology without excuses, the dishes you wash, the decisions you make with their mother rather than for her.

## Getting help to stop: counselling and Tele-MANAS

You cannot do this on willpower alone, and your wife should not have to be your counsellor.

- **Call Tele-MANAS on 14416** [[tele-manas]]. The Health Ministry's helpline is free, runs round the clock and offers counselling to anyone in need [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. You can say exactly this: "I have been violent to my wife and I want to stop." Ask about help with anger, stress and drinking.
- **See a psychologist or psychiatrist on your own,** at a government hospital or a private clinic. Do not push her into joint counselling while the violence continues; across a table from you, she may not feel free to speak.
- **Tell one man you trust** what you did and what you are changing, and ask him to check on you.
- **Measure change by her freedom, not your feelings.** She is no longer afraid, sees her friends and family, handles money and says no without fear of what follows.

Tele-MANAS also helps if you have thoughts of harming yourself, and anyone facing abuse, including men and people in same-sex relationships, can call it. In immediate danger, call 112.
men-who-hit-their-wives-how-to-stop.hg:
Yeh guide ek hi reader ke liye hai: woh aadmi jisne apni patni par haath uthaya hai, ya jise darr hai ki utha dega, aur jo rukna chahta hai. Aap akele nahi hain. 2014 mein ICRW-UNFPA ne saat Indian states mein 9,205 aadmiyon aur 3,158 auraton ka survey kiya; 60% aadmiyon ne maana ki unhone kabhi na kabhi patni ya partner ke saath violence ki thi [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 44% aadmiyon ne kaha ki saat mein se kam se kam ek situation mein pati ka patni ko maarna sahi hai; pichhle round mein yeh 42% tha, jab ki auraton mein yeh sahmati 52% se ghatkar 45% ho gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aam hona normal hona nahi hai. Iska matlab hai ki bahut se aadmi yeh choice karte hain, aur har ek alag choice kar sakta hai.

## Agar aapne haath uthaya hai, toh yahan se shuru kijiye

Apne guilt se pehle uski safety.

- **Use dobara haath mat lagaiye, aur uska raasta mat rokiye.** Agar woh kamre se ya ghar se bahar jaana chahti hai, ya maayke jaana chahti hai, toh jaane dijiye. Agar use chot lagi hai, toh pakka kijiye ki woh doctor ko dikha sake.
- **Jo kiya, bina "lekin" ke kahiye.** "Maine tumhe maara. Yeh galat tha." Yeh nahi ki "Maine maara, lekin tumne...".
- **Usse maaf karne, bhoolne ya chup rehne ko mat kahiye,** aur use samjhane ke liye rishtedaron ko mat bhejiye. Helpline, police ya lawyer ko call karna uski choice hai.
- **Uska darr dekhiye.** NFHS-5 mein jo auratein zyada tar waqt apne pati se darti thin, unme se 59% ne pati ki violence jheli thi, jab ki kabhi na darne wali auraton mein yeh 15% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Agar aapke ghar aate hi sannata chha jaata hai, toh woh shaanti nahi hai.
- **Agli baar ke liye plan banaiye.** Apne warning signs pehchaaniye: oonchi hoti awaaz, bhinchta jabda, ek aur drink. Jab yeh dikhein, toh shaant hone tak wahan se chale jaiye. Behas beech mein chhod kar chale jaana haar nahi hai.

## Bahaane, aur woh kyun nahi chalte

Har maarne wale aadmi ke paas ek wajah tayyar hoti hai. Apni wajah ko parakhiye.

**"Usne mujhe uksaaya."** NFHS-5 mein patni ko maarne ki sabse zyada maani gayi wajah thi patni ka sasural walon ki izzat na karna, jise 31% aadmiyon ne sahi maana [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Par zyada tar aadmi us boss ko nahi maarte jo unki insult karta hai, na us ajnabi ko jo unki maa se badtameezi kare. Woh use maarte hain jiske baare mein unhe lagta hai ki woh na palat kar maar sakti hai, na chhod kar ja sakti hai. Yeh control hai, uksaava nahi.

**"Main nashe mein tha."** Jin auraton ke pati aksar nashe mein rehte hain, unme se 71% ne pati ki physical ya sexual violence report ki, jab ki sharaab na peene wale patiyon ki patniyon mein yeh 23% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh ek link hai, is baat ka saboot nahi ki sharaab violence ki wajah hai; woh 23% batata hai ki hosh mein rehne wale aadmi bhi maarte hain. Agar sharaab aapke pattern ka hissa hai, toh peena chhodna rukne ka ek hissa hai, poora jawab nahi.

**"Meri family yahi chahti hai. Mere pita bhi yahi karte the."** Toh aapko yeh sikhaya gaya, aur jo sikhaya gaya woh bhulaya bhi ja sakta hai. ICRW-UNFPA study mein paaya gaya ki jin aadmiyon ne bachpan mein aksar bhed-bhaav jhela tha, unke partner ke saath violence karne ki sambhavna chaar guna zyada thi [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. Aapke saath jo hua, woh batata hai ki yeh aadat kahan se aayi. Woh is baat ka bahaana nahi banta ki aap ab us aadat ke saath kya karte hain.

**"Usne mana kar diya."** NFHS-5 mein 12.2% aadmiyon ne kaha ki agar patni mana kare, toh pati ko zabardasti sex karne ka haq hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aisa koi haq nahi hai. Use majboor karna violence hai, shaadi ka certificate chahe jo kahe.

## Ghar ki violence par law kya kehta hai

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Kisi ko maar kar chot pahunchana voluntarily causing hurt hai, jisme Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 115(2) ke under ek saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Patni ke saath yeh Section 85 ke under cruelty bhi ho sakti hai, jisme teen saal tak ki jail aur fine hai; Section 86 aise jaan-boojhkar kiye gaye bartaav ko cruelty maanta hai jo uski jaan, ang ya health ko, mental ho ya physical, khatre mein daal sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Patni 2005 ke Domestic Violence Act ke under protection order bhi le sakti hai; use todne par ek saal tak ki jail ya Rs 20,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Agar woh inme se kuch bhi use karti hai, toh use sweekar kijiye. Us par ya uski family par case wapas lene ka dabaav daalna usi control ka doosra roop hai.

## Aapke bachche kya seekh rahe hain

Bachchon ko seekhne ke liye maar dekhni nahi padti. Sochiye, Patna mein ek nau saal ka ladka raat ko deewar ke us paar se chillane ki awaazein sunta hai, phir subah naashte par dekhta hai ki maa aise jata rahi hai jaise sab theek hai. Woh seekh raha hai ki pati kya karta hai. Uski behen seekh rahi hai ki patni kya sehti hai.

Data dono sabak dikhata hai. Jin auraton ke pita unki maa ko maarte the, unke apne pati se violence jhelne ki sambhavna doguni se bhi zyada thi: 58% banaam 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sabak ulti disha mein bhi chal sakta hai: jin gharon mein pita ghar ka kaam karte the, wahan pale aadmiyon mein gender-equitable soch hone ki sambhavna doguni thi [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Isliye bachchon ko badlaav dekhne dijiye: bina bahaane ki maafi, aapke dhoye bartan, aur woh faisle jo aap unki maa ke saath milkar lete hain, uski jagah nahi.

## Rukne ke liye madad: counselling aur Tele-MANAS

Yeh sirf will-power se nahi hoga, aur aapki patni ko aapka counsellor nahi banna chahiye.

- **Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye** [[tele-manas]]. Health Ministry ki yeh helpline free hai, chaubees ghante chalti hai aur har zarooratmand ko counselling deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Aap bilkul yahi keh sakte hain: "Maine apni patni ke saath violence ki hai aur main rukna chahta hoon." Gusse, stress aur sharaab ke liye madad ke baare mein poochiye.
- **Akele psychologist ya psychiatrist se miliye,** kisi government hospital ya private clinic mein. Jab tak violence chal rahi hai, use joint counselling mein mat dhakeliye; aapke saamne baithkar shayad woh khul kar bol na paaye.
- **Kisi ek bharose ke aadmi ko bataiye** ki aapne kya kiya aur kya badal rahe hain, aur use kahiye ki woh aapki khabar leta rahe.
- **Badlaav ko apni feelings se nahi, uski azaadi se naapiye.** Woh ab darti nahi, apne doston aur family se milti hai, paisa khud sambhalti hai, aur bina kisi darr ke na keh sakti hai.

Agar aapke mann mein khud ko nuksaan pahunchane ke khayal aate hain, toh Tele-MANAS usme bhi madad karta hai, aur abuse jhel raha koi bhi insaan, chahe aadmi ho ya same-sex relationship mein ho, use call kar sakta hai. Turant khatre mein 112 par call kijiye.

neighbour-hears-domestic-violence-what-t.en:
Imagine it is past eleven on a weeknight in a Pune housing society. Through the wall you hear a man shouting, something heavy hitting the floor, a woman crying, then a silence that is worse. It is not the first time. The next morning she avoids your eyes in the lift, and you say nothing, because nobody does. This guide is about what a neighbour can safely do instead. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why the neighbour matters

In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 77.2% of women aged 18-49 who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told a single person; only 14.1% had ever sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Of those who did, 60.9% turned to their own family and 6.3% to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. By our arithmetic, that means fewer than one in 100 women who faced violence went to the police.

So the people who know are often the people nobody told: the family across the landing, the girl in the next hostel room, the cousin who visits on Sundays. You may be the only witness outside that home.

## In an emergency: 112

If you hear someone being hurt right now, or a threat to kill, call 112, the single emergency number that reaches the police [[mha-erss]]. Do not wait to be sure; working out what is happening is the police's job.

Give the building, floor and flat number, what you heard, and whether a weapon was mentioned or children are inside. Then stay on your side of the door. Walking in to "sort it out" can put you at risk and make things worse for her later.

That night, write down the date, the time and what you heard. If she later goes to court or the police, you can be a witness, and a dated note beats a memory.

If the person being hurt is a child, call the Child Helpline, 1098, which is linked to the 112 system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. If you learn that a child is being sexually abused, the POCSO Act makes reporting it a duty for anyone who knows [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Reporting when it is not an emergency

Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) lets anyone report a cognizable offence at any police station, wherever it was committed (a "Zero FIR"), or electronically, if the report is signed within 3 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. In Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh (2013), the Supreme Court held that police must register an FIR when information discloses a cognizable offence [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

But the same judgment allowed a short preliminary inquiry in matrimonial and family disputes [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]], and the BNSS now lets police, with a senior officer's approval, take up to 14 days for a preliminary enquiry into offences punishable with three to under seven years [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Cruelty by a husband or his relatives carries up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. So a report about a pattern of abuse may bring questions before it brings an FIR, and whether a case goes ahead will usually depend on her.

There is also a route that does not depend on an FIR. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is mainly a civil law: it lets a woman seek protection, residence and maintenance orders, and Protection Officers appointed under it are meant to help her use it [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Breaking a protection order is itself an offence, punishable with up to a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Only she can decide to use it, but you can help her find the Protection Officer or the One Stop Centre. The Act protects women; if a man is being hurt, 112 and the ordinary criminal law still apply.

## Talking to her safely

A call to 112 deals with one night. The longer work is a conversation.

- **Choose the moment.** Talk when he is out and she is not rushed, on the stairs or the walk to the bus stop. Never in front of him or his family.
- **Start small.** "I heard shouting last night. Are you all right? Is there anything you want me to do?" Then listen. Do not ask why she stays, and do not tell her to leave or to adjust.
- **Ask before you act.** Calling her parents, his family or the society secretary can feel like help and land as exposure; families can also push her to stay quiet.
- **Offer something concrete.** Your number saved under a harmless name, a code word that means "call 112", a safe place for copies of her ID and bank papers, your phone for calls he cannot see.
- **Keep it out of group chats.** Gossip travels back to the flat it is about.

Leaving, reporting or waiting is her decision. Your job is to make each option less frightening, and to still be there if she says no today.

## The Women Helpline, One Stop Centres and following up

The Women Helpline takes calls from women facing violence, and One Stop Centres (Sakhi) offer police help, medical and legal aid, counselling and short-stay shelter under one roof, both under the government's Mission Shakti [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. In July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 centres approved across India were operational, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Free legal aid is available through the District Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]]. Find your district's centre now, before she needs it.

Then keep showing up. If she decides to act, offer to go with her, and to say what you heard if she needs a witness. If she decides not to, respect that and leave the door open.

The aim is not to rescue her. It is to make sure that when she is ready to tell someone, the person next door has already shown it is safe to tell.
neighbour-hears-domestic-violence-what-t.hg:
Sochiye, Pune ki ek housing society mein kisi weekday ki raat ke gyarah baj chuke hain. Deewar ke us paar se ek aadmi ke chillane ki aawaaz aati hai, koi bhaari cheez farsh pe girti hai, ek aurat roti hai, aur phir ek khamoshi jo usse bhi buri lagti hai. Yeh pehli baar nahi hai. Agli subah lift mein woh aapse nazrein churaati hai, aur aap kuch nahi kehte, kyunki koi nahi kehta. Yeh guide is baare mein hai ki ek padosi iski jagah safely kya kar sakta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Padosi kyun maayne rakhta hai

NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 18-49 saal ki 77.2% women ne na kabhi help maangi thi, na kisi ek insaan ko bataya tha; sirf 14.1% ne kabhi help maangi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jinhone maangi, unme se 60.9% apne parivaar ke paas gayi aur 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Hamare hisaab se iska matlab hai ki violence jhelne wali 100 mein se ek se bhi kam women police tak pahunchti hain.

Toh jinhe pata hota hai, woh aksar woh log hote hain jinhe kisi ne bataya hi nahi: landing ke us paar wali family, hostel ke agle kamre wali ladki, har Sunday aane wala cousin. Us ghar ke bahar shayad sirf aap hi gawah hain.

## Emergency mein: 112

Agar aap sun rahe hain ki kisi ko abhi chot pahunchaayi ja rahi hai, ya koi jaan se maarne ki dhamki de raha hai, toh 112 pe call kijiye, woh single emergency number jo police tak pahunchta hai [[mha-erss]]. Pakka hone ka intezaar mat kijiye; kya ho raha hai, yeh samajhna police ka kaam hai.

Building, floor aur flat number bataiye, aapne kya suna, aur kya kisi hathiyaar ka zikr hua ya andar bachche hain. Phir apne darwaaze ke is taraf hi rahiye. "Maamla suljhaane" ke liye khud andar chale jaana aapko khatre mein daal sakta hai aur baad mein uske liye haalaat aur bigaad sakta hai.

Usi raat date, time aur jo suna woh likh lijiye. Agar baad mein woh court ya police jaaye, toh aap gawah ban sakte hain, aur date wala note yaaddasht se kahin zyada kaam aata hai.

Agar chot kisi bachche ko pahunchaayi ja rahi hai, toh Child Helpline 1098 pe call kijiye, jo 112 system se juda hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Agar aapko pata chale ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse ho raha hai, toh POCSO Act ke under iski report karna har us insaan ki duty hai jise iski jaankaari hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Jab emergency na ho, tab report karna

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 173 kisi ko bhi ek cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi police station pe karne deta hai, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho (yaani "Zero FIR"), ya electronically, agar report 3 din ke andar sign kar di jaaye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh (2013) mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki jab information se cognizable offence ka pata chalta hai, tab police ko FIR register karni hi hogi [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

Lekin isi judgment ne matrimonial aur family disputes mein ek chhoti preliminary inquiry ki ijaazat bhi di [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]], aur ab BNSS police ko, ek senior officer ki manzoori se, teen se saat saal se kam ki saza wale offences mein 14 din tak preliminary enquiry karne deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Husband ya uske relatives ki cruelty pe teen saal tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Isliye lagaataar abuse ki report pe FIR se pehle sawaal aa sakte hain, aur case aage badhega ya nahi, yeh aam taur pe usi woman pe nirbhar karega.

Ek raasta aisa bhi hai jo FIR pe nirbhar nahi karta. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 zyada tar ek civil law hai: isme woman protection, residence aur maintenance orders maang sakti hai, aur iske under appoint hue Protection Officers ka kaam use yeh law use karne mein madad karna hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Protection order todna khud ek offence hai, jiski saza ek saal tak ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Ise use karne ka faisla sirf uska hai, lekin aap Protection Officer ya One Stop Centre dhoondhne mein uski madad kar sakte hain. Yeh Act women ko protect karta hai; agar kisi aadmi ko chot pahunchaayi ja rahi hai, toh 112 aur normal criminal law phir bhi laagu hote hain.

## Usse safely baat karna

112 pe ek call ek raat ko sambhaalti hai. Lamba kaam ek baatcheet se hota hai.

- **Sahi waqt chuniye.** Tab baat kijiye jab woh aadmi ghar pe na ho aur use jaldi na ho, seedhiyon pe ya bus stop tak chalte hue. Kabhi bhi uske ya uske parivaar ke saamne nahi.
- **Chhote se shuru kijiye.** "Kal raat chillane ki aawaaz aayi thi. Aap theek ho? Kya aap chahti ho ki main kuch karun?" Phir suniye. Yeh mat poochhiye ki woh wahan kyun reh rahi hai, aur use chhod dene ya "adjust" karne ko mat kahiye.
