- **Kuch karne se pehle poochhiye.** Uske parents, uske sasuraal waalon ya society secretary ko phone karna help jaisa lag sakta hai par uske liye exposure ban sakta hai; parivaar use chup rehne ke liye bhi daba sakte hain.
- **Kuch thos offer kijiye.** Apna number kisi maamuli naam se save karwaana, ek code word jiska matlab ho "112 call karo", uske ID aur bank papers ki copies ke liye ek safe jagah, aur aisi calls ke liye apna phone jo woh aadmi na dekh sake.
- **Group chats se door rakhiye.** Gossip ghoom-phir ke usi flat tak pahunchti hai jiske baare mein hoti hai.

Chhodna, report karna ya abhi rukna, yeh faisla uska hai. Aapka kaam har option ko kam darawna banana hai, aur agar woh aaj na kahe toh bhi saath bane rehna hai.

## Women Helpline, One Stop Centres aur follow-up

Women Helpline violence jhel rahi women ki calls leti hai, aur One Stop Centres (Sakhi) ek hi chhat ke neeche police help, medical aur legal aid, counselling aur thode samay ka shelter dete hain; dono sarkar ke Mission Shakti ke under chalte hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. July 2026 mein poore India mein approve hue 1,033 centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se tab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada women ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. District Legal Services Authority se free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]]. Apne district ka centre abhi dhoondh ke rakhiye, zaroorat padne se pehle.

Phir saath bane rahiye. Agar woh kuch karne ka faisla kare, toh uske saath chalne ki offer kijiye, aur zaroorat pade toh gawah ban ke jo suna woh bataane ki bhi. Agar woh na kare, toh uska faisla maaniye aur darwaaza khula rakhiye.

Maksad use "bachaana" nahi hai. Maksad yeh pakka karna hai ki jab woh kisi ko batane ke liye taiyaar ho, tab tak bagal wala padosi dikha chuka ho ki use batana safe hai.

nfhs5-one-in-three-wives-violence.en:
Between 2019 and 2021, surveyors for India's fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) asked women questions their own families rarely ask. Not "are you abused?" but specific things: has your husband ever slapped you, humiliated you in front of others, or forced you to have sex when you did not want to? Nearly one in three ever-married women described at least one form of this violence: 31.9% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In the 12 months before the interview alone, it was 26.8% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. This is not about other families. It describes ordinary Indian homes.

## What NFHS-5 asked, and whom

NFHS is the Union health ministry's own household survey, run by the International Institute for Population Sciences [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Its questions about husbands go to ever-married women aged 18 to 49: married now, or widowed, separated or divorced.

The questions ask about acts, not labels. A woman who would never call her marriage abusive can still say whether she was pushed, threatened or insulted.

One caveat applies to every figure below. These are answers given face to face to a stranger, so under-reporting is likely. WHO notes that short violence modules inside broad health surveys, which is what NFHS uses, draw less disclosure than dedicated violence surveys [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. Read every NFHS number as a floor.

## 31.9%, 29.2%, 26.8%: three numbers, three meanings

31.9% is the widest count: ever-married women who have faced physical, sexual or emotional violence from a husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Emotional violence here means being humiliated, threatened or insulted.

29.2% leaves emotional violence out. It counts physical or sexual violence by a woman's current or most recent husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]], which makes it the figure to set beside WHO's estimate and later survey rounds. Inside it, 6.3% reported sexual violence by a husband, and 4.6% said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Under Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), that is still not rape if the wife is 18 or older [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

26.8% is the one to remember. It counts violence in the 12 months before the interview [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Put it next to 31.9% and the meaning is plain: most women who had ever faced violence from a husband had faced it in the past year. For them it was not a memory. It was the present.

It starts early, too. Among currently married women married only once, 11.2% first faced physical or sexual violence within two years of the wedding, and 20.9% within five [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Karnataka 48.4%, Lakshadweep 1.3%: the spread across states

The national figure hides a huge range. In Karnataka, 48.4% of ever-married women reported physical, sexual or emotional violence by their current or most recent husband, the highest in India. Bihar (42.5%), Manipur (41.6%) and Telangana (40.4%) followed, while Lakshadweep was lowest at 1.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

This is not a simple north-versus-south or village-versus-city map. Two of the top four are southern states. Cities are not exempt: 27% of urban women reported spousal violence, against 34% of rural women [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Schooling goes with less violence, not none. By their wives' accounts, husbands with 12 or more years of schooling were half as likely to be violent as husbands with no schooling, but that still meant 22% of them, against 43% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

WHO's warning about comparing countries applies here too: such gaps can reflect stigma and how freely women can speak, as well as real differences in violence [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## WHO's estimate and the police register

Is NFHS an outlier? No. WHO's modelled estimate for India, built from national survey data, puts physical or sexual violence by a partner at 29.9% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15 to 49 over their lifetime, and 22.4% in the past 12 months. That places India among the 33 countries and territory with the highest past-year rates in WHO's 2023 estimates; Afghanistan is the only other South Asian country in that group [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Newer numbers exist, and they are disputed. Provisional NFHS-6 fact sheets for 2023-24 put physical or sexual violence by a husband at 22.3% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], but experts quoted by Deccan Herald doubt that the fall reflects reality [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]]. Another story in this magazine weighs that evidence.

In 2024, police across India registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives, under Section 85 BNS and the old Section 498A IPC [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It is the largest single category of crimes against women, yet it works out to 17.6 cases for every lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Set that against a survey in which more than one in four ever-married women reported violence within a single year. The register is a sliver of what happens.

The gap is silence, not exaggeration. In NFHS-5, 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone. Only 14.1% had sought help, and of those, only 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. As another story in this magazine works out, that is fewer than one in 100 of all the women who faced violence. Among women abused only by their current husband, just 11.3% had ever sought help, against 23.6% of women abused only by a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## One in three, in your own building

Picture a housing society with 30 flats and one ever-married woman in each (an illustration, not a real building). If the national average held there, about 10 of those women would have faced violence from a husband, and about 8 would have faced it in the last year. Going by the survey's help-seeking figures, most would have told no one, and very likely not one would have gone to the police.

You may know some of them, and not only in villages or homes without schooling. NFHS-5 also points to a pattern across generations: women whose fathers beat their mothers were more than twice as likely to face violence from their own husbands, 58% against 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The children in that building are watching, and learning what a marriage looks like.

That is why "one in three" is not fate. What is passed down can be stopped: by the neighbour who does not look away, the relative who stops saying "adjust", the parent who will not let a child believe this is normal. The 2005 Domestic Violence Act counts sexual abuse, not only beating, as domestic violence [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. It is mainly a civil law: under it, a woman can seek protection, residence and maintenance orders without filing a criminal case.
nfhs5-one-in-three-wives-violence.hg:
2019 se 2021 ke beech National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) ki teams ne desh bhar ki auraton se woh sawaal poochhe jo aksar unke apne gharwale bhi nahi poochhte. Sawaal yeh nahi tha ki "kya aap abused hain?" Sawaal seedhe the: kya pati ne kabhi thappad maara? Kya sabke saamne beizzati ki? Kya aapke na chahne par bhi zabardasti sex kiya? Jin auraton ki kabhi shaadi hui, unmein se lagbhag har teen mein se ek ne aisi kisi na kisi violence ki baat batayi: 31.9% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sirf interview se pehle ke 12 mahinon mein yeh number 26.8% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh kisi aur ke ghar ki baat nahi hai. Yeh aam Indian gharon ki tasveer hai.

## NFHS-5 ne kya poochha, aur kisse

NFHS central government ki health ministry ka apna household survey hai, jise International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) karta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Pati se jude sawaal 18 se 49 saal ki un auraton se poochhe jaate hain jinki kabhi bhi shaadi hui ho: jo abhi married hain, aur woh bhi jo widow hain, pati se alag rehti hain ya divorced hain. Is story mein "married women" ka yahi matlab hai.

Sawaal kisi label ke baare mein nahi, incidents ke baare mein hote hain. Jo aurat apni shaadi ko kabhi "abusive" nahi kahegi, woh bhi bata sakti hai ki use dhakka diya gaya, dhamkaya gaya ya beizzat kiya gaya.

Ek baat har number par laagu hoti hai. Yeh jawaab ek anjaan insaan ko aamne-saamne diye gaye, isliye under-reporting ki poori sambhavna hai. WHO bhi kehta hai ki jab bade health survey ke andar violence par chhota sa module jod diya jaata hai, toh auratein kam khulti hain; sirf violence par bane survey mein zyada batati hain [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. NFHS mein violence wala hissa aisa hi chhota module hai. Isliye NFHS ke har number ko "kam se kam itna" samjhiye.

## 31.9%, 29.2%, 26.8%: teen numbers, teen matlab

31.9% sabse bada daayra hai: woh saari married women jinhone pati se physical, sexual ya emotional violence jheli [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Emotional violence matlab beizzati, dhamki, ya taane maar kar neecha dikhana.

29.2% mein emotional violence nahi gini jaati. Ismein sirf current pati ki, ya shaadi toot chuki ho toh aakhri pati ki, physical ya sexual violence gini jaati hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. WHO ke estimate aur survey ke agle rounds se compare karne ke liye yahi number sahi hai. Isi ke andar 6.3% auraton ne pati se sexual violence ki baat batayi, aur 4.6% ne kaha ki unke na chahne par bhi pati ne zabardasti unke saath sex kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Phir bhi Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke hisaab se, agar patni 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh law ise rape nahi maanta [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

26.8% wala number yaad rakhiye. Yeh sirf interview se pehle ke 12 mahinon ki violence ginta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ise 31.9% ke bagal mein rakhiye aur matlab saaf ho jaata hai: jin auraton ne kabhi bhi pati ki violence jheli, unmein se zyada tar ne pichhle ek saal mein bhi jheli. Unke liye yeh purani yaad nahi thi. Yeh unka aaj tha.

Aur yeh jaldi shuru ho jaati hai. Jo auratein abhi married hain aur jinki ek hi shaadi hui, unmein se 11.2% ke saath shaadi ke do saal ke andar pehli baar physical ya sexual violence hui, aur paanch saal ke andar 20.9% ke saath [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Karnataka 48.4%, Lakshadweep 1.3%: states mein kitna farq

Desh ka average ek bahut bada farq chhupa leta hai. Karnataka mein 48.4% married women ne apne current ya pichhle pati se physical, sexual ya emotional violence ki baat batayi, jo India mein sabse zyada tha. Uske baad Bihar (42.5%), Manipur (41.6%) aur Telangana (40.4%) the, aur sabse kam Lakshadweep mein tha: 1.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh koi seedha "north vs south" ya "gaon vs shehar" wala map nahi hai. Top chaar mein se do states south ke hain. Shehar bhi bache nahi hain: shehron mein 27% auraton ne pati ki violence ki baat batayi, gaon mein 34% ne [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Zyada padhai ke saath violence kam dikhti hai, khatam nahi hoti. Patniyon ke jawaab ke hisaab se, bina padhe patiyon mein 43% ne violence ki; 12 ya usse zyada saal padhe patiyon mein yeh aadha tha, phir bhi 22% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Countries ko compare karne par WHO ki warning yahan bhi kaam aati hai: aise farq ke peeche asli violence ka farq bhi ho sakta hai, aur yeh bhi ki auratein kitna khul kar bol paati hain aur society mein is baat par kitni sharm judi hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## WHO ka estimate aur police ka register

Kya sirf NFHS hi aisa kehta hai? Nahi. WHO ne survey data se ek model bana kar India ke liye apna estimate nikaala hai. Iske hisaab se 15 se 49 saal ki jin auraton ki shaadi hui ya jinka koi partner raha, unmein se 29.9% ne zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi partner se physical ya sexual violence jheli, aur pichhle 12 mahinon mein 22.4% ne. WHO ke 2023 ke estimates mein India un 33 countries aur territory mein hai jahan pichhle saal ki yeh rate sabse oonchi hai; South Asia se is list mein India ke alawa sirf Afghanistan hai [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

Naye numbers bhi aaye hain, par un par sawaal hain. NFHS-6 (2023-24) ki provisional fact sheets mein pati ki physical ya sexual violence ka number 22.3% hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], lekin Deccan Herald se baat karne wale experts ko shak hai ki yeh giravat asli hai [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]]. Hamari ek aur story is saboot ko detail mein parakhti hai.

Ab police ka register dekhiye. 2024 mein poore desh mein police ne "pati ya uske rishtedaaron ki cruelty" ke 1,20,227 cases darj kiye. Yeh BNS ka Section 85 aur purane IPC ka Section 498A wala crime hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Auraton ke khilaaf crimes mein sabse zyada cases isi ke hain, phir bhi yeh har ek lakh auraton par sirf 17.6 cases banta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Udhar survey mein sirf ek saal ke andar chaar mein se ek se zyada married women ne violence ki baat batayi. Matlab register asli tasveer ka bas ek chhota sa tukda hai.

Yeh gap badha-chadha kar batane ka nahi, chuppi ka hai. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% auraton ne na kabhi madad maangi thi, na kisi ko bataya tha. Sirf 14.1% ne madad maangi, aur unmein se bhi sirf 6.3% police ke paas gayin [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Hamari ek aur story mein hisaab lagaya gaya hai ki iska matlab hai: violence jhelne wali har 100 auraton mein se ek se bhi kam police tak pahunchti hai. Jin auraton ko sirf unke current pati ne sataya, unmein se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi madad maangi, jabki jinhe sirf pichhle pati ne sataya, unmein 23.6% ne [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Har teen mein se ek, aapki apni building mein

Sochiye, ek housing society hai jismein 30 flats hain, aur har flat mein ek married aurat rehti hai. (Yeh sirf samjhane ke liye ek example hai, kisi asli building ka data nahi.) Agar desh ka average wahan bhi laagu ho, toh inmein se kareeb 10 auraton ne pati ki violence jheli hogi, aur kareeb 8 ne pichhle ek saal mein. Survey ke help-seeking numbers ke hisaab se inmein se zyada tar ne kisi ko nahi bataya hoga, aur bahut mumkin hai ki ek bhi police tak nahi gayi hogi.

Inmein se kuch ko shayad aap jaante bhi hon, aur woh sirf gaon mein ya bina padhe-likhe gharon mein nahi hain. NFHS-5 peedhiyon ke beech ek pattern bhi dikhata hai: jin auraton ke papa unki mummy ko peette the, unke saath pati ki violence ka risk do guna se bhi zyada tha, 58%, jabki baaki auraton mein 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Us building ke bachche bhi yeh sab dekh rahe hain, aur seekh rahe hain ki shaadi kaisi hoti hai.

Isiliye "har teen mein se ek" koi kismat ka likha nahi hai. Jo cheez peedhi-dar-peedhi aage badhti hai, use roka bhi ja sakta hai: woh padosi jo nazrein nahi pherta, woh rishtedaar jo "adjust kar lo" kehna band karta hai, woh maa-baap jo bachche ko yeh nahi maanne dete ki yeh sab normal hai. 2005 ka Domestic Violence Act sirf maar-peet ko nahi, sexual abuse ko bhi domestic violence maanta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]], aur yeh mainly ek civil law hai: iske tahat aurat bina criminal case kiye bhi protection, ghar mein rehne aur kharche ke orders maang sakti hai.

nfhs6-domestic-violence-fall-doubts.en:
In 2026 India got what looked like its best news on violence at home in years. Provisional fact sheets from the sixth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6, 2023-24) reported that 22.3% of ever-married women aged 18 to 49 had faced physical or sexual violence from a husband, down from 29.2% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. If it is real, it is very good news. This investigation asks whether it is.

## The headline drop: 29.2% to 22.3%

Start with what the indicator measures. It counts women who have ever experienced spousal violence, defined as physical or sexual violence [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Ever means ever. A woman beaten by her husband in 2018, still married to him and 35 in 2024, should still answer yes. A lifetime figure like this should fall only slowly, as older women age out of the survey's 18-to-49 band and younger women enter it.

That is what happened before. Between NFHS-4 (2015-16) and NFHS-5, the same lifetime share fell only from 31% to 29% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Worldwide, WHO says partner violence has declined by about 0.2% a year on average over 20 years, and the "one in three" figure has barely moved [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. A drop from 29.2% to 22.3% in one round would outrun both India's own past and the world's.

The fine print matters too. The fact sheets are provisional. Fieldwork ran from May 2023 to December 2024 and Manipur was not covered. IIPS itself cautions that some states have small samples, and the urban sampling frame changed from NFHS-5 [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## Karnataka 44.4% to 14.1%, Kerala 9.8% to 17.7%

The state numbers make the puzzle sharper. In NFHS-5, Karnataka had the highest share in India: 44.4% of ever-married women had faced physical or sexual violence from a husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In NFHS-6, Karnataka reports 14.1%, well below the national average. Kerala moved the other way, from 9.8% to 17.7% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

For Karnataka's fall to be real, most women in the state who had ever been hit or sexually abused by a husband would have had to leave the survey's age band between two rounds only a few years apart. Neither ageing nor social change is likely to work that fast. A change in who answered, where and in front of whom, could.

Kerala is just as hard to read. Its police registered 496 of India's 616 criminal cases under the 2005 Domestic Violence Act in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]: the law is used there in a way it is not elsewhere. Kerala's rise could mean more violence, or more women willing to name it. The fact sheets cannot tell the two apart.

## What makes a woman tell a surveyor, or not

An honest answer depends on who else can hear. Experts quoted by Deccan Herald in June 2026, among them a Mumbai-based public-health researcher, doubted that the fall reflects reality. They said women may not disclose abuse to a surveyor in front of family members, and questioned whether interviews were private. The paper's headline said the decline "may be true only on paper" [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]].

WHO makes a related point about method. Dedicated surveys on violence against women are likely to draw more disclosure than short modules inside broader surveys [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. NFHS is the second kind: its violence questions are one module in a broad family-health survey.

Now imagine one interview (a hypothetical, not a real case). A surveyor with a tablet. A mother-in-law in the next room. A husband due home soon. Late in a long interview, the question comes: has your husband ever...? Saying yes could cost her a great deal. Saying no costs nothing. In NFHS-5, 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For many, the surveyor would be the first person ever told. So even small changes in how interviews are run could move the numbers a lot.

## Police numbers fall too: less violence or fewer complaints?

Police data seem to agree. Registered cases of cruelty by a husband or relatives fell from 1,40,019 in 2022 to 1,33,676 in 2023 [[ncrb-cii-2023]] and 1,20,227 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Two sources pointing the same way is a serious argument that something real may be shifting.

But the police series also depends on women speaking up and officers writing it down. NCRB itself says a rise in registered crime and a rise in crime are two different things [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]], and the same is true of a fall. From 1 July 2024, Section 173(3) of the BNSS lets police, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering offences punishable with three to under seven years [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Cruelty under Section 85 BNS carries up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]], so cruelty complaints can fall inside that window. A complaint that stays an enquiry never enters the count. Our story on why cruelty is the largest crime against women walks through the full police series.

The strongest evidence for a real fall comes from a crime that is much harder to hide. Registered dowry deaths fell from 6,450 in 2022 to 6,156 in 2023 and 5,737 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That deserves weight. It is also a different crime, counted under a different section of the law.

## How to read a 'violence is down' headline

Ask five questions. Which measure: violence ever, or in the past year; physical and sexual only, or emotional too? Is it final, or provisional? Did the method change: sampling, coverage, who was in the room? Do the parts make sense, such as a lifetime figure falling by more than two-thirds in one state? And do other sources measure violence, or only complaints?

A real fall would be the best news Indian women could get, and nobody should wish it away. But until the full NFHS-6 report explains its methods, treat 22.3% as what women felt able to tell a stranger in 2023-24, not as a measure of what happened behind their doors.
nfhs6-domestic-violence-fall-doubts.hg:
2026 mein India ko ghar ki violence par saalon ki sabse achhi khabar jaisa kuch mila. National Family Health Survey ke chhathe round (NFHS-6, 2023-24) ki provisional fact sheets aayin. Inke hisaab se 18 se 49 saal ki 22.3% married women (yaani jinki kabhi bhi shaadi hui ho) ne pati se physical ya sexual violence jheli thi, jabki NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein yeh number 29.2% tha [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Agar yeh sach hai, toh yeh bahut achhi khabar hai. Yeh investigation yahi check karti hai ki kya yeh sach hai.

## Headline giravat: 29.2% se 22.3%

Pehle samjhiye ki yeh number ginta kya hai. Yeh un auraton ko ginta hai jinhone kabhi bhi pati ki violence jheli ho, aur yahan violence ka matlab hai physical ya sexual violence [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. "Kabhi bhi" ka matlab hai kabhi bhi. Jis aurat ko 2018 mein uske pati ne peeta, jo ab bhi usi pati ke saath hai aur 2024 mein 35 saal ki hai, uska jawaab ab bhi "haan" hona chahiye. Isliye aisa lifetime number dheere-dheere hi girna chahiye: jaise-jaise badi umar ki auratein survey ke 18-49 saal wale band se bahar nikalti hain aur nayi, kam umar ki auratein usmein judti hain.

Pehle yahi hua bhi tha. NFHS-4 (2015-16) se NFHS-5 ke beech yahi number sirf 31% se 29% par aaya tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Duniya bhar mein WHO ke hisaab se pichhle 20 saal mein partner violence har saal average sirf 0.2% ghati hai, aur "har teen mein se ek" wala number lagbhag wahin ka wahin hai [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]]. Ek hi round mein 29.2% se 22.3% ki giravat India ke apne purane record se bhi tez hai, aur baaki duniya se bhi.

Fine print bhi important hai. Yeh fact sheets provisional hain, final nahi. Fieldwork May 2023 se December 2024 tak chala aur Manipur cover nahi hua. IIPS ne khud warning di hai ki kuch states mein sample chhote hain, aur shehron mein sample chunne ka frame bhi NFHS-5 se badal gaya hai [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

## Karnataka 44.4% se 14.1%, Kerala 9.8% se 17.7%

States ke numbers is puzzle ko aur uljha dete hain. NFHS-5 mein Karnataka India mein sabse upar tha: wahan 44.4% married women ne pati se physical ya sexual violence jheli thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. NFHS-6 mein Karnataka ka number 14.1% hai, yaani national average se bhi kaafi neeche. Kerala ulti disha mein gaya: 9.8% se 17.7% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Karnataka ki giravat tabhi sach ho sakti hai jab state ki zyada tar woh auratein, jinhe kabhi pati ne maara-peeta ya jinke saath sexual violence ki, survey ke do rounds ke beech ke kuch hi saalon mein survey ki age-range se bahar ho gayi hon. Umar ya society itni tezi se badle, yeh bahut mushkil hai. Haan, yeh zaroor badal sakta hai ki jawaab kisne diya, kahan diya aur kiske saamne diya.

Kerala ko samajhna bhi utna hi mushkil hai. 2024 mein 2005 ke Domestic Violence Act ke tahat poore desh mein police ne 616 criminal cases darj kiye, aur unmein se 496 akele Kerala mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Matlab wahan yeh law aise use hota hai jaise baaki jagah nahi hota. Kerala mein badhat ka matlab zyada violence bhi ho sakta hai, aur yeh bhi ki ab zyada auratein ise khul kar bata rahi hain. Fact sheets se yeh farq pata nahi chalta.

## Aurat surveyor ko kab batati hai, kab nahi

Aurat sach bataayegi ya nahi, yeh is par bhi tika hai ki aas-paas kaun sun raha hai. June 2026 mein Deccan Herald ne kuch experts ki raay chhaapi, jismein Mumbai se ek public-health researcher ki raay bhi hai. Unhe shak hai ki yeh giravat asli hai. Unka kehna hai ki family ke saamne auratein surveyor ko violence ke baare mein shayad na batayein, aur unhone yeh sawaal bhi uthaya ki kya interviews sach mein akele mein hue. Akhbaar ki headline thi ki yeh giravat "shayad sirf kaagaz par sach hai" [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]].

WHO bhi survey ke tareeke par aisi hi baat kehta hai: jo surveys sirf auraton par hone wali violence ke liye hote hain, unmein auratein shayad zyada batati hain, aur bade survey ke andar violence ke chhote module mein kam [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]]. NFHS doosri tarah ka survey hai. Iske violence wale sawaal family health par bane ek bade survey ka bas ek hissa hain.

Ab ek interview ki kalpana kijiye (yeh ek hypothetical example hai, koi asli case nahi). Haath mein tablet liye ek anjaan surveyor. Bagal ke kamre mein saas. Pati ke ghar lautne ka time hone wala hai. Lambe interview mein kaafi der baad sawaal aata hai: kya aapke pati ne kabhi...? "Haan" kehne ki use bahut badi keemat chukani pad sakti hai. "Nahi" kehne mein kuch nahi jaata. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% auraton ne na kabhi madad maangi thi, na kisi ko bataya tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Bahuton ke liye surveyor hi woh pehla insaan hota jise woh apni baat batatin. Isliye interview ke tareeke mein chhota sa badlav bhi numbers ko bahut hila sakta hai.

## Police ke numbers bhi ghate: violence kam hui ya complaints?

Police data bhi yahi kehta dikhta hai. Pati ya uske rishtedaaron ki cruelty ke darj cases 2022 mein 1,40,019 the, 2023 mein 1,33,676 hue [[ncrb-cii-2023]], aur 2024 mein 1,20,227 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab do alag sources ek hi direction dikhayein, toh yeh ek serious argument banta hai ki shayad sach mein kuch badal raha hai.

Lekin police ke numbers bhi isi par tike hain ki aurat bole aur police likhe. NCRB khud kehta hai ki darj crime ka badhna aur crime ka badhna do alag baatein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]], aur ghatne par bhi yahi baat laagu hoti hai. 1 July 2024 se BNSS ka Section 173(3) police ko ek chhoot deta hai: teen saal se lekar saat saal se kam saza wale crimes mein, DSP ki permission se, police FIR likhne se pehle 14 din tak preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. BNS ke Section 85 mein cruelty ki saza teen saal tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], isliye cruelty ki complaints bhi is daayre mein aa sakti hain. Jo complaint enquiry mein hi atki reh gayi, woh ginti mein kabhi nahi aati. Police ke poore numbers ki kahani hamari us story mein hai jo batati hai ki cruelty auraton ke khilaaf sabse bada crime kyun hai.

Asli giravat ka sabse mazboot saboot aise crime se aata hai jise chhupana kahin zyada mushkil hai. Darj dowry death cases 2022 mein 6,450 the, 2023 mein 6,156 aur 2024 mein 5,737 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is baat ko seriously lena chahiye. Par yeh ek alag crime hai, jo law ke ek alag section ke tahat gina jaata hai.

## "Violence ghati" wali headline kaise padhein

Paanch sawaal poochhiye. Pehla: kaunsa measure hai? Kabhi bhi jheli gayi violence, ya sirf pichhle ek saal ki? Sirf physical aur sexual, ya emotional bhi? Doosra: data final hai ya provisional? Teesra: kya tareeka badla? Sample, kaunse states cover hue, aur kamre mein kaun-kaun tha? Chautha: kya saare hisse aapas mein match karte hain, jaise kya kisi state mein lifetime number do-tihaai se zyada gir sakta hai? Paanchwaan: baaki sources violence ginte hain ya sirf complaints?

Asli giravat India ki auraton ke liye sabse achhi khabar hogi, aur koi nahi chahega ki yeh galat nikle. Lekin jab tak NFHS-6 ki poori report apna tareeka nahi samjhati, tab tak 22.3% ko aise padhiye: 2023-24 mein auratein ek anjaan insaan ko bas itna bata paayin. Yeh is baat ka paimana nahi hai ki unke band darwazon ke peeche asal mein kya hua.

one-stop-centres-cameras-before-shelters.en:
In July 2026 the government told the Rajya Sabha where the Nirbhaya Fund, India's main pot of money for women's safety, had gone. The biggest share, Rs 1,686.73 crore, went to Safe City projects in eight cities. One Stop Centres, the crisis centres for women facing violence, had received Rs 1,299.10 crore for the whole country [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Public spaces in eight cities got more than every crisis centre in India put together. What does that say about where India thinks women are in danger?

## Rs 1,686.73 crore for eight cities, Rs 1,299.10 crore for the centres

The fund was announced in the February 2013 Budget, weeks after the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, with Rs 1,000 crore; the Finance Minister said "recent incidents" had "cast a long, dark shadow" on India's credentials [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]]. By July 2026, Rs 7,990.85 crore had been set aside for it and Rs 1,287.83 crore, about 16%, was still unspent. Three schemes took 63% of everything released [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]:

| Nirbhaya Fund scheme | Released by July 2026 |
|---|---|
| Safe City projects, eight cities | Rs 1,686.73 crore |
| One Stop Centres, all India | Rs 1,299.10 crore |
| Fast-track courts for rape and POCSO cases | Rs 1,234.55 crore |

The government's reply counts money released and money used as one figure.

The eight cities are Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow and Mumbai. Their projects aim to make public places safer through better urban infrastructure and faster access to police [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. That is real work, but it is work on streets, stations and markets in eight cities, and it has cost more than the national network of centres meant to serve every district.

## From 'one in every district' to 985 centres

In December 2018, in the Nipun Saxena case, the Supreme Court asked every state and union territory to set up at least one One Stop Centre in every district within a year [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. That deadline fell in December 2019.

The count has risen since: 802 centres by March 2025 [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]] and 926 by March 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]]. By July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 centres approved were running, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

More than six years after that deadline, some approved centres are still not open. And "one per district" measures paperwork, not distance: one centre is one building and one team, however far away a woman lives.

Set 15.20 lakh women over eleven years against the need. In NFHS-5, 29.3% of ever-married women aged 18-49 reported physical or sexual violence by a husband, and 77.2% of women who had faced such violence from anyone never sought help or told a single person [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## What a centre can and cannot do at 2 am

Consider this situation. It is 2 am in a small town in Bundelkhand. A 24-year-old woman has been pushed out of her in-laws' house after a night of violence, with her phone and her one-year-old son. Her parents live in another district.

A One Stop Centre is built for this moment. It brings police help, medical care, legal aid, counselling and short-stay shelter under one roof, for women facing violence at home or outside it [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. The national Women Helpline can connect her to it, and 112 can send the police.

Now the limits. She has to know the centre exists and reach it, at night, with a baby, unless a helpline call brings someone to her. The shelter is short-stay: after it, she needs her parents, a longer-term home, or a magistrate's residence order under the Domestic Violence Act to return safely to her marital home [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. The centre cannot give her an income, and money often decides whether a woman can stay away.

By March 2025 police stations had 14,658 Women Help Desks [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Yet in NFHS-5 only 6.3% of women who sought help after violence went to the police; 60.9% turned to their own family [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. At 2 am, the real first responder is usually a mother or a brother on the phone.

## 21 shelters for transgender people forced out of home

Now imagine a 19-year-old trans woman whose family has thrown her out. The Centre's shelter scheme for destitute transgender persons, the Garima Greh, had 21 homes in 17 states by November 2025, under the SMILE scheme [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. In many states there is none. In August 2025, 429 people were living in these homes, and the Social Justice Ministry had released Rs 8.25 crore to them in all [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

The government still uses the 2011 Census count of 4,87,803 people in the "other" gender category as India's transgender population [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Not all of them need a shelter. But Rs 8.25 crore for these homes, against Rs 1,686.73 crore of Nirbhaya money for eight cities' public spaces, shows how far down the list a person thrown out by family sits. And by November 2025 only 20 states and union territories had set up the Transgender Protection Cells that 2020 rules required in every state [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

## Street safety or home safety: what the spending says

Police data point inside the home. Cruelty by a husband or his relatives was the largest category of crime against women in 2024: 1,20,227 cases, 27.2% of the 4,41,534 registered [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yet the fund keeps turning to surveillance of public space. By July 2026, an AI facial-recognition pilot at seven railway stations showed zero spending, and a proposal for CCTV cameras at village panchayats still awaited financial approval. A Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men on women's issues had also spent nothing [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Even the plan for villages was cameras, and the programme aimed at men had not spent a rupee.

Lit streets and faster police matter; women are harassed and attacked in public too. But a camera cannot see into a kitchen, and a control room cannot give a woman a bed. A safety budget should pass one test: if a woman is pushed out of her home at 2 am anywhere in India, can she reach a safe bed that night? Today the honest answer depends on her district, her phone battery and her family.
one-stop-centres-cameras-before-shelters.hg:
July 2026 mein sarkar ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki Nirbhaya Fund, yaani auraton ki safety ke liye India ka khaas fund, ka paisa kahan gaya. Sabse bada hissa, Rs 1,686.73 crore, aath shehron ke Safe City projects ko mila. One Stop Centres, yaani violence jhel rahi auraton ke liye bane crisis centres, ko poore desh ke liye Rs 1,299.10 crore mile [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Matlab aath shehron ki public jagahon ko India ke saare crisis centres ko milakar bhi zyada paisa mila. Isse kya pata chalta hai ki India ke hisaab se auratein asal mein kahan khatre mein hain?

## Aath shehron ke liye Rs 1,686.73 crore, centres ke liye Rs 1,299.10 crore

Yeh fund February 2013 ke Budget mein, 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ke kuch hi hafton baad, Rs 1,000 crore ke saath announce hua tha; Finance Minister ne kaha tha ki "recent incidents" ne India ki image par "a long, dark shadow" daal di hai [[indiabudget-speech-2013-14]]. July 2026 tak isme Rs 7,990.85 crore rakhe ja chuke the, aur Rs 1,287.83 crore, yaani qareeb 16%, ab tak kharch nahi hue the. Jitna paisa release hua, uska 63% sirf teen schemes mein gaya [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]:

| Nirbhaya Fund scheme | July 2026 tak release hua |
|---|---|
| Safe City projects, aath shehar | Rs 1,686.73 crore |
| One Stop Centres, poora India | Rs 1,299.10 crore |
| Rape aur POCSO cases ke fast-track courts | Rs 1,234.55 crore |

Sarkar ka jawab release hue paise aur kharch hue paise ko ek hi figure mein ginta hai.

Yeh aath shehar hain Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow aur Mumbai. In projects ka maqsad hai behtar urban infrastructure aur police tak jaldi pahunch ke zariye public jagahon ko safe banana [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Yeh asli kaam hai, par yeh kaam aath shehron ki sadkon, stations aur bazaaron par hai, aur iska kharch un centres ke poore national network se zyada hai jo har district ke liye bane hain.

## 'Har district mein ek' se 985 centres tak

December 2018 mein, Nipun Saxena case mein, Supreme Court ne har state aur union territory se kaha ki ek saal ke andar har district mein kam se kam ek One Stop Centre banaya jaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Yeh deadline December 2019 mein khatam ho gayi.

Tab se ginti badhi hai: March 2025 tak 802 centres [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]] aur March 2026 tak 926 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]]. July 2026 tak approved 1,033 centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se ab tak inhone 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad ki thi [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

Deadline ke chhe saal se zyada baad bhi kuch approved centres khule nahi hain. Aur "har district mein ek" kaagzi target hai, doori ka hisaab nahi: ek centre matlab ek building aur ek team, chahe aurat usse kitni bhi door rehti ho.

Ab gyarah saalon mein 15.20 lakh auraton ko zaroorat ke saamne rakhiye. NFHS-5 mein 18-49 saal ki 29.3% ever-married auraton ne pati ki taraf se physical ya sexual violence report ki, aur jin auraton ne kisi se bhi aisi violence jheli, unme se 77.2% ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ek insaan ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Raat ke 2 baje centre kya kar sakta hai, aur kya nahi

Sochiye. Bundelkhand ke ek chhote shehar mein raat ke 2 baje hain. 24 saal ki ek aurat ko raat bhar ki violence ke baad sasural se bahar nikaal diya gaya hai. Uske paas uska phone hai aur ek saal ka beta. Uske maa-baap doosre district mein rehte hain.

One Stop Centre isi pal ke liye bana hai. Yeh ek hi chhat ke neeche police help, medical care, legal aid, counselling aur kuch dinon ka shelter deta hai, un auraton ke liye jo ghar ke andar ya bahar violence jhel rahi hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. National Women Helpline use centre se jod sakti hai, aur 112 police bhej sakta hai.

Ab iski limits. Jab tak helpline call se koi use lene na aaye, use khud pata hona chahiye ki centre kahan hai, aur wahan pahunchna hoga, raat mein, ek bachche ke saath. Shelter short-stay hai: uske baad use maa-baap chahiye, ya lambe samay ka koi ghar, ya Domestic Violence Act ke under magistrate ka residence order, taaki woh safely sasural laut sake [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Centre use kamai nahi de sakta, aur aksar paisa hi tay karta hai ki aurat door reh paayegi ya nahi.

March 2025 tak police stations mein 14,658 Women Help Desks ban chuke the [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Phir bhi NFHS-5 mein violence ke baad madad maangne wali auraton mein se sirf 6.3% police ke paas gayi; 60.9% ne apni family ka sahara liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Raat ke 2 baje asli first responder aksar phone par maa ya bhai hota hai.

## Ghar se nikaale gaye transgender logon ke liye 21 shelters

Ab ek 19 saal ki trans woman ke baare mein sochiye jise uski family ne ghar se nikaal diya hai. Beghar transgender logon ke liye Centre ki shelter scheme, Garima Greh, ke November 2025 tak 17 states mein 21 homes the, SMILE scheme ke under [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Kai states mein ek bhi nahi hai. August 2025 mein in homes mein 429 log reh rahe the, aur Social Justice Ministry ne inhe kul milakar Rs 8.25 crore release kiye the [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Sarkar aaj bhi 2011 Census ke "other" gender category ke 4,87,803 logon ko India ki transgender population maanti hai [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Sabko shelter ki zaroorat nahi hai. Par in homes ke liye Rs 8.25 crore, aur aath shehron ki public jagahon ke liye Nirbhaya Fund ke Rs 1,686.73 crore: yeh farq dikhata hai ki family se nikaala gaya insaan sarkar ki list mein kitna neeche hai. Aur November 2025 tak sirf 20 states aur union territories ne woh Transgender Protection Cells banaye the jo 2020 ke rules har state mein zaroori karte hain [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

## Sadak ki safety ya ghar ki safety: kharch kya kehta hai

Police data ghar ke andar ki taraf ishaara karta hai. 2024 mein auraton ke khilaf crime ki sabse badi category pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty thi: 1,20,227 cases, yaani register hue 4,41,534 cases ka 27.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Phir bhi fund baar-baar public jagahon ki nigraani ki taraf mudta hai. July 2026 tak saat railway stations par AI facial recognition ke pilot par zero kharch dikha, aur village panchayats mein CCTV cameras ka proposal abhi bhi financial approval ke intezaar mein tha. Mardon ko auraton ke muddon par sensitise karne wale Panchayati Raj programme ne bhi kuch kharch nahi kiya tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Gaon ke liye bhi plan cameras ka tha, aur mardon ke liye bane programme ne ek rupaya bhi kharch nahi kiya tha.

Roshan sadkein aur jaldi pahunchne wali police zaroori hain; auraton ko public jagahon par bhi harass kiya jaata hai aur un par hamle hote hain. Par camera kitchen ke andar nahi dekh sakta, aur control room kisi aurat ko raat ka bistar nahi de sakta. Kisi bhi safety budget ko ek test paas karna chahiye: agar India mein kahin bhi kisi aurat ko raat 2 baje ghar se nikaal diya jaye, toh kya woh usi raat kisi safe bistar tak pahunch sakti hai? Aaj iska imaandaar jawab uske district, uske phone ki battery aur uski family par tika hai.

section-80-bns-dowry-death-explained.en:
Consider this situation. A 26-year-old woman in Jaipur dies at her in-laws' home, three years after her wedding. Her in-laws say it was an accident. Her parents say she had complained for months about demands for money and a car, and about how she was treated when they did not pay. Which law applies, and who has to prove what? The answer starts with Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). In 2024, police registered 5,737 cases under it and under its older form, Section 304B of the IPC [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This explainer is general information, not legal advice.

## The four ingredients of a 'dowry death'

Section 80 calls a woman's death a "dowry death" when four things come together [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

1. **The death.** She died of burns or bodily injury, or "otherwise than under normal circumstances".
2. **The window.** It happened within seven years of her marriage.
3. **The cruelty.** "Soon before her death", her husband or a relative of her husband subjected her to cruelty or harassment.
4. **The dowry link.** That cruelty or harassment was "for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry".

The punishment is at least seven years in prison and can extend to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

"Otherwise than under normal circumstances" is wide: the UN Office on Drugs and Crime notes that the provision can apply to any unnatural death of a woman within seven years of marriage [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]], which is why a suicide can be a dowry death too. The law does not fix a number of days for "soon before", so it turns on the facts of each case. The seven-year window is strict, but it covers the years when violence in a marriage often begins. In NFHS-5, 11.2% of currently married women who had married only once had first faced physical or sexual violence from their husband within two years of the wedding, and 20.9% within five [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## The clause that makes Section 80 different

Once those four ingredients are proved, the law deems the husband or the relative who harassed her to have caused her death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Normally the prosecution must prove who caused a death. A death inside a marital home often has no outside witness, and the people who know what happened may be the accused. The deeming clause closes that gap. In the Jaipur situation, the prosecution would need no one who saw how she died. It would need proof that the death was not natural, that it came within seven years of the wedding, and that cruelty or harassment over the money and the car came soon before it.

It is not automatic guilt. If the dowry-linked cruelty soon before the death is not proved, the presumption never starts, and the accused can contest every fact it rests on. That is why the record a woman leaves while alive matters so much: messages, call logs, letters, money transfers, and the people she told.

## 46.2% conviction, 93.6% pending

In 2024, courts had 63,516 dowry-death cases before them. They finished trials in only 4,043, and 1,869 of those ended in conviction, a conviction rate of 46.2%. At the end of the year, 59,446 cases, or 93.6%, were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

By Indian standards that rate is high. Across all crimes against women, courts convicted in 25.7% of completed trials in 2024, and in cases of cruelty by husbands or their relatives the figure was 20.1% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The data cannot show why these trials end in conviction more often; the deeming clause is one likely reason, not a proven one.

Two cautions. A rate of 46.2% still means that more than half of completed trials ended without a conviction. And with 59,446 cases in the queue, most families are still waiting for any verdict at all.

## Murder, abetment of suicide or dowry death: how a case is classed

One death can be filed under different sections, and the choice shapes the trial.

- **Murder** (Section 103 BNS, earlier Section 302 IPC) is charged where there is evidence of an intentional killing. In 2024, NCRB recorded 701 murders with dowry as the motive [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Because NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]], these are not also counted as dowry deaths.
- **Abetment of suicide** (Sections 107 and 108 BNS, earlier Sections 305 and 306 IPC) covers instigating or helping to bring about another person's suicide. Police registered 4,220 such cases with women as victims in 2024, for all reasons, not only dowry, and courts convicted in just 15.5% of completed trials [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Dowry death** (Section 80) applies only inside the seven-year window and only with dowry-linked cruelty. A woman who dies in the eighth year of her marriage cannot be a "dowry death" in law, however long the demands went on.
- **Cruelty** (Sections 85 and 86 BNS) covers wilful conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide or cause her grave injury, and harassment to force her or her family to meet unlawful demands for property. It carries up to three years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. It is the charge that can protect a woman while she is alive.

If this has brought up thoughts of suicide for you or someone you know, call Tele-MANAS, the national mental-health helpline, on 14416 [[tele-manas]].

## From IPC 304B to BNS 80 on 1 July 2024

The offence is not new. Section 304B entered the IPC in 1986 [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]]. When the BNS replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], dowry death became Section 80, with the same definition and the same punishment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The date of the offence decides the section, not the date of the complaint. That is why NCRB's 2024 count is split: 3,057 cases under Section 304B for deaths before 1 July and 2,680 under Section 80 for deaths from 1 July [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. To compare years, use the total, 5,737; our guide to India's first BNS-era crime data explains the two columns.

For a family, little changes: the ingredients are the same under either section. Under the new procedure code, whoever files the FIR must get a free copy, and police must tell the informant how the investigation is going within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
section-80-bns-dowry-death-explained.hg:
Sochiye, Jaipur mein 26 saal ki ek aurat ki maut sasural mein ho jaati hai, shaadi ke teen saal baad. Sasural wale kehte hain ki accident tha. Uske maa-baap kehte hain ki woh mahino se paise aur car ki demand ki shikayat kar rahi thi, aur yeh bhi batati thi ki paise na milne par uske saath kaisa bartaav hota tha. Ab kaunsa law lagega, aur kise kya prove karna hoga? Iska jawab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 80 se shuru hota hai. 2024 mein police ne is Section aur iske purane roop, IPC ke Section 304B, ke under 5,737 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh explainer general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 'Dowry death' ki chaar shartein

Section 80 kisi aurat ki maut ko "dowry death" tab kehta hai jab yeh chaar cheezein ek saath hon [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

1. **Maut.** Uski maut jalne se ya body par chot se hui, ya "normal circumstances se hatkar" hui.
2. **Time window.** Maut shaadi ke saat saal ke andar hui.
3. **Cruelty.** Maut se "kuch hi pehle" uske pati ya pati ke kisi relative ne uske saath cruelty ki, ya use harass kiya.
4. **Dowry link.** Yeh cruelty ya harassment dowry ki kisi demand ke liye thi, ya usse judi thi.

Saza kam se kam saat saal jail hai, jo life imprisonment tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

"Normal circumstances se hatkar" bahut wide hai: UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) batata hai ki yeh provision shaadi ke saat saal ke andar kisi aurat ki kisi bhi unnatural death par lag sakta hai [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]], isiliye suicide bhi dowry death ho sakta hai. "Kuch hi pehle" ke liye law dinon ki koi ginti tay nahi karta, isliye yeh har case ke facts par tika hota hai. Saat saal ki limit strict hai, par isme wahi saal aate hain jab shaadi mein violence aksar shuru hoti hai. NFHS-5 mein, jo auratein survey ke waqt shaadishuda thin aur jinki ek hi baar shaadi hui thi, unmein se 11.2% ke saath pati ki physical ya sexual violence shaadi ke do saal ke andar shuru ho gayi thi, aur paanch saal ke andar yeh number 20.9% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Woh clause jo Section 80 ko alag banata hai

Agar yeh chaar shartein prove ho jayein, toh law maan leta hai ki uski maut ke zimmedar wahi pati ya relative hain jinhone use harass kiya tha [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Normally prosecution ko prove karna hota hai ki maut kisne ki. Par sasural ke andar hui maut ka aksar koi bahar ka gawah nahi hota, aur jo log jaante hain ki kya hua, woh khud accused ho sakte hain. Yeh "deeming" clause isi gap ko bharta hai. Jaipur wali situation mein prosecution ko kisi aise insaan ki zaroorat nahi hogi jisne maut hote dekhi ho. Use yeh proof chahiye hoga ki maut natural nahi thi, shaadi ke saat saal ke andar hui, aur paise aur car ko lekar cruelty ya harassment maut se kuch hi pehle hui thi.

Iska matlab automatic saza nahi hai. Agar maut se kuch hi pehle dowry ke liye hui cruelty prove na ho, toh law yeh maankar chalta hi nahi, aur accused us har baat ko challenge kar sakte hain jis par yeh presumption tika hai. Isiliye woh record bahut maayne rakhta hai jo ek aurat apne jeete-ji chhodti hai: messages, call logs, chitthiyan, money transfers, aur woh log jinhe usne apni baat batayi.

## 46.2% conviction, 93.6% pending

2024 mein courts ke saamne dowry death ke 63,516 cases the. Inme se sirf 4,043 ke trials poore hue, aur unme se 1,869 mein conviction hua, yaani conviction rate 46.2% raha. Saal ke end mein 59,446 cases, yaani 93.6%, abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

India ke hisaab se yeh rate ooncha hai. 2024 mein auraton ke khilaf saare crimes ko milakar, jin trials ka faisla aaya unme se 25.7% mein conviction hua, aur pati ya uske rishtedaron ki cruelty ke cases mein yeh 20.1% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data yeh nahi bata sakta ki in trials mein zyada conviction kyun hota hai; deeming clause ek mumkin wajah hai, proven wajah nahi.

Do baatein yaad rakhiye. 46.2% rate ka matlab yeh bhi hai ki poore hue aadhe se zyada trials mein conviction nahi hua. Aur 59,446 cases abhi bhi line mein hain, yaani zyada tar families abhi bhi kisi bhi faisle ka intezaar kar rahi hain.

## Murder, abetment of suicide ya dowry death: case kis section mein jaata hai

Ek hi maut alag-alag sections mein file ho sakti hai, aur section se tay hota hai ki trial kis raaste chalega.

- **Murder** (BNS Section 103, pehle IPC Section 302) tab lagta hai jab jaan-boojhkar maarne ke saboot hon. 2024 mein NCRB ne 701 aise murders darj kiye jinka motive dowry tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar, uske sabse serious offence ke naam se ginta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]], isliye yeh dowry death mein dobara nahi gine jaate.
- **Abetment of suicide** (BNS Section 107 aur 108, pehle IPC Section 305 aur 306) tab lagta hai jab koi kisi ko suicide ke liye uksaaye ya usme madad kare. 2024 mein police ne aise 4,220 cases register kiye jinme victim auratein thi, har tarah ki wajah se, sirf dowry nahi, aur jin trials ka faisla aaya unme sirf 15.5% mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Dowry death** (Section 80) sirf saat saal ki limit ke andar, aur sirf dowry se judi cruelty par lagti hai. Jis aurat ki maut shaadi ke aathvein saal mein ho, woh law mein "dowry death" nahi ho sakti, chahe demands kitne bhi saal chali hon.
- **Cruelty** (BNS Section 85 aur 86) mein jaan-boojhkar kiya gaya aisa bartaav aata hai jo kisi aurat ko suicide ki taraf dhakel sakta ho ya use gambhir nuksaan pahuncha sakta ho, aur woh harassment bhi jo aurat ya uski family se property ki illegal demand poori karwane ke liye ho. Isme teen saal tak jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yahi woh charge hai jo kisi aurat ko uske jeete-ji bacha sakta hai.

Agar yeh padhkar aapke man mein, ya aapke kisi jaanne wale ke man mein, suicide ka khayal aa raha hai, toh sarkar ki national mental health helpline Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye [[tele-manas]].

## 1 July 2024 ko IPC 304B se BNS 80 tak

Yeh offence naya nahi hai. Section 304B 1986 mein IPC mein joda gaya tha [[unodc-gsh-gender-killing-2018]]. 1 July 2024 ko jab BNS ne IPC ki jagah li [[ncrb-cii-2024]], toh dowry death Section 80 ban gayi, wahi definition aur wahi saza ke saath [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section offence ki date se tay hota hai, complaint ki date se nahi. Isiliye NCRB ka 2024 ka count do hisson mein bata hai: 1 July se pehle ki maut ke 3,057 cases Section 304B mein, aur 1 July se hui maut ke 2,680 cases Section 80 mein [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Saalon ko compare karna ho toh total 5,737 hi lijiye; BNS ke baad aaye pehle crime data par hamari guide in do columns ko samjhati hai.

Family ke liye asal mein zyada kuch nahi badalta: dono sections mein shartein wahi hain. Naye procedure law (BNSS) mein, jo FIR darj karwaye use uski copy free milni chahiye, aur police ko 90 din ke andar informant ko batana hota hai ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

section-85-86-bns-cruelty-explained.en:
Say "498A" in an Indian living room and you will hear "dowry" and "misuse", rarely what the law says. Yet it is the criminal law used most against violence at home: in 2024 police registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives, the single largest category of crimes against women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Since 1 July 2024 the offence sits in Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced the Indian Penal Code; cases about conduct from before that date are still registered under Section 498A of the IPC, which is why the 2024 police count mixes both laws [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This explainer, general information and not legal advice, reads both sections line by line.

## The text of Sections 85 and 86

Section 85 is one sentence. A husband, or a relative of the husband, who "subjects such woman to cruelty" can be jailed for up to three years "and shall also be liable to fine" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. It does not define cruelty.

Section 86 does, in two limbs [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

- **(a)** "any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman"; or
- **(b)** "harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security", or harassment because she or her family failed to meet such a demand.

Three words do most of the work. "Wilful" means deliberate. "Likely" means the law looks at what the conduct would probably do to her; it does not wait for the injury. And "mental" means harm to her mind counts as much as harm to her body.

## Conduct that counts: threats, humiliation, danger to health

Consider this situation. A 27-year-old in Nagpur has been married two years. Her husband reads her phone every night, threatens to throw her out without her child if she "talks back", mocks her before his relatives and stops her visiting her parents. His mother joins in. He has never hit her. She has stopped sleeping, and a doctor has prescribed medicine for anxiety.

Under limb (a), the question is not whether he hit her but whether this deliberate pattern is likely to endanger her health, mental or physical. The doctor's record is evidence of exactly that. Her mother-in-law can be named too, because Section 85 covers the husband's relatives [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The words "wilful" and "grave" set a high bar: the conduct must be deliberate and serious. Beatings plainly do, and so can threats, confinement and humiliation that leave no mark.

## Money and property demands

Now consider a second situation. Eight months after a wedding in Meerut, the groom's family says a car was "expected". The bride's father cannot afford one. They stop speaking to her, send her back to her parents and message that she can return when the car comes.

That is limb (b): harassment to coerce her or "any person related to her" into meeting an unlawful demand for property, or harassment because the demand was not met [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The demand need not be called dowry or come before the wedding, and can be aimed at her parents. "Any property" covers money for a business or a plot of land as much as a car.

The same demand can also be a separate offence under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, which punishes demanding dowry with six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

## What Section 85 does not cover

**Rape by a husband.** Exception 2 to Section 63 BNS says sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A wife can describe forced sex in a cruelty complaint where it meets the Section 86 test, but it is then charged as cruelty, with a three-year maximum. Only if the couple live apart does Section 67 punish forced sex by a husband, with two to seven years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. As of 20 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on the challenge to the marital exception [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

**Anyone outside the husband's family.** A woman abused by her own father or brother, a man abused at home, or a partner in a same-sex relationship cannot use Section 85. They must rely on other laws, such as voluntarily causing hurt, with up to one year under Section 115(2) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Women can also seek a protection order under the 2005 Domestic Violence Act; breaking one is itself an offence, with up to one year in prison or a fine of up to Rs 20,000 [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## Describing cruelty in a complaint

A complaint needs no legal language, only facts an officer can check:

- **What happened, when and where,** in order. "Since March 2025 he locks me in the bedroom when I ask to visit my mother" beats "he tortures me".
- **Who did what.** Name each person with their own acts; vague allegations against a whole family weaken a complaint.
- **What it did to you:** dated notes and prescriptions from a doctor or counsellor, which link the conduct to "danger to life, limb or health".
- **Every demand:** what, by whom, when, and the messages, call logs or transfers that show it.
- **Who you told,** and when.

Because Section 85 carries up to three years, Section 173(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) lets police, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering an FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. You can file at any police station, whatever the area where the offence happened (a Zero FIR), or as an e-FIR signed within 3 days, and you must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Police act on most of these complaints: of 1,20,390 cruelty cases they disposed of in 2024, they charge-sheeted 1,08,574, a rate of 90.2%, and closed 4,593, about 3.8%, as "false" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The long wait comes later, in court, where 92.2% of cruelty cases were pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

If this has left you thinking of ending your life, call Tele-MANAS on 14416 [[tele-manas]].
section-85-86-bns-cruelty-explained.hg:
Kisi bhi Indian drawing room mein "498A" boliye, toh "dowry" aur "misuse" sunne ko milega, yeh bahut kam ki law asal mein kehta kya hai. Phir bhi ghar ki violence ke khilaf sabse zyada yahi criminal law use hota hai: 2024 mein police ne pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye, jo auraton ke khilaf crimes ki sabse badi single category hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 1 July 2024 se yeh offence Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Sections 85 aur 86 mein hai, jisne Indian Penal Code ki jagah li; us date se pehle ke bartaav wale cases ab bhi IPC ke Section 498A mein register hote hain, isliye 2024 ke police count mein dono laws mile hue hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh explainer dono sections ko line by line padhta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Sections 85 aur 86 ka text

Section 85 sirf ek sentence hai. Jo pati, ya pati ka koi relative, kisi aurat ke saath cruelty karta hai ("subjects such woman to cruelty"), use teen saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai, aur "shall also be liable to fine", yaani fine bhi lagega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh section cruelty ki definition nahi deta.

Woh kaam Section 86 karta hai, do hisson mein [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

- **(a)** "any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman"; ya
- **(b)** "harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security", ya phir aisi harassment jo isliye ho ki woh ya uski family aisi demand poori nahi kar paayi.

Saara wazan teen shabdon par hai. "Wilful" yaani jaan-boojhkar. "Likely" yaani law yeh dekhta hai ki us bartaav se use kya nuksaan hone ki sambhavna hai; woh chot lagne ka intezaar nahi karta. Aur "mental" yaani uske mann ko pahuncha nuksaan utna hi maayne rakhta hai jitna uske shareer ko.

## Kaunsa bartaav count hota hai: dhamkiyan, zillat, health ko khatra

Sochiye. Nagpur mein 27 saal ki ek aurat ki shaadi ko do saal hue hain. Uska pati har raat uska phone padhta hai, dhamki deta hai ki agar usne "palat ke jawab diya" toh use bachche ke bina ghar se nikaal dega, apne relatives ke saamne uska mazaak udaata hai, aur use maayke jaane se rokta hai. Uski maa bhi saath deti hai. Pati ne kabhi haath nahi uthaya. Aurat ki neend ud chuki hai, aur doctor ne use anxiety ki dawai di hai.

Limb (a) mein sawaal yeh nahi ki usne maara ya nahi, balki yeh ki kya yeh jaan-boojhkar chalaya gaya pattern uski mental ya physical health ko khatre mein daal sakta hai. Doctor ka record isi baat ka saboot hai. Saas ka naam bhi complaint mein aa sakta hai, kyunki Section 85 pati ke relatives ko bhi cover karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

"Wilful" aur "grave" shabd bar ko ooncha rakhte hain: bartaav jaan-boojhkar aur gambhir hona chahiye. Maar-peet saaf taur par aati hai, aur aisi dhamkiyan, band karke rakhna aur zaleel karna bhi aa sakta hai jiska koi nishaan nahi dikhta.

## Paise aur property ki demand

Ab ek doosri situation sochiye. Meerut mein shaadi ke aath mahine baad, ladke wale kehte hain ki car toh "expected" thi. Ladki ke pita ke paas itne paise nahi hain. Woh usse baat karna band kar dete hain, use maayke bhej dete hain aur message karte hain ki car aayegi tabhi wapas aana.

Yeh limb (b) hai: use ya "any person related to her" ko property ki gair-kanooni demand poori karne par majboor karne ke liye harassment, ya demand poori na hone ki wajah se harassment [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Demand ka naam dowry hona zaroori nahi, uska shaadi se pehle hona bhi zaroori nahi, aur pressure uske maa-baap par bhi daala ja sakta hai. "Any property" mein business ke liye paise ya zameen ka plot bhi utna hi aata hai jitni car.

Yahi demand Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ke under ek alag offence bhi ho sakti hai, jo dowry maangne par chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail deta hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

## Section 85 mein kya nahi aata

**Pati dwara rape.** Section 63 BNS ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki koi aadmi apni patni ke saath, agar patni 18 se kam umar ki nahi hai, sexual intercourse ya sexual acts kare, toh woh rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Patni zabardasti sex ko cruelty complaint mein likh sakti hai jahan woh Section 86 ke test par khara utre, par tab case cruelty ka hi banega, jiski maximum saza teen saal hai. Sirf tab, jab couple alag reh raha ho, Section 67 pati ki zabardasti par do se saat saal ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 20 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne marital exception ke challenge par faisla nahi diya tha [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

**Pati ki family ke bahar ka koi bhi.** Jis aurat ko uske apne pita ya bhai satate hain, jis aadmi ke saath ghar mein abuse hota hai, ya same-sex relationship mein koi partner, yeh sab Section 85 use nahi kar sakte. Unhe doosre laws ka sahara lena padta hai, jaise voluntarily causing hurt, jisme Section 115(2) ke under ek saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Auratein 2005 ke Domestic Violence Act ke under protection order bhi maang sakti hain; use todna khud ek offence hai, jisme ek saal tak ki jail ya Rs 20,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## Complaint mein cruelty kaise likhein

Complaint mein legal bhasha ki zaroorat nahi, bas aise facts chahiye jinhe officer check kar sake:

- **Kya hua, kab aur kahan,** sahi order mein. "March 2025 se jab bhi main maa se milne jaane ko kehti hoon, woh mujhe bedroom mein band kar deta hai" likhna "woh mujhe torture karta hai" se kahin zyada mazboot hai.
- **Kisne kya kiya.** Har insaan ka naam uske apne kaam ke saath likhiye; poori family ke khilaf gol-mol aarop complaint ko kamzor karte hain.
- **Aap par kya asar hua:** doctor ya counsellor ke date wale notes aur prescriptions, jo is bartaav ko "danger to life, limb or health" se jodte hain.
- **Har demand:** kya maanga, kisne, kab, aur woh messages, call logs ya transfers jo ise dikhate hain.
- **Aapne kise bataya,** aur kab.

Kyunki Section 85 mein teen saal tak ki saza hai, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 173(3) police ko, Deputy Superintendent ki permission se, FIR register karne se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry karne deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Aap kisi bhi police station mein complaint kar sakte hain, chahe offence kisi bhi area mein hua ho (Zero FIR), ya e-FIR ke through, jise 3 din ke andar sign karna hota hai, aur FIR ki copy aapko free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Police in zyada tar complaints par action leti hai: 2024 mein police ne jin 1,20,390 cruelty cases ko dispose kiya, unme se 1,08,574 mein charge-sheet hui, yaani 90.2% ka rate, aur 4,593, lagbhag 3.8%, "false" bolkar band kiye gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lamba intezaar baad mein court mein hota hai, jahan saal ke end tak 92.2% cruelty cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Agar is sab se aapke mann mein apni jaan lene ke khayal aa rahe hain, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call kijiye [[tele-manas]].

violence-after-separation-former-husband.en:
Consider a 29-year-old in Indore who moved back to her parents' home with her son last year. The divorce case has barely begun. Her husband calls from new numbers, waits outside her office and insists on seeing the boy at her parents' gate, where the shouting starts again. Everyone tells her the worst is over because she has left. The data, and the law, suggest otherwise. This explainer is general information, not legal advice.

## Former husbands in the data

NFHS-5 (2019-21) asked ever-married women aged 18-49 who had faced sexual violence to name the perpetrator. 82% named their current husband and 14% a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That is about one survivor in seven.

The survey does not say when the violence happened, and some of it took place while the marriage still stood. But ending a marriage does not take a man out of the data, and it changes who speaks. Women abused only by a former husband were twice as likely to have sought help as women abused only by their current husband: 23.6% against 11.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. If more women seek help once a marriage is over, the system has to be ready for the months after separation.

Police data acknowledge the risk without measuring it. NCRB's 2024 table of known accused in rape cases puts "separated husbands" in one group with friends, online friends and live-in partners on the pretext of marriage: 13,879 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. How many were husbands, the table does not say.

## Section 67: a lesser crime for a separated husband

Indian law still says that sex forced on a wife aged 18 or older by her husband is not rape (Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Separation opens one narrow door. Under Section 67, a husband who has sex with his wife without her consent while she is living separately, "whether under a decree of separation or otherwise", faces 2 to 7 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Two things follow. She does not need a court decree; living apart is enough. And the punishment is lighter than for any other man: rape under Section 64 carries at least 10 years and up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The law treats forced sex by a man she has left as less serious than the same act by a stranger, at the very moment she is trying to get away from him.

The exception speaks only of a man and "his own wife" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. But a contested divorce can take years, and for that whole stretch a separated wife is still his wife in law, so Section 67, not the rape law, is what applies.

## Stalking, threats and protection orders

Much of what follows separation is pursuit, and the BNS treats stalking as a crime of its own under Section 78, with up to 3 years in prison, and up to 5 on a repeat conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 9,865 stalking cases across India in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A woman's complaint of stalking must be recorded by a woman police officer or another woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If he threatens to share private photos, know that sharing a private image without consent is voyeurism under Section 77, even if she agreed to the photo being taken, with 1 to 3 years on a first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Report it on cybercrime.gov.in or the 1930 helpline [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

The Domestic Violence Act, 2005 adds civil remedies: protection, residence and maintenance orders that a woman asks a magistrate for, with a Protection Officer meant to help her [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. But breaking a protection order is punishable with at most a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]], a third of the maximum for stalking. A broken order and a Protection Officer's failure of duty are the Act's only crimes. Police registered just 616 cases under it in all of India in 2024, and of 4,017 such cases before the courts that year, trials were completed in only 84 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Planning the months after leaving

The law's tools work best when a woman uses them early and keeps a record.

- **Ask about an order early.** While the divorce or maintenance case is still pending, ask a Protection Officer, a One Stop Centre or a legal-aid lawyer whether a protection order fits your case, and spell out exactly what you need to stop: calls, messages, visits to your home or office.
- **Keep copies everywhere.** On your phone, with someone you trust, and at your local police station.
- **Log everything.** Date, time, the number he used, what he said or did, screenshots, voice notes, and anyone who saw.
- **Plan handovers.** Contact over children puts you face to face with him. Use a public place or a trusted third person.
- **Lock down your phone.** Change passwords, sign out of shared accounts and check location sharing.

If he forces sex on you, you do not have to wait for the divorce to go to the police. Under the BNSS, information about a cognizable offence can be given at any police station, wherever it happened, and the victim must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Where to get help

In danger, call 112 [[mha-erss]]. One Stop Centres offer police help, medical and legal aid, counselling and short-stay shelter under one roof [[wcd-mission-shakti]]; 985 were operational across India in July 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Free legal aid is available through the District Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]], and a legal-aid lawyer can tell you which of these laws fits your situation.

Leaving is often treated as the end of the story. The data say it can open a new chapter of risk, and the law should take that chapter as seriously as the marriage before it.
violence-after-separation-former-husband.hg:
Sochiye, Indore ki ek 29 saal ki woman pichhle saal apne bete ko lekar maa-baap ke ghar laut aayi. Divorce case abhi mushkil se shuru hua hai. Uska husband naye-naye numbers se call karta hai, uske office ke bahar intezaar karta hai, aur bete se milne ki zid karta hai, unke gate pe, jahan chillana phir se shuru ho jaata hai. Sab kehte hain ki sabse bura waqt nikal gaya, kyunki woh chhod aayi hai. Data aur law, dono kuch aur kehte hain. Yeh explainer general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Data mein former husbands

NFHS-5 (2019-21) ne sexual violence jhel chuki 18-49 saal ki ever-married women se perpetrator ka naam poochha. 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya aur 14% ne former husband ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani lagbhag har saat mein se ek survivor.

Survey yeh nahi batata ki violence kab hui, aur iska kuch hissa shaadi ke rehte hi hua tha. Lekin shaadi khatam hone se aadmi data se bahar nahi ho jaata, aur isse yeh badal jaata hai ki kaun bolta hai. Sirf former husband se abuse jhelne wali women mein help maangne ki dar, sirf current husband se abuse jhelne wali women se dugni thi: 23.6% ke muqable 11.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Agar shaadi khatam hone ke baad zyada women help maangti hain, toh system ko separation ke baad ke mahino ke liye taiyaar rehna hoga.

Police data is khatre ko maanta hai, par naapta nahi. NCRB ki 2024 ki table, jo rape cases mein known accused dikhati hai, "separated husbands" ko friends, online friends aur shaadi ka jhaansa dene wale live-in partners ke saath ek hi group mein rakhti hai: 13,879 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Inme se kitne husbands the, table nahi batati.

## Section 67: alag rehne wale husband ke liye halka crime

Indian law aaj bhi kehta hai ki 18 ya usse badi wife ke saath husband ka zabardasti sex rape nahi hai (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 63 ka Exception 2) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Separation ek patla sa darwaaza kholta hai. Section 67 ke under, jo husband alag reh rahi wife ke saath uski consent ke bina sex karta hai, "chahe separation ki decree ke under ya kisi aur tarah", use 2 se 7 saal ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Isse do baatein nikalti hain. Woman ko court decree ki zaroorat nahi; alag rehna kaafi hai. Aur saza kisi bhi doosre aadmi se kam hai: Section 64 ke under rape pe kam se kam 10 saal aur umr qaid tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Law us aadmi ke zabardasti sex ko, jise woh chhod chuki hai, kisi anjaan aadmi ke wahi kaam se kam serious maanta hai, theek us waqt jab woh usse door jaane ki koshish kar rahi hoti hai.

Exception sirf aadmi aur "uski apni wife" ki baat karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Lekin contested divorce mein saalon lag sakte hain, aur us poore waqt alag rehne wali wife law ki nazar mein ab bhi uski wife hai, isliye rape law nahi, Section 67 laagu hota hai.

## Stalking, dhamkiyan aur protection orders

Separation ke baad zyada tar jo hota hai, woh peecha karna hai, aur BNS stalking ko Section 78 ke under ek alag crime maanta hai, jiski saza 3 saal tak ki jail hai, aur dobara conviction pe 5 saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne stalking ke 9,865 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kisi woman ki stalking ki complaint ek woman police officer ya kisi aur woman officer ko hi record karni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar woh private photos share karne ki dhamki de, toh jaan lijiye ki bina consent private image share karna Section 77 ke under voyeurism hai, chahe photo uski marzi se li gayi ho, aur pehle conviction pe 1 se 3 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Iski report cybercrime.gov.in pe ya 1930 helpline pe kijiye [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

Domestic Violence Act, 2005 civil remedies deta hai: protection, residence aur maintenance orders, jo woman magistrate se maangti hai, aur Protection Officer ka kaam isme uski madad karna hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Lekin protection order todne pe zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]], jo stalking ki maximum saza ka ek-tihaai hai.
