Toota hua order aur Protection Officer ka apni duty na nibhaana hi is Act ke under crimes hain. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne iske under sirf 616 cases register kiye, aur us saal courts ke saamne aise 4,017 cases mein se sirf 84 ka trial poora hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Chhodne ke baad ke mahino ki planning

Law ke tools tab sabse achha kaam karte hain jab woman unhe jaldi use kare aur record rakhe.

- **Order ke baare mein jaldi poochhiye.** Divorce ya maintenance case chalte hue hi kisi Protection Officer, One Stop Centre ya legal-aid lawyer se poochhiye ki protection order aapke case mein fit baithta hai ya nahi, aur saaf bataiye ki aap kya band karwana chahti hain: calls, messages, ghar ya office aana.
- **Copies har jagah rakhiye.** Apne phone mein, kisi bharosemand insaan ke paas, aur apne local police station mein.
- **Sab kuch record kijiye.** Date, time, usne kaun sa number use kiya, kya kaha ya kiya, screenshots, voice notes, aur kisne dekha.
- **Handover plan kijiye.** Bachchon ke maamle mein milna aapko uske aamne-saamne la deta hai. Public jagah ya kisi bharosemand teesre insaan ka sahara lijiye.
- **Apna phone surakshit kijiye.** Passwords badliye, shared accounts se sign out kijiye aur location sharing check kijiye.

Agar woh aapke saath zabardasti sex kare, toh police ke paas jaane ke liye divorce ka intezaar karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. BNSS ke under cognizable offence ki information kisi bhi police station pe di ja sakti hai, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho, aur victim ko FIR ki copy free mein milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Madad kahan milegi

Khatre mein hon toh 112 pe call kijiye [[mha-erss]]. One Stop Centres ek hi chhat ke neeche police help, medical aur legal aid, counselling aur thode samay ka shelter dete hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]]; July 2026 mein poore India mein 985 centres chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. District Legal Services Authority se free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]], aur legal-aid lawyer bata sakta hai ki in mein se kaun sa law aapke case mein fit baithta hai.

Chhod dene ko aksar kahani ka ant maana jaata hai. Data kehta hai ki isse khatre ka ek naya chapter bhi khul sakta hai, aur law ko us chapter ko utni hi gambhirta se lena chahiye jitna usse pehle ki shaadi ko.

why-doesnt-she-just-leave.en:
Consider a 24-year-old in Pune. Her husband hits her, checks her phone and decides whom she may meet. She has a two-year-old son, no income of her own, and her wedding jewellery sits in her in-laws' locker. When a cousin finally hears, she asks the question almost everyone asks: why doesn't she just leave?

It sounds like concern. It works as a verdict: if she stays, it cannot be that bad, or she has chosen it. The question looks at the woman and skips the doors she would have to walk through. Here are four of them, and what the evidence says about each.

## The myth: if it were that bad, she would leave

Most women in her position never tell anyone, let alone leave. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told a single person; only 14.1% had sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Silence is not acceptance. It is usually a calculation about what telling would cost and who would actually help. The myth reads that calculation as proof that things are fine. The exits below show why it so often comes out the same way.

## Exit one: a family that says 'adjust'

Those who do look for help mostly turn to their own people. Of women who sought help after violence, 60.9% went to their own family; 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

So the first exit runs through her parents' house. In our hypothetical, her mother's answer is one word: adjust. Think of the child. What will people say? Her parents may also be weighing a younger sister's marriage, or the money already spent on hers. A family that says "adjust" does more than refuse her a room. It tells her the problem is her patience, not his violence.

NFHS records where women went for help, not what they were told when they got there. That second number does not exist, and it may matter more.

## Exit two: no income of her own

Leaving with a child means rent, a deposit, school fees and, sooner or later, a lawyer. In 2023-24 only 28.0% of urban women aged 15 and above were in the labour force, meaning working or looking for work [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. That is up from 20.4% in 2017-18, but still leaves more than seven in ten outside it. For most women in a city like Pune, leaving means leaving without a salary.

Even a salary may not be hers to spend. Abuse often runs through money: wages handed over, jewellery kept "safe", no bank account in her own name. The 2005 Domestic Violence Act is mainly a civil law: instead of a prison sentence, a magistrate can issue protection, residence and maintenance orders [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. But an order has to be applied for, argued and enforced, which takes time and money she may not have.

## Exits three and four: a case that takes years, and a bed for a few nights

The criminal route is slow. In 2024 Indian courts had 9,27,199 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives before them. They completed trials in 53,137, convicted in 10,689, a conviction rate of 20.1%, and left 92.2% pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More cases, 16,396, ended in compromise than in conviction. That can mean reconciliation or pressure on the woman; the data do not say which [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For a 24-year-old, a case still pending when her son starts school is not an exit. It is a second front.

The civil route has weak teeth. Breaking a protection order under the Domestic Violence Act is punishable with at most a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Police registered only 616 cases under the whole Act in 2024, and 496 of them were in Kerala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Outside one state, a broken order rarely becomes a police case.

Then there is the night itself. By July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 One Stop Centres approved across India were running, and they had helped over 15.20 lakh women since 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. They bring police help, legal aid, counselling and a short stay under one roof [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. The Supreme Court asked in 2018 for at least one in every district [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]: a start, not a door within reach of every woman. And a short stay is a breathing space, not a new home.

## Truth: leaving is a process, and it needs support

Leaving is rarely one decision on one night. A woman tests the exits: she tells a sister, goes to her parents for a week, asks about a job, sees a lawyer once. Each door that stays shut sends her back, and teaches the man she lives with that she has nowhere to go.

Help and leaving move together. Women abused only by a former husband were twice as likely to have sought help as women abused only by their current husband: 23.6% against 11.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey cannot say which came first. Either way, the women still living with their abuser are less likely to have told anyone, which is why their silence should never be read as "it can't be that bad".

> Staying is often not a choice to accept violence. It is a judgment that the exits are shut, for now.

The same question is put to men and queer people in abusive relationships, who have even fewer doors: the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, as its name says, is written for women [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

What would make leaving possible is not courage she lacks. It is a family that says "come home", money in her own name, orders that police enforce, cases that end, and a bed she can reach tonight. The honest question is not why she stays. It is what she would need to go, and who will help her get it.
why-doesnt-she-just-leave.hg:
Pune ki ek 24 saal ki ladki ke baare mein sochiye. Uska husband use maarta hai, uska phone check karta hai, aur tay karta hai ki woh kisse mil sakti hai. Uska do saal ka beta hai, apni koi kamai nahi hai, aur shaadi ke gehne sasural ke locker mein rakhe hain. Jab ek cousin ko aakhir pata chalta hai, toh woh wahi sawaal poochti hai jo lagbhag sab poochte hain: woh chhod kyun nahi deti?

Sunne mein yeh fikr lagti hai. Asal mein yeh ek faisla sunata hai: agar woh ruki hai, toh itna bura nahi hoga, ya usne khud yeh chuna hai. Yeh sawaal aurat ko dekhta hai, aur un darwaazon ko chhod deta hai jinse use guzarna padega. Yeh rahe unme se chaar, aur har ek ke baare mein evidence kya kehta hai.

## Myth: agar itna bura hota, toh woh chhod deti

Uski jaisi situation mein zyada tar women kisi ko batati tak nahi, chhodna toh door ki baat hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% women ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ek insaan ko bataya; sirf 14.1% ne help maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Chup rehna maan lena nahi hai. Aksar yeh ek hisaab hota hai: batane ki kya keemat chukani padegi, aur asal mein madad kaun karega. Myth is hisaab ko saboot maan leta hai ki sab theek hai. Neeche ke raaste dikhate hain ki yeh hisaab baar-baar ek hi jawab pe kyun pahunchta hai.

## Pehla raasta: family jo kehti hai 'adjust karo'

Jo women help maangti hain, woh zyada tar apno ke paas jaati hain. Violence ke baad help maangne wali women mein se 60.9% apni family ke paas gayi; police ke paas sirf 6.3% gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Toh pehla raasta uske maayke se hokar jaata hai. Hamare hypothetical mein, maa ka jawab ek shabd ka hai: adjust karo. Bachche ka socho. Log kya kahenge? Maa-baap shayad chhoti behen ki shaadi ke baare mein bhi soch rahe hain, ya us paise ke baare mein jo iski shaadi pe pehle hi kharch ho chuka hai. "Adjust karo" kehne wali family sirf use ek kamra dene se mana nahi karti. Woh use yeh batati hai ki problem uske sabr mein hai, husband ki violence mein nahi.

NFHS yeh record karta hai ki women help ke liye kahan gayi, yeh nahi ki wahan pahunch kar unhe kya kaha gaya. Woh doosra number exist hi nahi karta, aur shayad wahi zyada maayne rakhta hai.

## Doosra raasta: apni koi kamai nahi

Bachche ke saath ghar chhodne ka matlab hai kiraaya, deposit, school fees, aur der-saver ek lawyer. 2023-24 mein 15 saal aur usse upar ki urban women mein se sirf 28.0% labour force mein thi, yaani kaam kar rahi thi ya kaam dhoondh rahi thi [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. 2017-18 ke 20.4% se yeh badha hai, par phir bhi das mein se saat se zyada women iske bahar hain. Pune jaise shehar mein zyada tar women ke liye ghar chhodne ka matlab hai bina salary ke chhodna.

Salary ho bhi, toh zaroori nahi ki use kharch karne ka haq uske paas ho. Abuse aksar paise ke raaste chalta hai: tankhwah haath mein thama do, gehne "safe" rakhe hain, apne naam pe koi bank account nahi. 2005 ka Domestic Violence Act mainly ek civil law hai: jail ki saza ki jagah magistrate protection, residence aur maintenance ke orders de sakte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Lekin order ke liye apply karna padta hai, behes karni padti hai, use lagu karwana padta hai, aur iske liye waqt aur paisa chahiye jo shayad uske paas na ho.

## Teesra aur chautha raasta: saalon chalne wala case, aur kuch raaton ka bistar

Criminal raasta dheema hai. 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne husband ya uske relatives ki cruelty ke 9,27,199 cases the. Trial poora hua sirf 53,137 mein, conviction 10,689 mein hua, yaani 20.1% conviction rate, aur saal ke end tak 92.2% cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Conviction se zyada cases, 16,396, compromise pe khatam hue. Iska matlab reconciliation bhi ho sakta hai aur woman pe dabaav bhi; data yeh nahi batata ki kaun sa [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek 24 saal ki ladki ke liye aisa case, jo uske bete ke school shuru hone tak bhi pending ho, bahar nikalne ka raasta nahi hai. Woh ek doosra morcha hai.

Civil raaste ke daant kamzor hain. Domestic Violence Act ke protection order ko todne ki saza zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne is Act ke under sirf 616 cases register kiye, aur unme se 496 Kerala mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek state ke bahar, toota hua order shayad hi kabhi police case banta hai.

Aur phir raat ka sawaal. July 2026 tak India mein approve hue 1,033 One Stop Centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur 2015 se ab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada women ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Yahan police help, legal aid, counselling aur kuch din rukne ki jagah ek hi chhat ke neeche milti hai [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. Supreme Court ne 2018 mein kaha tha ki har district mein kam se kam ek centre ho [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]: yeh ek shuruaat hai, har woman ki pahunch mein ek darwaaza nahi. Aur kuch din ka thikana saans lene ki mohlat hai, naya ghar nahi.

## Sach: ghar chhodna ek process hai, aur iske liye support chahiye

Ghar chhodna shayad hi kabhi ek raat ka ek faisla hota hai. Woman raaste test karti hai: behen ko batati hai, ek hafte ke liye maayke jaati hai, kisi naukri ke baare mein poochti hai, ek baar lawyer se milti hai. Har darwaaza jo band rehta hai, use waapas bhej deta hai, aur jis aadmi ke saath woh rehti hai use sikha deta hai ki uske paas jaane ki koi jagah nahi.

Help aur ghar chhodna saath-saath chalte hain. Jin women ko sirf former husband ne abuse kiya tha, unme help maangne wali women ka share un women se dugna tha jinhe sirf current husband ne abuse kiya: 23.6% vs 11.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey yeh nahi bata sakta ki pehle kya hua. Jo bhi ho, jo women abhi bhi abuser ke saath reh rahi hain, unke kisi ko batane ke chances kam hain, aur isiliye unki chuppi ko kabhi "itna bura nahi hoga" nahi samajhna chahiye.

> Rukna aksar violence ko qubool karna nahi hota. Yeh ek andaaza hota hai ki abhi ke liye saare raaste band hain.

Yahi sawaal abusive rishton mein phanse mardon aur queer logon se bhi poocha jaata hai, jinke liye darwaaze aur bhi kam hain: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, jaisa naam se hi saaf hai, women ke liye bana hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Ghar chhodna us himmat se mumkin nahi hoga jo use "dikhani chahiye". Woh mumkin hoga ek family se jo kahe "ghar aa jao", uske apne naam pe paise se, aise orders se jinhe police lagu karwaye, aise cases se jo khatam hon, aur ek bistar se jahan woh aaj raat pahunch sake. Imaandaar sawaal yeh nahi ki woh ruki kyun hai. Sawaal yeh hai ki jaane ke liye use kya chahiye, aur use dilaane mein madad kaun karega.

wife-beating-justified-state-map.en:
Ask Indian women and men whether a husband is ever right to hit his wife, and close to half will find a reason. In the fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 45% of women and 44% of men aged 15-49 agreed that a husband is justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Split by state, that average becomes a map of where the excuse is strongest, and it sits uncomfortably close to the map of where wives are actually hurt.

## The seven 'reasons' NFHS asks about

Surveyors read out seven situations and ask whether a husband is justified in beating his wife if she goes out without telling him, neglects the house or children, argues with him, refuses to have sex with him, does not cook properly, if he suspects her of being unfaithful, or if she shows disrespect to her in-laws.

Read the list again. Apart from the husband's suspicion, which is about his mind rather than her actions, every item is about an adult woman's everyday choices and work: leaving the house, running a home, disagreeing, saying no, getting dinner wrong. The reason accepted most often is not even about the husband. It is disrespect for in-laws, accepted by 32% of women and 31% of men. The least accepted is refusing sex, and even that was accepted by 11% of women and 10% of men [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The trend splits by sex. Women's agreement fell from 52% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 45%. Men's rose, from 42% to 44% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Women are slowly walking away from the excuse. Men are not.

## 84%, 82%, 78%: the state extremes

In Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, 84% of women said wife-beating could be justified. In Tamil Nadu it was 78%. Among men, the figure reached 82% in Karnataka [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Among women in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and men in Karnataka, more than four in five accepted that a husband may hit his wife for some reason; in Tamil Nadu, close to four in five women did. This is not a fringe view. It is the majority view, held by the very women it is used against. The point is not to shame these states. It is that changing the belief there means reaching almost every household.

## Where acceptance and violence travel together

Lay the violence data on top. Nationally, 29.2% of ever-married women aged 18-49 reported physical or sexual violence by their husband in NFHS-5. The highest shares were in Karnataka (44.4%), Bihar (40.1%), Manipur (39.6%), Tamil Nadu (38.1%) and Telangana (37.2%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Three of the four states named above, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, are in that top five.

A survey cannot prove that belief causes beating. But calling it "justified" can make it easier to do, easier to forgive and harder to name. A woman taught that there are good reasons may not call it violence at all. She may blame herself instead.

Newer data do not erase the pattern. Provisional NFHS-6 fact sheets (2023-24) report a lower national figure, 22.3%, but still place Telangana (30.8%) and Tamil Nadu (28.5%) among the four states with the most reported spousal violence, behind Bihar (36.1%). Karnataka's figure fell to 14.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Experts quoted by Deccan Herald doubt that falls like this are real, saying women may not disclose abuse to a surveyor in front of family members [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]].

## Why so many women accept it

Nationally, women agreed slightly more often than men: 45% against 44%. That is not because women want to be hit. Part of the answer may lie in what girls see at home. NFHS-5 found that women whose fathers beat their mothers were more than twice as likely to face violence from their own husbands: 58% against 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A girl who watched her mother being hit "for a reason" may grow up knowing the reasons by heart.

There is a grim logic, too. If a beating has a reason, she can try to avoid the reason: come home on time, cook carefully, never answer back. That may feel safer than accepting that the man she depends on may hurt her whatever she does.

The belief may also keep women quiet. Of women who faced physical or sexual violence, 77.2% never sought help or told anyone. Of those who did seek help, 60.9% went to their own family and only 6.3% to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. And a family that shares the belief is likely to repeat the excuse: "adjust", "don't provoke him", "every marriage has this".

Police records show that belief is not the whole story. In 2024 Tamil Nadu registered 2.2 cases of cruelty by husband or relatives per lakh women, against 52.8 in Telangana [[ncrb-cii-2024]], where women accepted the excuse even more widely. Belief alone does not decide whether a complaint reaches the register; what police do matters too. But in Tamil Nadu, where 78% of women accepted the excuse and 38.1% reported violence, a rate that low looks more like silence than safety, even allowing for the different years and measures.

## Answering the excuse at home

These beliefs live at dinner tables, in WhatsApp forwards and at weddings, so answer them there:

- "She went out without telling him." She is an adult, not a child under house arrest.
- "She disrespected his mother." Then the family can talk. Disagreement is not a licence to hit.
- "She refused him." Her no is an answer, not a provocation.
- "She must have done something." Nothing she does makes it legal. Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is a crime under Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), punishable with up to three years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Men have a particular job, because their agreement rose. An uncle, brother or friend who says "no reason, ever" at the table can move the line further than any poster.

If a woman tells you she is being hurt, believe her, ask what she needs and never send her back to "adjust". In danger, call 112; for help, call the Women Helpline.
wife-beating-justified-state-map.hg:
Logon se poochhiye ki kya pati ka patni par haath uthana kabhi sahi ho sakta hai, aur lagbhag aadhe log koi na koi wajah dhoondh lenge. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 15 se 49 saal ki 45% women aur 44% men ne yahi kaha: saat mein se kam se kam ek situation mein pati ka patni ko peetna justified hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh poore desh ka average hai. Ise state-wise todiye toh ek map banta hai ki yeh excuse kahan sabse mazboot hai. Aur yeh map us map se kaafi milta hai jahan patniyon par sach mein haath uthaya jaata hai.

## NFHS kaun si saat 'wajahein' poochhta hai

Surveyor saat situations padhkar sunaate hain aur poochhte hain ki kya inmein pati ka patni ko peetna sahi hai. Situations yeh hain: patni pati ko bataye bina bahar jaaye, ghar ya bachchon ka dhyan na rakhe, pati se behas kare, sex se mana kare, khaana theek se na banaye, pati ko us par bewafai ka shak ho, ya woh sasural walon ki izzat na kare.

Is list ko ek baar phir padhiye. Pati ke shak ko chhod dein, jo uske mann ki baat hai, aurat ke kisi kaam ki nahi, toh har point ek adult aurat ke rozmarra ke faislon aur kaam ke baare mein hai: bahar jaana, ghar chalana, apni baat rakhna, mana karna, khaane mein kami reh jaana. Sabse zyada logon ne jo wajah maani, woh pati ke baare mein hai hi nahi. Woh hai sasural walon ki disrespect, jise 32% women aur 31% men ne sahi maana. Sabse kam maani gayi wajah hai sex se mana karna, aur use bhi 11% women aur 10% men ne sahi thehraya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yahan women aur men ka raasta alag ho jaata hai. Women mein yeh soch NFHS-4 (2015-16) ke 52% se ghatkar 45% reh gayi. Men mein yeh 42% se badhkar 44% ho gayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Matlab women dheere-dheere is excuse se door ja rahi hain. Men nahi.

## 84%, 82%, 78%: sabse aage wale states

Andhra Pradesh aur Telangana mein 84% women ne kaha ki wife-beating justified ho sakti hai. Tamil Nadu mein yeh 78% tha. Men mein Karnataka sabse aage raha, jahan 82% men ne yeh maana [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Iska matlab samajhiye. Andhra aur Telangana ki women mein, aur Karnataka ke men mein, har paanch mein se chaar se zyada log maante the ki kisi wajah se pati patni ko peet sakta hai. Tamil Nadu mein bhi paanch mein se lagbhag chaar women yahi maanti thin. Yeh kuch gine-chune families ki soch nahi hai. Yeh majority ki soch hai, aur ise wahi women maanti hain jinke khilaaf yeh use hoti hai. Maqsad in states ko sharminda karna nahi hai. Baat yeh hai ki wahan yeh soch badalne ke liye lagbhag har ghar tak pahunchna padega.

## Jahan yeh soch hai, wahin violence bhi

Ab is map par violence ka data rakhiye. NFHS-5 mein desh ki 18 se 49 saal ki married women mein se 29.2% ne bataya ki pati ne un par physical ya sexual violence ki. Sabse zyada figures Karnataka (44.4%), Bihar (40.1%), Manipur (39.6%), Tamil Nadu (38.1%) aur Telangana (37.2%) mein the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Upar jin chaar states ka naam aaya, unmein se teen, yaani Karnataka, Tamil Nadu aur Telangana, is top five mein bhi hain.

Survey yeh prove nahi kar sakta ki yahi soch maar-peet ki wajah hai. Lekin jab maar-peet ko "justified" bol diya jaaye, toh use karna aasaan ho sakta hai, maaf karna aasaan ho sakta hai, aur use violence kehna mushkil. Jis aurat ko sikhaya gaya ho ki pitaai ki wajahein hoti hain, woh shayad ise violence maane hi nahi. Ho sakta hai woh ulta khud ko hi dosh de.

Naya data bhi yeh pattern nahi mitaata. NFHS-6 (2023-24) ki provisional fact sheets mein national figure ghatkar 22.3% hai. Phir bhi Bihar (36.1%) ke baad Telangana (30.8%) aur Tamil Nadu (28.5%) un chaar states mein hain jahan sabse zyada spousal violence report hui. Karnataka ka figure girkar 14.1% ho gaya [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Deccan Herald se baat karne wale experts ko aisi giravat par shak hai. Unka kehna hai ki ghar walon ke saamne women surveyor ko abuse ke baare mein shayad na batayein [[deccanherald-nfhs6-gbv-2026]].

## Itni women ise sahi kyun maanti hain

Desh mein women ne yeh baat men se thoda zyada maani: 45% vs 44%. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki auratein pitna chahti hain. Iska ek hissa shayad us cheez mein hai jo ladkiyan ghar mein dekhti hain. NFHS-5 ke hisaab se jin women ke papa unki mummy ko peette the, unke saath khud pati ki violence hone ka chance double se bhi zyada tha: 58% vs 25% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jis bachchi ne maa ko "kisi wajah se" pitte dekha ho, ho sakta hai use yeh wajahein bachpan se ratt jaayein.

Iske peeche ek kadwa hisaab bhi hai. Agar pitaai ki koi wajah hai, toh aurat us wajah se bachne ki koshish kar sakti hai: time par ghar aao, dhyan se khaana banao, palat kar jawab mat do. Aisa sochkar use shayad thoda safe feel hota hai. Sach maanna zyada darawna hai: woh kitna bhi sambhal kar rahe, jis aadmi par woh depend karti hai, woh us par haath utha sakta hai.

Yahi soch auraton ko chup bhi rakh sakti hai. Physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% women ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya. Jinhone help maangi, unmein se 60.9% apni hi family ke paas gayin aur sirf 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aur jo family khud yeh soch rakhti hai, woh shayad wahi excuse dohraayegi: "adjust kar lo", "use gussa mat dilao", "har shaadi mein yeh hota hai".

Police records batate hain ki poori kahani sirf soch ki nahi hai. 2024 mein Tamil Nadu mein pati ya relatives ki cruelty ke sirf 2.2 cases per lakh women register hue, jabki Telangana mein 52.8 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], jahan women mein yeh excuse aur bhi zyada maana jaata tha. Yaani sirf soch se tay nahi hota ki complaint register tak pahunchegi; police kya karti hai, yeh bhi maayne rakhta hai. Lekin Tamil Nadu mein, jahan 78% women ne yeh excuse maana aur 38.1% ne violence jhelne ki baat kahi, itni kam rate safety kam, chuppi zyada lagti hai, bhale hi dono figures ke saal aur measure alag hon.

## Ghar par is excuse ka jawab kaise dein

Yeh baatein dinner table par, WhatsApp forwards mein aur shaadiyon mein dohraayi jaati hain. Toh jawab bhi wahin dijiye:

- "Woh bina bataye bahar gayi thi." Woh adult hai, koi nazarband bachchi nahi.
- "Usne saas ki izzat nahi ki." Toh family baith kar baat kare. Disagreement haath uthane ka licence nahi hai.
- "Usne mana kar diya." Uski 'na' ek jawab hai, provocation nahi.
- "Usne zaroor kuch kiya hoga." Woh kuch bhi kare, haath uthana legal nahi ho jaata. Pati ya uske relatives ki cruelty Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 85 ke under crime hai, jismein teen saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yahan men ki khaas zimmedari hai, kyunki men mein yeh soch badhi hai. Jab koi chacha, bhai ya dost dinner table par kehta hai, "koi wajah nahi, kabhi nahi", toh uska asar kisi bhi poster se zyada ho sakta hai.

Agar koi aurat aapko bataye ki use peeta ja raha hai, toh us par bharosa kijiye, poochhiye use kya chahiye, aur use "adjust" karne ke liye wapas mat bhejiye. Khatra ho toh 112 par call karein; madad ke liye Women Helpline par call karein.

witch-hunting-murders-india-data.en:
In 2024, police in India recorded witchcraft as the motive in 54 murders [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Behind each of these killings is an accusation: before anyone was killed, someone was branded a witch, whether by a neighbour, a relative, a healer or a village gathering. By the time a case reaches the National Crime Records Bureau's (NCRB) table of murder motives, the chance to act on that warning has passed. This data story looks at what India's records show about these killings, and at everything they leave out.

## Five years of 'witchcraft' murders

| Year | Murders with witchcraft recorded as the motive |
|---|---|
| 2020 | 88 |
| 2021 | 68 |
| 2022 | 85 |
| 2023 | 74 |
| 2024 | 54 |

All five figures come from NCRB's Crime in India reports [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even in the lowest year, that is more than one killing a week.

The line does not fall steadily. It dropped from 88 to 68, climbed back to 85, then fell twice. One low year is not a trend, and NCRB itself warns that a "rise in crime" and an "increase in registration of crime by police" are two different things [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. The same logic works in reverse: a fall can mean fewer killings, or fewer killings that police recorded with this motive. The table cannot tell the two apart.

## Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh in 2024

Madhya Pradesh recorded the most witchcraft murders in 2024 (17), followed by Chhattisgarh (10): together, exactly half of the national total. Odisha recorded 7 and Jharkhand 5 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

It is tempting to read this as a map of where witch-hunting happens. NCRB advises against it: comparing states on its data alone "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. NCRB only compiles what state and union territory police send, and says it is not responsible for the authenticity of that information [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A state whose police write "witchcraft" in the motive field whenever it applies will look worse than one whose police write something else. A high number may partly reflect honest recording; a low one may reflect the opposite.

## What the motive table leaves out

**Everyone who survives.** The witchcraft column sits in NCRB's table of murder motives and counts only killings [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A woman who is branded, fined, beaten, cut off from the village well or driven out of her home, and lives, does not appear in it. Neither does the accusation itself.

**Who died.** The table does not record the victim's sex. Witch-hunting is widely reported to target women, often widows and older women, but the count covers every victim, whatever their sex, and the data cannot say how many were women or men [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**The road to the killing.** NCRB counts each FIR once, under the offence that attracts the heaviest punishment: the "principal offence rule" [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. When an accusation, threats, a beating and a killing end up in one FIR, the national data keep only the murder. Whatever escalation came before it leaves no trace in the national count.

## From accusation to killing

Consider this situation. A child in a village falls ill and dies. The grieving family wants an explanation, and a local healer offers one: a widow who lives alone, on a plot of land her late husband's brothers have long wanted. Whispers become a meeting. The meeting demands a fine. When she cannot pay, shopkeepers stop selling to her and neighbours stop speaking to her. Then someone hits her, and nobody steps in.

The law does not have to wait for the last step. Beating her is voluntarily causing hurt, punishable under Section 115(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) with up to a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Killing her is murder, whatever anyone believes about her. (This is general information, not legal advice.) The point of the hypothetical is that a witch-hunt does not have to be sudden. It can build over days or months, in public, in front of people who could stop it.

## What to do when someone is branded a witch

- **Do not repeat the label**, in person or on WhatsApp. Every repetition spreads the accusation further.
- **Treat a 'meeting', a fine or a crowd as an emergency.** Call 112 before it becomes an attack [[mha-erss]].
- **Help her reach safety.** Call the Women Helpline 181. One Stop Centres offer police help, medical aid, legal aid, counselling and short-stay shelter under one roof [[wcd-mission-shakti]]; 985 centres were operational across India as of July 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].
- **Report it, at any station.** Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, a cognizable offence can be reported at any police station, whatever the area where it happened, or electronically, and the victim must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Write it down.** Note who made the accusation, who called the meeting, who threatened her, and when. A record like this shows police and courts that the violence did not come out of nowhere.
- **When an illness or death is being blamed on a person**, ask a doctor or health worker to explain what happened, early, before a rumour hardens into a verdict.

The 54 murders of 2024 are the cases where nothing stopped the violence in time. The accusations that never reach the table are where it can still work.
witch-hunting-murders-india-data.hg:
2024 mein India mein police ne 54 murders mein motive "witchcraft" darj kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In har killing ke peeche ek ilzaam hai: kisi ki jaan jaane se pehle use witch, yaani "daayan", kaha gaya, chahe kisi padosi ne, kisi rishtedaar ne, kisi local healer ne ya gaon ki kisi baithak ne. Jab tak case National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ki murder-motive table tak pahunchta hai, tab tak us chetavni par kuch karne ka mauka nikal chuka hota hai. Yeh data story dekhti hai ki India ke records in killings ke baare mein kya dikhate hain, aur kya kuch chhod dete hain.

## Paanch saal ke 'witchcraft' murders

| Saal | Murders jinka motive witchcraft darj hua |
|---|---|
| 2020 | 88 |
| 2021 | 68 |
| 2022 | 85 |
| 2023 | 74 |
| 2024 | 54 |

Yeh paanchon figures NCRB ki Crime in India reports se hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sabse kam wale saal mein bhi, yeh har hafte ek se zyada killing hai.

Line seedhi neeche nahi aati. Yeh 88 se 68 par giri, phir 85 tak chadhi, phir do baar giri. Ek kam wala saal trend nahi hota, aur NCRB khud warning deta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" do alag cheezein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Yahi logic ulta bhi lagta hai: girawat ka matlab kam killings bhi ho sakta hai, ya aisi kam killings jinme police ne yeh motive darj kiya. Table in dono mein farq nahi kar sakti.

## 2024 mein Madhya Pradesh aur Chhattisgarh

2024 mein sabse zyada witchcraft murders Madhya Pradesh mein darj hue (17), phir Chhattisgarh mein (10): dono milkar national total ka theek aadha. Odisha mein 7 darj hue aur Jharkhand mein 5 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ise is baat ka map samajh lena aasaan hai ki witch-hunting kahan hoti hai. NCRB aisa karne se mana karta hai: sirf uske data par states ki tulna "will be too simplistic and is best avoided" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. NCRB sirf wahi compile karta hai jo state aur union territory police bhejti hai, aur kehta hai ki us information ki authenticity ki zimmedari uski nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis state ki police har laagu case mein motive ke khane mein "witchcraft" likhti hai, woh us state se buri dikhegi jiski police kuch aur likh deti hai. Bada number kuch had tak imaandaar recording ka nateeja ho sakta hai; chhota number iska ulta.

## Motive table kya chhod deti hai

**Har woh insaan jo bach jaata hai.** Witchcraft column NCRB ki murder-motive table mein hai aur sirf killings ginta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis aurat ko daayan bataya gaya, jurmana lagaya gaya, peeta gaya, gaon ke kuen se door kar diya gaya ya ghar se nikaal diya gaya, aur woh zinda bach gayi, woh is table mein nahi dikhti. Ilzaam bhi nahi dikhta.

**Kaun maara gaya.** Table victim ka sex darj nahi karti. Aam taur par report hota hai ki witch-hunting mein auraton ko, aksar widows aur buzurg auraton ko, nishana banaya jaata hai, lekin yeh count har victim ko ginta hai, chahe woh kisi bhi sex ka ho, aur data nahi bata sakta ki unme kitni auratein thi aur kitne mard [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Killing tak ka raasta.** NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, us offence ke naam se jiski saza sabse bhaari ho: yeh "principal offence rule" hai [[ncrb-cii-2024-methodology]]. Jab ilzaam, dhamkiyan, maar-peet aur killing ek hi FIR mein aate hain, toh national data mein sirf murder bachta hai. Usse pehle jo bhi hinsa badhti rahi, uska national count mein koi nishaan nahi rehta.

## Ilzaam se killing tak

Yeh situation socho. Ek gaon mein ek bachcha beemar padta hai aur uski maut ho jaati hai. Dukhi family ko koi wajah chahiye, aur ek local healer wajah de deta hai: ek widow jo akeli rehti hai, zameen ke us tukde par jis par uske guzar chuke pati ke bhaiyon ki nazar barson se hai. Kanaphoosi baithak ban jaati hai. Baithak jurmana maangti hai. Jab woh nahi de paati, toh dukaandaar use saamaan bechna band kar dete hain aur padosi usse baat karna. Phir koi use maarta hai, aur koi beech mein nahi aata.

Law ko aakhri kadam ka intezaar nahi karna padta. Use peetna voluntarily causing hurt hai, jiske liye Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 115(2) ke under ek saal tak jail, Rs 10,000 tak fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Use maar dena murder hai, chahe uske baare mein koi kuch bhi maanta ho. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.) Is hypothetical ka point yeh hai ki witch-hunt ka achanak hona zaroori nahi. Woh dinon ya mahino mein, sabke saamne, un logon ki aankhon ke aage badh sakta hai jo use rok sakte hain.

## Jab kisi ko daayan kaha jaye, tab kya karein

- **Label ko dohrao mat**, na saamne, na WhatsApp par. Har baar dohraane se ilzaam aur door tak failta hai.
- **'Baithak', jurmane ya bheed ko emergency samjho.** Hamla hone se pehle 112 par call karo [[mha-erss]].
- **Use surakshit jagah tak pahunchao.** Women Helpline 181 par call karo. One Stop Centres ek hi chhat ke neeche police help, medical aid, legal aid, counselling aur kuch din rehne ki jagah dete hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]]; July 2026 mein India mein 985 centres chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].
- **Report karo, kisi bhi station mein.** Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ke Section 173 ke under cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai, chahe ghatna kisi bhi area mein hui ho, ya electronically bhi, aur victim ko FIR ki copy free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Likh kar rakho.** Ilzaam kisne lagaya, baithak kisne bulayi, dhamki kisne di, aur kab. Aisa record police aur courts ko dikhata hai ki hinsa achanak nahi aayi.
- **Jab kisi beemari ya maut ka ilzaam kisi insaan par daala ja raha ho**, toh jaldi se kisi doctor ya health worker se samjhaane ko kaho ki asal mein kya hua, isse pehle ki afwaah faisla ban jaye.

2024 ke 54 murders woh cases hain jahan hinsa ko waqt par kisi ne nahi roka. Jo ilzaam table tak kabhi nahi pahunchte, wahan yeh sab abhi bhi kaam kar sakta hai.
